<s>Daśavidhahetunirūpaṇa</s> (Determination of the Ten Reasons)
Invocatory Verses (<s>maṅgalācaraṇam</s>)
Obeisance to the glorious great teacher <s>Vikhanasa</s>!
Obeisance to <s>Śrī Śrīnivāsa</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>! //
The <s>Daśavidhahetunirūpaṇa</s> (Determination of the Ten Reasons) in the <s>Tātparyacintāmaṇi</s> on the <s>Śrīvaikhānasagṛhyasūtra</s>, composed by <s>Śrīnivāsamakhi</s>.
Born in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> lineage, devoted to the worship of <s>Veṅkaṭeśa</s>,
I pay homage to <s>Vedāntadeśika</s>, the venerable <s>Śrīnivāsāryadīkṣita</s>. //

children.text: śrīveṅkaṭeśam akhileśam anantam ādyaṃ kāruṇyavāridhim aśeṣasurais suvandyam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa</s>, the Lord of all, infinite, primordial, an ocean of compassion, well-praised by all the gods,

children.text: vande samastajagatāṃ sthitisṛṣṭihetuṃ mānyān gurūṃś ca śataśo*{4}* bhṛgukaśyapādīn //
children.translated_text: I pay homage to the cause of the creation and sustenance of all worlds, and to the revered teachers <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and others, a hundredfold. //
Filled with the rivers of <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture) and <s>Smṛti</s> (remembered tradition), crowded with the waves of <s>śāstras</s> (treatises),
Pure with the water of devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — I pay homage to the ocean of <s>Vaikhānasa</s>! //
By which the eye of the <s>sūtras</s> composed by others has been made free from darkness,
This <s>Vaikhānasa sūtra</s> indeed bestows the fruit of the four aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>). //
Whose greatness is established through <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s> (epics), and other [authoritative texts],
I pay homage to the supreme <s>Sūtropaniṣad</s>, devoted entirely to the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>). //
Regarding the lineage, name, etc. of the commentator
By a descendant of the illustrious <s>Kauśika</s> lineage, the son of <s>Govindācārya</s>,
Whose soul delights in the worship of the lotus-feet of <s>Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa</s>,
Who follows the established path of <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and other [texts],
Who follows the tradition well-trodden by the earlier <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers),
By the foremost of <s>Vedānta ācāryas</s>, the sacrificer <s>Śrīnivāsārya</s>,
The commentary on the <s>Vaikhānasa sūtra</s> is properly illuminated. //

children.text: vikhānasasūtrasya tadanuyāyināṃ ca sarvotkṛṣṭatve daśavidhahetūnāṃ nirdeśaḥ
children.translated_text: Statement of the ten reasons for the supreme excellence of the <s>Vikhanasa sūtra</s> and its followers

children.text:
atha satyatvādisamastakalyāṇaguṇaviśiṣṭāt parabrahmaṇaḥ śrīmannārāyaṇād utpannena vikhanaśśabdavācyena caturmukhabrahmaṇā praṇītasya vaikhānasasūtrasya sarvasūtrottamatve tatsūtroktadharmānuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ sarvotkṛṣṭatamatve ca daśavidhahetavo nirūpyante.
[2.4] yathā:
[2.5-9] akhilajagatkāraṇabhūtena vikhanasā praṇītatvāt.*{9}* sarvasūtrāṇām āditvāt.*{10}* sarvakarmasu śrutimārgānusāritvāt.*{11}* samantrakasarvakriyāpratipādakatvāt.*{12}* niṣekasaṃskārādimatvāt.*{13}* aṣṭādaśaśārīrasaṃskārapratipādakatvāt.*{14}* sāṅgakriyākalāpavattvāt.*{15}* manvādyaiḥ svīkṛtatvāt.*{16}* akhilajagadekakāraṇabhūtaśrīmannārāyaṇaikaparatvāt.*{17}* etatsūtroktadharmānuṣṭhānavatām eva bhagavatpriyatamatvopapatteś ca.*{18}* iti.
[2.10-12] ebhir hetubhir asya sūtrasya sarvasūtrottamatvaṃ etatsūtroktadharmānuṣṭhānād eva vaikhānasānāṃ sarvebhyaḥ śreṣṭhatamatvāñ ca śrutismṛtipurāṇādimukhena pratipādyate. tatrādau akhilajagatkāraṇabhūtena vikhanasā praṇītatvād iti hetur nirūpyate.
[2.13] vikhanaśśabdārthanirṇayaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now, the ten reasons are set forth for the supreme excellence of the <s>Vaikhānasa sūtra</s> — which was composed by the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>, designated by the word <s>Vikhanasa</s>, who originated from the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> <s>Śrīmannārāyaṇa</s> who is distinguished by all auspicious qualities such as truth — and for the supreme excellence of those who practice the <s>dharmas</s> prescribed by that <s>sūtra</s>.
[2.4] As follows:
[2.5-9] (1) Because it was composed by <s>Vikhanasa</s>, who is the cause of the entire world. (2) Because it is the first among all <s>sūtras</s>. (3) Because it follows the path of <s>Śruti</s> in all rituals. (4) Because it teaches all ritual acts accompanied by <s>mantras</s>. (5) Because it possesses the <s>niṣeka saṃskāra</s> (conception-rite) as its starting point. (6) Because it teaches the eighteen bodily <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments). (7) Because it possesses a complete corpus of ritual acts with their auxiliaries. (8) Because it was adopted by <s>Manu</s> and others. (9) Because it is exclusively devoted to <s>Śrīmannārāyaṇa</s>, who is the sole cause of the entire world. (10) And because only those who practice the <s>dharmas</s> prescribed by this <s>sūtra</s> are proven to be the most dear to the Lord.
[2.10-12] By these reasons, the supreme excellence of this <s>sūtra</s> over all other <s>sūtras</s>, and the supreme excellence of the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> over all others through the practice of the <s>dharmas</s> prescribed by this <s>sūtra</s>, is established through the authority of <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and other texts. First, the reason 'because it was composed by <s>Vikhanasa</s>, who is the cause of the entire world' is examined.
[2.13] Determination of the meaning of the word <s>Vikhanasa</s>.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> being denoted by the words <s>Vikhanasa</s>, <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, etc.

children.text:
vikhanā nāma kaścid ṛṣiḥ, uta nārāyaṇaḥ? nārāyaṇa eva kevalaṃ.
[2.15-16] munimātrasya vaikhānasaśabdavācyatvena pratipādanābhāvāt. paramātmano nārāyaṇasya vikhano vaikhānasādiśabdavācyatvaṃ śrutismṛtipurāṇādiṣv avagamyate. yathā:
[2.17] khilaśrutau: "dhenur vahāṇām aditis surāṇāṃ brahmā ṛbhūṇāṃ vikhanā munīnām".
children.translated_text:
Is <s>Vikhanā</s> merely some sage, or is he <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>? He is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone.
[2.15-16] Because there is no statement establishing that a mere sage is denoted by the word <s>Vaikhānasa</s>. That the Supreme Self <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is denoted by the words <s>Vikhanasa</s>, <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, etc. is understood from <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and other texts. As follows:
[2.17] In the <s>Khilaśruti</s>: 'The cow is [the mother] of draft animals, <s>Aditi</s> of the gods, <s>Brahmā</s> of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, <s>Vikhanā</s> of the sages.'

children.text: iti śruyate. ayam arthaḥ. vahānāṃ ataḍudādīnāṃ dhenuḥ utpattikāraṇam. surāṇāṃ indrādīnām aditiḥ. ṛbhūṇāṃ:
children.translated_text: Thus it is heard. The meaning is this: the cow (<s>dhenu</s>) is the cause of origin of draft animals such as bulls. <s>Aditi</s> [is the mother] of the gods such as <s>Indra</s>. Of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>:

children.text: "sādhyā viśve ca vasavo maruto ṛbhavas tathā /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and the <s>Ṛbhus</s>,

children.text: tathaivāṅgiraso rudrā ādityāś ca tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Likewise the <s>Āṅgirasas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and also the <s>Ādityas</s>,
These eight classes of gods are the lords of the groups in each <s>Manvantara</s>. //'

children.text: iti bhṛgūktānāṃ sādhyādīnāṃ brahmā. munīnāṃ muniśabdavācyānāṃ vikhanāḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> [is the progenitor] of the <s>Sādhyas</s> and others mentioned by <s>Bhṛgu</s>. <s>Vikhanā</s> [is the progenitor] of the sages, i.e., those denoted by the word <s>muni</s>.
That <s>Brahmā</s> is denoted by the word <s>muni</s> is also understood from the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:
'Having slept through the night, the Lord awakened at the end of the night.' [MBh 13, App. 3.265]

children.text: paścād buddhvā sasarjāpaḥ tāsu vīryam avāsṛjat* //{20}* [MBh 13, App. 3.266]
children.translated_text: 'Thereafter, having awakened, he created the waters and discharged his potency into them.' [MBh 13, App. 3.266]

children.text: tad aṇḍam abhavad dhaimaṃ sahasrāṃśusamaprabham / [MBh 13, App. 3.267]
children.translated_text: 'That [potency] became a golden egg, with radiance equal to the thousand-rayed [sun].' [MBh 13, App. 3.267]

children.text: ahaṅkṛtyā*{21}* tatas tasmin sasarja prabhur īśvaraḥ / [MBh 13, App. 3.268]
children.translated_text: 'Then, with self-assertion, the powerful Lord created therein' [MBh 13, App. 3.268]

children.text: hiraṇyagarbhaṃ viśvātmā brahmāṇaṃ jalajaṃ*{22}* munim //" iti [MBh 13, App. 3.269]
children.translated_text: '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the Universal Self, <s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born sage (<s>muni</s>).' [MBh 13, App. 3.269]
The plural 'of sages' is used with the intention of [indicating] the multiplicity of cosmic eggs. As:
'Thousands upon thousands and tens of thousands of [such] eggs,
Hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>koṭīs</s> of such infinite [eggs].' Thus it is remembered.

children.text: niśā cātra pralayaḥ, sā etāvatīti kutrāvagamyata iti cet.
children.translated_text: And 'night' here means <s>pralaya</s> (cosmic dissolution). If one asks, 'Where is it understood that [the night] is of such [duration]?'
In the <s>Mahābhārata</s>: 'Four thousand <s>caturyugas</s> and four hundred <s>caturyugas</s>,' [MBh 13, App. 3.261]

children.text: prāhuḥ kalpasahasran tu*{24}* brāhmaṇās tattvadarśinaḥ / [MBh 13, App. 3.262]
children.translated_text: '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who perceive the truth call [this] a thousand <s>kalpas</s>.' [MBh 13, App. 3.262]

children.text: daśakalpasahasrāṇi apy ayas sā mahāniśā*{25}* //" iti. [MBh 13, App. 3.263]
children.translated_text: 'Ten thousand <s>kalpas</s> is indeed that great night.' [MBh 13, App. 3.263]

children.text: anayā khilaśrutyā bhagavato vikhanaśśabdavācyatvaṃ katham avagamyata iti cet ucyate.
children.translated_text: If one asks, 'How is the Lord's being denoted by the word <s>Vikhanasa</s> understood from this <s>Khilaśruti</s>?' — it is stated [as follows].
The meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> is to be determined through <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s>

children.text: "durbodhā vaidikāś śabdā prakīrṇatvāc ca ye khilāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Vedic words that are difficult to understand, and those in the <s>Khilas</s> (supplementary texts) because of their scattered nature,

children.text: tadjñais ta eva spaṣṭārthāḥ smṛtitantre pratiṣṭhitāḥ //"*{26}* iti
children.translated_text: Are made clear in meaning by those who know them, established in <s>Smṛti</s> and <s>Tantra</s>.' //
'If a twice-born person were to know the four <s>Vedas</s> together with their limbs and <s>Upaniṣads</s>,

children.text: na cet purāṇasadvidyā na vedārthavicakṣaṇaḥ //" iti
children.translated_text: If one is not versed in ancient sacred knowledge, one is not skilled in the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>." Thus,
"One should supplement the <s>Veda</s> with <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>,

children.text: bibhety alpaśruvād*{28}* vedo mām ayaṃ pratariṣyati //" iti ca [MBh 1.1.204]
children.translated_text: the <s>Veda</s> fears one of little learning, [thinking] 'this one will distort me.'" Thus also. [MBh 1.1.204]

children.text: smaraṇāt itihāsapurāṇābhyām evārthanirṇayaḥ kartavyaḥ. bhārate mokṣadharme nāradastutau:
children.translated_text: From the <s>smṛti</s> texts, the determination of meaning is to be made through <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> alone. In the <s>Bhārata</s>, in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>, in the praise of <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: "namas te devadeveśa"*{29}* ity ārabhya stotramadhye "phenapācārya vālakhilya vikhano vikhanasa vaikhānasācārya abhagnayoga abhagnaparisaṅkhyāna"*{30}* iti.
children.translated_text: Beginning with "Salutation to you, O lord of the gods of gods" and in the middle of the hymn: "<s>Phenapācārya</s>, <s>Vālakhilya</s>, <s>Vikhanas</s>, <s>Vikhanasa</s>, <s>Vaikhānasācārya</s>, <s>Abhagnayoga</s>, <s>Abhagnaparisaṅkhyāna</s>." Thus.

children.text: tatraiva: "yat tasminn upalabhyaṃ te tat tejas tat trayīmayam /
children.translated_text: In that same passage: "That splendor which is found in him is that which consists of the <s>Trayī</s> (triple Veda),

children.text: tad vaikhānaḥ paraṃ brahma iti vedavido viduḥ //" iti coktam. [MBh ]
children.translated_text: that <s>Vaikhānas</s> is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — thus know those who know the <s>Vedas</s>." Thus it is also stated. [MBh]

children.text: ! Dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 94.16-17 zitiert.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 28] Read with MBh: alpaśrutād.
[Footnote 29] MBh 12.325.4A: namas te devadeva.

children.text: !{30}! Bezug auf MBh 12.325.4J-K: prathamatrisauparṇa [91] pañcāgne [92] triṇāciketa [93] ṣaḍaṅgavidhāna [94] prāgjyotiṣa [95] jyeṣṭhasāmaga [96] sāmikavratadhara [97] atharvaśiraḥ [98] pañcamahākalpa [99] phenapācārya [100] // vālakhily.a [101] vaikhānasa [102] abhagnayoga [103] abhagnaparisaṃkhyāna [104] yugāde [105] yugamadhya [106] yuganidhana [107] ākhaṇḍala [108] prācīnagarbha [109] kauśika [110]; s.u., DHN[D] 10.1-3.
children.translated_text: [Footnote 30] Reference to MBh 12.325.4J-K: prathamatrisauparṇa [91] pañcāgne [92] triṇāciketa [93] ṣaḍaṅgavidhāna [94] prāgjyotiṣa [95] jyeṣṭhasāmaga [96] sāmikavratadhara [97] atharvaśiraḥ [98] pañcamahākalpa [99] phenapācārya [100] // vālakhilya [101] vaikhānasa [102] abhagnayoga [103] abhagnaparisaṃkhyāna [104] yugāde [105] yugamadhya [106] yuganidhana [107] ākhaṇḍala [108] prācīnagarbha [109] kauśika [110]; see below, DHN[D] 10.1-3.
Etymology of the word Vikhanasa
Likewise, in the chapter of the thousand names, it is remembered: "<s>Vaikhānas</s>, singer of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>."
The purpose of the creation of the world
In the <s>Pañcarātra</s>, in the <s>Ātmasaṃhitā</s>:
"The world is pervaded by <s>Vikhanasa</s>, the great being among beings,

children.text: tam eva śaraṇaṃ gaccha jagatkāraṇam acyutam //" [Ātmasaṃhitā]
children.translated_text: take refuge in him alone, <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable), the cause of the world." [<s>Ātmasaṃhitā</s>]
Thus said by <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> addressing <s>Śatānanda</s>.
In the Vaikhānasa tradition, in the <s>Ānandasaṃhitā</s>:
"<s>Hari</s> performed the digging (<s>khanana</s>) into the truth of <s>Vedānta</s> investigation,

children.text: nāmnā vikhanasaṃ prāhur yañ ca vaikhānasaṃ tathā* //{33}*" iti proktam. [ĀS ]
children.translated_text: by name they call him <s>Vikhanasa</s>, and likewise <s>Vaikhānasa</s>." Thus it is stated. [ĀS]

children.text: atra khananaśabdena saṅkalpa ucyate. "so 'kāmayata. bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti sa tapo 'tayata"*{34}* ityādi śrutibhyaḥ. avāptasamastakāmasyāpi bhagavataḥ sṛṣṭikārye pravṛttir bhavati.
children.translated_text: Here the word <s>khanana</s> (digging) means resolve (<s>saṅkalpa</s>). From <s>śruti</s> texts such as: "He desired: 'May I become many, may I be born forth.' He performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity)." Even though the Lord has all desires fulfilled, he engages in the activity of creation.
The characteristic of aggregate creation
Now, regarding the Lord who speaks truth and is distinguished by all auspicious qualities:
"Of complete sovereignty, valor, fame, prosperity,
wisdom, and dispassion — these six constitute <s>Bhaga</s> (divine attributes), so it is declared."

children.text: iti samagraṣāḍguṇyaparipūrṇasya avāptasamastakāmasya kimarthaṃ sṛṣṭyadikam*{35}* iti cet ucyate.
children.translated_text: If it is asked: for what purpose is creation and the like undertaken by one who is endowed with complete sixfold perfection and has all desires fulfilled? — it is said:
"Immeasurable, not to be commanded, going where he wills, self-sovereign, [MBh 2, App. 21.1605]

children.text: modate bhagavān bhūtaiḥ bālaḥ kīḍanakair iva* //{36}*" [MBh 2, App. 21.1606]
children.translated_text: the Lord delights with beings, as a child with toys." [MBh 2, App. 21.1606]
In accordance with such statements of the <s>Bhārata</s>, it is solely for the sake of <s>līlā</s> (divine play).
For the purpose of experiencing the divine play of the creation of the world, after the aggregate creation by the Lord,

children.text: devamanuṣyādivividhaviśeṣasṛṣṭyarthaṃ caturmukhasṛṣṭiṃ prati dhyānaṃ kṛtam. eṣā cidacidātmikā sṛṣṭiḥ bhagavatā kriyate. vyaṣṭisṛṣṭis tu brahmaṇā. samaṣṭisṛṣṭir nāma:
children.translated_text: meditation was undertaken toward the creation of <s>Caturmukha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) for the purpose of the individual creation of the various specific beings such as gods, humans, and so on. This creation consisting of sentient and insentient beings is performed by the Lord. The individual creation, however, is by <s>Brahmā</s>. The aggregate creation is defined as:

children.text: "bhūtais tu pañcabhiḥ prāṇaiḥ svāntair daśabhir indriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "With five elements, vital breaths, internal organs, and ten sense-faculties —
those who know the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> system know twenty-four principles.

children.text: !{31}! Bezug auf MBh 13.135.119: ātmayoniḥ svayañjāto vaikhānaḥ sāmagāyanaḥ / devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭā kṣitīśaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ.
! Lies mit DHN[T] 54: kṛtavān; vgl. DHN[D] 11.13; vgl. ĀS 4.15cd: viśeṣakhananaṃ tatra kṛtavān kṛtināṃ varaḥ; vgl. ĀS 15.19ab: vedāntatattvamīmāṃsākhananaṃ kṛtvān prabhuḥ.
! Die zweite Vershälfte ist zitiert als "Purātantra" in DHN[D] 33.23.
! Lies mit MBh und DHN[T] 61: krīḍanakair iva.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 31] Reference to MBh 13.135.119: <s>Ātmayoni</s>, self-born, <s>Vaikhānas</s>, singer of the <s>Sāman</s> / <s>Devakīnandana</s>, the creator, lord of the earth, destroyer of sin.

children.text: mahān kālaḥ pradhānañ ca māyāvidyā ca pūruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The great [principle], time, <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>māyā</s> (illusion), <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit) —

children.text: iti paurāṇikāḥ prāhuḥ triṃśattatvāni tais saha //"
children.translated_text: thus the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (followers of the <s>Purāṇas</s>) declare thirty principles together with these."
The characteristic of individual creation

children.text: iti vacanāt tattvasṛṣṭir ity avagamyate. "svāntair" ity anena "mano buddhir ahaṅkāraś cittañ ca karaṇāny amī" ity antaḥkaraṇacatuṣṭayam ucyate. vyaṣṭisṛṣṭir nāma: aṇḍāntarvartibhūtajātasṛṣṭiḥ. "ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇām" "nityo nityānām cetanaś cetanānām". ityādi śrutibhiḥ nityatvena śrutānāṃ prakṛtipuruṣānāṃ sṛṣṭir nāma pralayadaśāyāṃ sūkṣmarūpeṇa avibhaktanāmarūpeṇa ca paramātmany ekībhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭikāle paramātmano 'nupraveśānantaraṃ sthūlarūpavatvaṃ vibhaktanāmarūpabhāktvañ ca. "tat sṛṣṭvā". "tad evānuprāviśat. tad anupraviśya. sac ca tyac cābhavat" ityādi śruteḥ.
children.translated_text: From this statement, it is understood as the creation of principles. By the word "internal organs" [is meant]: "mind, intellect, ego, and thought — these are the four inner instruments." Individual creation is defined as: the creation of the classes of beings existing within the cosmic egg. From <s>śruti</s> texts such as: "The unborn One, red, white, and black," "The eternal among eternals, the conscious among the conscious" — the creation of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit), which are heard of as eternal in the <s>śruti</s>, means that those who during the period of dissolution existed in subtle form with undifferentiated name and form, merged as one in the Supreme Self, at the time of creation, after the Supreme Self's entering into them, attain gross form and differentiated name and form. "Having created that," "He himself entered into it. Having entered into it, he became both the real and the unreal." — from such <s>śruti</s> texts.
In the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>: "This entire world, O best of sages, is imperishable and eternal,
[merely] having the appearance of manifestation and disappearance, of birth and destruction." [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>]
"Entering into <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit) by his own will, <s>Hari</s>
agitated them when the time of creation arrived, [being himself] beyond decay and non-decay." Thus. [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: gītāsu: "prakṛtiṃ puruṣam caiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api /" [BhGī = MBh 6.35.19ab]
children.translated_text: In the <s>Gītā</s>: "Know both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> to be without beginning." [BhGī = MBh 6.35.19ab]

children.text: mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham /
children.translated_text: "My womb is the great <s>Brahman</s>; in that I place the seed,

children.text: sambhavas sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata //" [BhGī = MBh 6.36.3]
children.translated_text: from that arises the birth of all beings, O <s>Bhārata</s>." [BhGī = MBh 6.36.3]
The manner of the production of the cosmic egg and so forth

children.text: iti coktarītyā sṛṣṭikāle jagadyonibhūtaṃ "mahabrahma" tadīyaṃ prakṛtyākhyam ācidvastu*{38}* yat, tasmin cetanākhyaṃ garbhaṃ yojayati. tatkṛtāc cidacitsaṃsargāt devādisthāvarāntānām acinmiśrāṇāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ sambhavo bhavati. evam eva paramātmanā pañcīkṛtānāṃ bhūtānāṃ anyonyasaṃyogādinā aṇḍoptattyādikaṃ*{39}* śrīviṣṇupurāṇe pratipādyate. yathā:
children.translated_text: In the manner thus stated, at the time of creation, the Lord conjoins the seed called 'the sentient' into that which is the womb of the world, the 'great <s>Brahman</s>' — his own material called <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is the insentient substance. From the contact of sentient and insentient produced by that, the birth of all beings arises — from gods down to immovable things, all being mixtures with the insentient. In this same way, the production of the cosmic egg and so forth, through the mutual combination of the elements quintupled by the Supreme Self, is set forth in the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>. As follows:
"Space, wind, fire, water, and earth,
endowed with the qualities of sound and so on, each combined with successively more qualities. [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> 1.2.46]

children.text: śāntā ghorāś ca mūḍhāś ca viśeṣās tena te smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Calm, fierce, and dull — thus their specific qualities are declared,

children.text: nānāvīryāḥ pṛthagbhūtāḥ tataḥ te saṃhatiṃ vinā // [ViṣṇuP ]
children.translated_text: of various powers, existing separately, therefore without cohesion. [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>]
[Footnote 37] Read with DHN[T] 72: āvirbhāvatirobhāvajanmanāśavikalpavat.
Unable to create beings without coming together completely,
coming together in mutual combination, depending upon one another, [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>]
characterized as a single aggregate, and attaining complete unity, [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> 1.2.49cd]
and because of being presided over by <s>Puruṣa</s>, and through the favor of the Unmanifest — [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> 1.2.50ab]

children.text: mahadādyā viśeṣāntā hy aṇḍam utpādayanti te /
children.translated_text: from <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle) down to the specific elements, they produce the cosmic egg.
That, gradually awakened, resembling a water-bubble,
the egg, O great intellect, expanded from the elements, resting upon the waters,
the primordial, unsurpassed abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> whose form is <s>Brahman</s>. [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> 1.2.51]
Therein, he whose form is unmanifest, yet whose form is manifest, the lord of the world,
<s>Viṣṇu</s> himself established himself in the form of <s>Brahmā</s>." [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>]
Beginning from that,
"In that egg, <s>Brahmā</s> came to be, together with <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and humans." [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> 1.2.54]

children.text: ityādibhiḥ samaṣṭisṛṣṭyādikam*{46}* uktam. viśeṣeṇa vyaṣṭisṛṣṭāv api brahmaṇo 'ṇḍādiṣūtpattiprakāraḥ śrūyate. yathā:
children.translated_text: By such statements, the aggregate creation and the like are described. Specifically, in the individual creation too, the manner of <s>Brahmā</s>'s birth in the egg and so forth is heard. As follows:

children.text: mahopaniṣadi: "athāto mahopaniṣadaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ. eko ha vai nārāyaṇa āsīd" ity ārabhya "tasya dhyānāntassthasya yajñastomam ucyate. tasmin caturdaśapuruṣā jāyante. ekā kanyā*{47}*. daśendriyāṇi mana ekādaśaṃ tejo dvādaśam ahaṅkāraḥ trayodaśaḥ praṇāś*{48}* caturdaśaḥ ātmā pañcadaśaḥ buddhir bhūtāni pañca tanmātrāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni ca sa ekaḥ pañcaviṃśaḥ puruṣaḥ."*{49}* "atha punar eva nārāyaṇas so 'nyatkāmo*{50}* manasā dhyāyata tasya dhyānāntassthasya lalāṭāt svedo 'patat, ta imāḥ pratatā āpaḥ, tāsu tejaḥ, tat tejo*{51}* hiraṇmayam aṇḍam tatra brahmā caturmukho 'jāyata."*{52}* iti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Mahopaniṣad</s>: "Now we shall explain the <s>Mahopaniṣad</s>. <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone existed" — beginning thus — "While he was in meditation, what is called the <s>yajñastoma</s> (sacrificial hymn of praise) [arose]. In that, fourteen <s>puruṣas</s> (persons) are born and one <s>kanyā</s> (maiden). The ten sense-faculties, mind as the eleventh, fire as the twelfth, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) as the thirteenth, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) as the fourteenth, <s>ātman</s> (self) as the fifteenth, intellect, the five elements, the five subtle elements, and the five great elements — that is the one twenty-fifth <s>puruṣa</s>." "Then again <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, desiring something else, meditated with his mind. While he was in meditation, sweat fell from his forehead; these are the waters that spread forth. In those [waters] was radiance. That radiance was a golden egg. Therein was born <s>Brahmā</s> with four faces." Thus.
The manner of <s>Brahmā</s>'s birth in the egg and so forth

children.text: yajuṣi: "sa prajāpatir ekaḥ puṣkaraparṇe samabhavat" iti ca.*{53}*
children.translated_text: In the <s>Yajurveda</s>: "That <s>Prajāpati</s> alone came into being upon a lotus leaf." Thus also.

children.text: *{54}*manau: evaṃ "apa eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryam avāsṛjat* //{55}*" ity ārabhya [ManuDhŚ 1.8cd]
children.translated_text: In <s>Manu</s>: thus "He first created the waters, and in them deposited his seed." — beginning thus. [<s>Manu Dharmaśāstra</s> 1.8cd]
"In that [egg] was born <s>Brahmā</s> himself, the grandfather of all worlds." Thus. [<s>Manu Dharmaśāstra</s> 1.9cd]

Bezug auf MahāU 1.1: athāto mahopaniṣadaṃ vyākhyāsyāmas tad āhur eko ha vai nārāyaṇa āsīn na brahmā neśāno nāpo nāgniśomau neme dyāvāpṛthivī na nakṣatrāṇi na sūryo na candramāḥ. sa ekākī na ramate. tasya dhyānāntaḥsthasya yajñastomam ucyate. tasmin puruṣāś caturdaśa jāyante. ekā kanyā. daśendriyāṇi mana ekādaśaṃ tejaḥ. dvādaśam ahaṅkāraḥ. trayodaśaḥ prāṇāḥ. caturdaśaḥ ātmā. pañcadaśī buddhiḥ. bhūtāni pañca tanmātrāṇi. pañca mahābhūtāni. sa ekaḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ puruṣaḥ. tatpuruṣam puruṣo niveśya nāsya pradhānasaṃvatsarā jāyante. saṃvatsarādadhijāyante. atha punar eva nārāyaṇaḥ so 'nyatkāmo manasādhyāyata. tasya dhyānāntaḥsthasya lalāṭān trayakṣaḥ śūlapāṇiḥ puruṣo jāyate. bibhrac chriyaṃ yaśaḥ satyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ tapo vairāṅyaṃ mana aiśvaryaṃ sapraṇava vyāhṛtaya ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvāṅgirasaḥ sarvāṇi chandāṃsi tāny aṅge samāśritāni. tasmād īśāno mahādevo mahād eva. atha punar eva nārāyaṇaḥ so 'nyatkāmo manasādhyāyata. tasya dhyānāntaḥsthasya lalāṭāt svedo 'patat. tā imāḥ pratatā āpaḥ tatas tejo hiraṇyamayam aṇḍam. tatra brahmā caturmukho 'jāyata. children.translated_text: [Footnote 41] <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> reads: ekasaṅghātalakṣmāś ca.
In the <s>Bhārata</s>: "While that god was sleeping, a lotus of splendor equal to the sun

children.text: nābhyāṃ vinissṛtam abhūt tatrotpannaḥ prajāpatiḥ //"*{57}* iti ca smaryate.*{58}* [MBh 3.194.11]
children.translated_text: emerged from his navel; therein was born <s>Prajāpati</s>." Thus it is also remembered. [MBh 3.194.11]

children.text: nanu nābhyām aṇḍe cotpattir ekasya katham upapadyata*{59}* iti cet - tat kalpāntara iti vaktayam. taduktaṃ hayaśira upākhyāne:
children.translated_text: Now, if it is asked: how can the birth of one [being] both from the navel and in the egg be reconciled? — that is to be explained as [occurring in] different <s>kalpas</s>. This is stated in the episode of <s>Hayaśiras</s> (Horse-head):

children.text: ekasya brahmaṇaḥ nābhyām aṇḍe ca utpattiḥ
children.translated_text: The birth of the one <s>Brahmā</s> both from the navel and in the egg
"My first birth from you was mental, honored by the twice-born;

children.text: cākṣuṣaṃ vai dvitīyaṃ me āsīj janma purātanam //
children.translated_text: my second birth was from the eye, that ancient birth of mine.

children.text: tvatprasādāc ca me janma tṛtīyaṃ vācikaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: And by your grace, my third birth was vocal, a great one;

children.text: tvatto me śrāvaṇañ cāpi caturthaṃ janma vai prabho //
children.translated_text: and from you my fourth birth was auditory, O Lord.

children.text: nāsikyañ caiva me janma tvattaḥ pañcamam ucyate /
children.translated_text: And my fifth birth from you is said to be nasal;

children.text: aṇḍajañ cāpi me janma tvattaḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ vinirmittam //
children.translated_text: and my sixth birth from you was egg-born, fashioned [by you].

children.text: idan tu saptamaṃ janma padmajaṃ me 'mitaprabha* /{60}*" iti.
children.translated_text: And this, my seventh birth, is lotus-born, O one of immeasurable splendor." Thus.
<s>Caturmukha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) being denoted by the words <s>Vaikhānasa</s> and so forth

children.text: atas samastajagajjanmasthitidhvaṃsamahānandaikahetoḥ bhagavataḥ parabrahmaṇo nārāyaṇasya vaikhānasādiśabdavācyatvasambhavāt tannābhinalinasañjātasya brahmaṇo 'pi "aṅgād aṅgād"*{61}* iti mantroktaprakāreṇa bhāratādipratipāditarītyā ca*{62}* vaikhānasādiśabdavācyatvam upapadyate.
children.translated_text: Therefore, since it is possible for the Lord, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — the sole cause of the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the entire world, and of supreme bliss — to be denoted by the words <s>Vaikhānasa</s> and so forth, it is also fitting that <s>Brahmā</s>, born from the lotus of his navel, be denoted by the words <s>Vaikhānasa</s> and so forth, in the manner stated by the <s>mantra</s> "from limb to limb" and in the manner set forth in the <s>Bhārata</s> and other texts.
In the <s>Śāntiparvan</s>: "Because he especially dug (<s>akhanat</s>) for the creation of the sages of contemplation,

children.text: tasmād vikhanaso nāma sa āsīd aṇḍajaḥ priyaḥ //" iti [MBh ]
children.translated_text: therefore he was named <s>Vikhanasa</s>, the beloved egg-born one." Thus. [MBh]

children.text: tatraiva: "sraṣṭuṃ sa tu samudyukto brahmayonimayaḥ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: In that same passage: "That lord, composed of the <s>Brahman</s>-source, being intent upon creation,
having dug into himself by himself, endowed with qualities such as <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: dhyānam āviśya yogena hy āsīd vikhanaso muniḥ //" iti [MBh ]
children.translated_text: entering meditation through <s>yoga</s>, became the sage <s>Vikhanasa</s>." Thus. [MBh]

children.text: śrībhāgavate: "na khalu gopikānandano bhavān akhiladehinām antarātmadṛk /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>: "You are certainly not the son of the <s>gopī</s>s; you are the inner Self beholding all embodied beings.

children.text: vikhanasārthito viśvaguptaye sakha udeyivān sāttvatāṃ kule //" iti [BhāgavataP 10.31.4]
children.translated_text: "<s>Vikhanasa</s> (the digger/excavator), sought by [the <s>gopīs</s>], arose in the family of the <s>Sāttvatas</s> for the protection of the universe." Thus [<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.31.4].
The <s>Vaikhānasa</s> worship at <s>Śrīraṅga</s>
In the <s>Gāruḍa</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] — in the <s>Śrīraṅgamāhātmya</s>:
"<s>Brahmā</s> also, with a divine swan, resembling a white cloud,
followed <s>Viṣṇu</s> from behind, covering *{64}* his face with a cloth."

"There, the greatly fortunate one, the venerable <s>Vikhanā</s>, was then *{65}* the priest (<s>arcaka</s>),
and he distributed the <s>prasāda</s> (consecrated offerings) of the gods, by the permission of <s>Raṅganātha</s>." *{66}* Thus [<s>Garuḍa Purāṇa</s>].
In the <s>Śrī Vaikhānasa</s> [tradition] — in the <s>Ānandasaṃhitā</s>:
"Because of the digging out (<s>khanana</s>) of the <s>Vedas</s> that had become hidden,

children.text: sa vibhuḥ procyate sarvaiḥ vikhanā brahmavādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: that all-pervading one is called by all the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> as <s>Vikhanā</s>;

children.text: vaikhānasaś ca bhagavān procyate sa pitāmahaḥ* //{67}*" iti [ĀS ]
children.translated_text: and that grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>), the venerable one, is called <s>Vaikhānasa</s>." *{67}* Thus [<s>Ānandasaṃhitā</s>].

children.text: vyāsanighaṇṭau: "vikhanasañ ca vidhātāraṃ viriñca*{68}* taṃ caturmukham /" iti
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vyāsanighaṇṭu</s>: "<s>Vikhanasa</s> means the Creator (<s>Vidhātṛ</s>), <s>Viriñca</s> *{68}*, the four-faced one (<s>Caturmukha</s>)." Thus.
"Born from the navel (<s>nābhijanman</s>), the first egg-born one, <s>Vikhanā</s>, the lotus-seated one (<s>Kamalāsana</s>),
<s>Śatānanda</s> (having a hundred joys), <s>Śatadhṛti</s> (having a hundred resolves), <s>Satyaka</s> (the truthful one), the one whose vehicle is the swan (<s>Haṃsavāhana</s>), *{69}*

children.text: padmāsano vikhanasaś cāharmukhaḥ*{70}* itīritaḥ //" iti ca pratipāditam.*{71}*
children.translated_text: the lotus-seated (<s>Padmāsana</s>), <s>Vikhanasa</s>, and <s>Āharmukha</s> *{70}* — thus it is declared." And thus it has been established. *{71}*

children.text: evaṃ kāryakāraṇayor abhedāvagamāt*{72}* pramāṇabāhulyāc ca bhagavati nārāyaṇe caturmukhe ca vaikhānasaśabdaprayogaprakāraḥ*{73}* pratipāditaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, because of the understanding of the non-difference between cause and effect, and because of the abundance of authoritative evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>), the manner of the application of the word '<s>Vaikhānasa</s>' to both the venerable <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> *{73}* has been established.
The manner of the origin of the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> *{74}*
The manner of the origin of the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> as stated in <s>Śruti</s>

children.text: vaikhānasānām utpattiḥ viśeṣeṇa śrūyate. yajuṣi āruṇaketuke iṣṭakopadhānakathanānuvāke sṛṣṭiprakaraṇe*{75}* - "āpo vā idam āsan*{76}* salilam eva. sa prajāpatir ekaḥ puṣkaraparṇe samabhavat. tasyāntar manasi kāmas samavartata. idaṃ sṛjeyam iti"*{77}* ity ārabhya "sa tapas taptvā. śarīram adhūnuta. tasya yan māṃsam āsīt. tato 'ruṇāḥ ketavo vātaraśanā ṛṣaya udatiṣṭhan.*{78}* ye 'nakhāḥ te vaikhānasāḥ. ye vālāḥ te vālakhilyāḥ."*{79}* iti. asyārthaḥ. samaṣṭisṛṣṭer anantaraṃ vyaṣṭisṛṣṭau caturmukhaḥ*{80}* devamanuṣyādivividhaviśeṣasṛṣṭyarthaṃ matsyādirūpeṇāvatariṣyamāṇasya*{81}* bhagavato nārāyaṇasya paramavaidikatvena sampratipannaśrīvaikhānasabhagavacchāstramārgeṇa*{82}* samārādhdanarthañ ca svātmatulyāḥ prajās sambhaveyur iti svāntaryāmiṇaṃ paramātmānaṃ dhyonenānukṛtavān*{83}* ayam evārtho brāhmāṇḍe 'py ucyate
children.translated_text: The origin of the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> is heard about in particular detail. In the <s>Yajurveda</s>, in the <s>Āruṇaketuka</s> [section], in the <s>anuvāka</s> describing the laying of bricks (<s>iṣṭakopādhāna</s>), in the passage on creation *{75}* — "In the beginning, these were waters *{76}*, just the ocean. <s>Prajāpati</s> alone came into being on a lotus leaf. Within his mind, a desire arose: 'Let me create this.'" *{77}* — beginning thus, "He, having performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity), shook his body. From what was his flesh, from that arose the <s>Aruṇāḥ Ketavaḥ</s> (the ruddy-bannered ones), the wind-girdled <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages). *{78}* Those who were 'without nails' (<s>anakhāḥ</s>) — they are the <s>Vaikhānasas</s>. Those who were 'hairs' (<s>vālāḥ</s>) — they are the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>." *{79}* Thus. The meaning of this is: After the collective creation (<s>samaṣṭisṛṣṭi</s>), during the individual creation (<s>vyaṣṭisṛṣṭi</s>), the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> *{80}*, for the purpose of creating the various particular beings such as gods and humans, and also for the purpose of properly worshiping the venerable <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — who was to incarnate in forms such as <s>Matsya</s> (the fish) and others *{81}* — through the path of the sacred <s>Vaikhānasa Bhagavacchāstra</s>, which is accepted as supremely Vedic *{82}* — [thinking] 'Let creatures equal to myself come into being' — he meditated upon the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), his own inner controller (<s>Antaryāmin</s>), through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and emulated [Him]. *{83}* This very meaning is stated also in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]:

children.text: "om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharan saṃsmaran harim /
children.translated_text: "Uttering the single syllable '<s>Om</s>' that is <s>Brahman</s>, remembering <s>Hari</s>,
the venerable one, seated in the lotus posture (<s>Padmāsana</s>), undertook the supreme <s>tapas</s> (austerity)." [<s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>]

children.translated_text: !{65}! DHN[D] 26.6 reads with DHN[T] 87: <s>tathā</s>.
The manner of the creation of <s>Sanaka</s> and others

children.text: ity ārabhya*{84}* brahmaṇā brahuśaḥ*{85}* kṛtaṃ tapaścaraṇam uktam. tapaścaraṇakāle sākṣātkṛtabhagavatsvarūpavaibhavānubhavātiśayāt bhagavaddattasṛṣṭiśaktilābhāt tadupajanitaviśeṣavegāc ca pulakitasarvāṅgaḥ śarīram adhūnuta - kampam akarot. "tasya yan māṃsam āsīd"*{86}* māṃsaṃ mānasam iti yāvat. "arthāt prakaraṇāl liṅgād aucityād arthanirṇayaḥ" ity arthādibhiḥ*{87}* samīcīnārthanirṇayavidhānāt "akṣarasāmyān nirbrūyād"*{88}* iti niruktavidhānāñ ca.
children.translated_text: Beginning thus *{84}*, the <s>tapas</s> (austerity) performed by <s>Brahmā</s> many times *{85}* is described. At the time of performing <s>tapas</s>, due to the excess of the direct experience of the essential nature and glory of the Lord that had been directly realized, due to the attainment of the power of creation bestowed by the Lord, and due to the special impetus produced thereby, with all his limbs thrilling with horripilation, he shook his body — he trembled. "From what was his flesh" *{86}* — 'flesh' (<s>māṃsa</s>) means 'mental' (<s>mānasa</s>), that is to say. Because the proper determination of meaning is established "through context, circumstance, indication, and propriety" (<s>arthāt prakaraṇāl liṅgād aucityād arthanirṇayaḥ</s>), and because of the <s>Nirukta</s> principle that "one should derive [the meaning] from similarity of syllables" (<s>akṣarasāmyān nirbrūyāt</s>) *{88}*.

children.text: tathā ca tasya manaḥ paramātmani saṃsaktam āsīd iti yat, tena hetunā tadanugrahas samajani. tenānugṛhītāt brahmaṇaḥ "ketavo vātaraśanāḥ ṛṣayaḥ udatiṣṭhan"*{89}*. "aruṇāḥ" paramātmani vasantaḥ taditararaviktāḥ "ketavaḥ" ucchritasvabhāvāḥ paramātmapravaṇānām agresarāḥ "vātaraśanā" digvāsasaḥ "ṛṣayaḥ" sarvārthadarśinaḥ sanakādayaḥ "udatiṣṭhan" utkṛṣya samabhavan iti.*{90}*
children.translated_text: And thus, because his mind was attached to the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), by that reason, the grace of that [Lord] arose. From <s>Brahmā</s>, who was thus favored by that grace, "the wind-girdled sages arose" *{89}*. "<s>Aruṇāḥ</s>" — dwelling in the Supreme Self, distinct from all others; "<s>Ketavaḥ</s>" — of exalted nature, foremost among those devoted to the Supreme Self; "<s>Vātaraśanāḥ</s>" — sky-clad (naked); "<s>Ṛṣayaḥ</s>" — seers of all truths, namely <s>Sanaka</s> and the others; "<s>udatiṣṭhan</s>" — they arose in an exalted manner. Thus. *{90}*

children.text: idaṃ viṣṇupurāṇe 'pi: "sanandanādayo ye ca pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭās tu vedhasā /
children.translated_text: This is also [stated] in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>: "<s>Sanandana</s> and the others who were first created by the Creator (<s>Vedhas</s>),

children.text: na te lokeṣv asajjanta nirapekṣāḥ prajāvidhau* //{91}* [ViṣṇuP 1.7.9]
children.translated_text: they did not become attached to the worlds, being indifferent to the business of progeny." *{91}* [<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> 1.7.9]

children.text: sarve te yogino jātā*{92}* vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ /

"ye nakhā" ityādi*{94}*. bhagavadanugrahavikasite prajāpater manasi vaikhānasā nāma ṛṣayas sambhūtāḥ atra "ye nakhā" ity atra ādyantavarṇaviparyayo bhavati. children.translated_text: That <s>Prajāpati</s>, seeing them to be of such a nature and incapable of fulfilling his purpose, became somewhat dejected, and again pleased the Lord, his own cause, through the means of meditation, by digging (<s>khanana</s>). "Those who were nails" and so forth *{94}*. In the mind of <s>Prajāpati</s>, which had blossomed through the grace of the Lord, sages named <s>Vaikhānasas</s> were born. Here, in "those who were nails" (<s>ye nakhāḥ</s>), there is a transposition of the initial and final letters. Just as "<s>Kaśyapa</s>" becomes "<s>Paśyaka</s>" (the seer), so "<s>khanā</s>" becomes "<s>nakhā</s>" through transposition — that is the meaning. *{95}*

children.text: evañ ca sati "saumyaṃ jitendriyaṃ"*{102}* "suprasannendriyaṃ"*{103}* ityādinā bhagavacchāstreṣv ācāryalakṣaṇasya*{104}* pratipāditatvāt "vaikhānasa vikhanasācarya"*{105}* iti. viṣṇor*{106}* ācāryatvena śāntyparvaṇy abhihitatvāt.
children.translated_text: And this being so, because the characteristics of an <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) *{104}* have been established in the sacred scriptures of the Lord through [statements such as] "one who is gentle, who has conquered the senses" *{102}* and "one whose senses are well-composed" *{103}* and so forth, [therefore it is said] "<s>Vaikhānasa</s> — having <s>Vikhanasa</s> as preceptor" *{105}*. Because <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s *{106}* preceptorship is declared in the <s>Śāntiparvan</s> [of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>].
"<s>Vikhanā</s> means <s>Viṣṇu</s>; those born from him are known as the <s>Vaikhānasas</s>. *{107}* [<s>Kriyādhikāra</s> 36.28cd]

children.text: iti vacanāt, "guros sānavṛttir*{108}* vaikhānasa"*{109}* iti bodhāyanasūtre uktatvāc ca bhāgavatādiṣu*{110}* pratipāditam "ācāryapuṃstvam eteṣāṃ vaikhānasānām*{111}* eve"ty avagamyate.

mayā sañcodito yasmāt tvam eva munisattama* //
ātmārthaṃ vā parārthaṃ vā nityanaimittikādi yat // [Ā.S 4.39]
athāha sa ṛṣis tasmai praṇamya jagadātmane // [ĀS 4.40]
nātaḥ parataraṃ kāryaṃ kim apy anyad divaukasām* //
