children.translated_text: as <s>Viṣṇu</s> is [foremost] among the three forms (<s>trimūrti</s>), and <s>Sadāśiva</s> among the <s>Śivas</s>, // [Brahmakaivarta.P]

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ vaiṣṇavo dharmaḥ smṛtīnāṃ mānavī smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>Vaiṣṇava dharma</s> among <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Mānava smṛti</s> (Laws of Manu) among <s>smṛtis</s>,
as among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> learned in the <s>Veda</s>, the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> is the best, // [Brahmakaivarta.P]
as <s>Vikhanas</s> is called the primordial among sages,* /{359}*

children.text: sūtrāṇāṃ tatpraṇītan tu yathā śreṣṭhatamaṃ smṛtam // [Brahmakaivarta.P ]
children.translated_text: as the <s>sūtra</s> composed by him is remembered as the most excellent, // [Brahmakaivarta.P]
so too, O king, <s>Puṣkara</s> is the best of the best among pilgrimage sites."*{360}* [BrahmakaivartaP]
In the <s>Kūrma</s> [Purāṇa]:
"Their minds fixed on me, their life-breath devoted to me, their minds absorbed in me,
having no other refuge, O king — therefore the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> are the best.* //{361}*" [KūrmaP]
The presence of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in places inhabited by <s>Vaikhānasas</s>
In another <s>Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: "yatra vaikhānasā viprā yatra santi gavāṃ gaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Where there are <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, where there are herds of cows,

children.text: yatra bilvāḥ palāśāś ca tatra sannihito hariḥ* //{362}*"
children.translated_text: where there are <s>Bilva</s> and <s>Palāśa</s> trees — there <s>Hari</s> is present.* //{362}*"
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s> [Purāṇa]:
"Those who always worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> are purifiers of the world,

children.text: durvṛttā vā suvṛttā vā pūjanīyā viśeṣataḥ //" [BṛhannāradaP]
children.translated_text: whether of bad conduct or good conduct, they are especially worthy of honor." // [BṛhannāradaP]
In <s>Hārīta</s>:

children.text: tasmāt te śuddhasattvasthāś śuddhā vaikhānasāḥ smṛtāḥ* /{363}*
children.translated_text: Therefore they, established in pure <s>sattva</s>, are known as the pure <s>Vaikhānasas</s>,* /{363}*

children.text: yān lokān prāpnuvanty ete tān śṛṇuṣva samāhitaḥ //"
children.translated_text: the worlds which they attain — hear about those attentively."
In the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, [specifically] the <s>Pauṣkara</s> [Saṃhitā]:

children.text: "viprā vaikhānasākhyā ye te bhaktās tattvam ucyate* //{364}* [PauṣkaraS 36.260cd]
children.translated_text: "Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> called <s>Vaikhānasas</s> — they are truly called devotees.* //{364}* [PauṣkaraS 36.260cd]
They are exclusively devoted (<s>ekāntin</s>), established in pure <s>sattva</s>, until the end of their body they do not sacrifice to any other [deity],

children.text: !{359}! Diese Zeile fehlt im Zitat in DHN[D] 26.19-27.2.
! Die Verse bis hier sind ähnlich auch als "Brahmakaivartapurāṇa" in DHN[D] 26.19-27.2 zitiert.
! Dieser Vers ist auch zitiert in DHN[D] 118.10-11.
! Dieser Vers ist auch zitiert in DHN[D] 48.23-24 und 118.8-9.
! DHN[T] 183: tasmāt te śuddhasatvasthāś śuddhā vaikhānasā smṛtāḥ /.
! PauṣkaraS: viprā ekāyanākhyā ye te bhaktās tattvato 'cyute; dieser Halbvers ist als "Pauṣkarasaṃhitā" ähnlich zitiert in 24.6, 42.25, 48.18, 118.12, als "Purātantra" ähnlich in DHN[D] 36.24.

children.translated_text: !{359}! This line is missing from the citation in DHN[D] 26.19-27.2.

children.text: kartavyam iti deveśaṃ saṃyajante phalaṃ vinā* //{365}* [PauṣkaraS 36.261]
children.translated_text: [Thinking] 'it is one's duty' — they worship the Lord of Gods without [desire for] fruit.* //{365}* [PauṣkaraS 36.261]

children.text: prāpnuvanti ca dehānte vāsudevatvam abjaja //" iti*{366}* [PauṣkaraS 36.262ab]
children.translated_text: And at the end of their body they attain the state of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O Lotus-born One." *{366}* [PauṣkaraS 36.262ab]
In the <s>Gautamīya</s>:
"One who knows the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> injunctions, established in the truth of the self,

children.text: sūkṣmāt sūkṣmam avāpnoti paraṃ brahmāṇam avyayam //" iti
children.translated_text: attains that which is subtler than the subtle — the supreme, imperishable <s>Brahman</s>." //
The <s>Vaikhānasa</s> hermitage at <s>Puṣkara</s>
In the <s>Āraṇyaparvan</s> (Book of the Forest): <s>Rāmeśa</s> [says]:*{367}*
"And the <s>Saindhavāraṇya</s> (Sindhu Forest) was contemplated, frequented by hosts of sages,*{368}* [MBh 3.87.12cd]
the sacred lake of the Grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>), the holy <s>Puṣkara</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>. // [MBh 3.87.12ef]

children.text: vaikhānasānāṃ siddhānām ṛṣīṇām āśramaṃ priyam* //{369}*" iti [MBh 3.87.13]
children.translated_text: The beloved hermitage of the perfected <s>Vaikhānasa</s> sages.* //{369}*" [MBh 3.87.13]
Elsewhere:
"Having reached the <s>Saindhavāraṇya</s> (Sindhu Forest), that river which reveals the world,*{370}*

children.text: puṣkareṣu mahārāja sarveṣu ca jalaṃ spṛśan //" ity ārabhya [MBh 3.125.12]
children.translated_text: touching the water in all the <s>Puṣkaras</s>, O great king —" beginning thus, [MBh 3.125.12]
"To this <s>Candrasaras</s> (Moon-Lake) the sages always offer,* /{371}*
the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> and the like, and the <s>Vālakhilyas</s> as well." // [MBh 3.125.14]
The honorability of the <s>Vaikhānasas</s>
Elsewhere: <s>Gālava</s> [says]:
"I see all the worlds*{372}* by your grace, O one of excellent vows,

children.text: vaikhānasānāṃ japatām eṣa śabdo mahātmanām //" iti [MBh 3.114.15]
children.translated_text: — this is the sound of the great-souled <s>Vaikhānasa</s> sages who are chanting." // [MBh 3.114.15]
In the <s>Gāruḍa</s> [Purāṇa]:
"He assigned three villages to the <s>Kauṣītakin</s> sacrificial priests,

children.text: akalpayac ca trīn grāmān vaikhānasamahātmanām //" iti [GaruḍaP ]
children.translated_text: and assigned three villages to the great-souled <s>Vaikhānasas</s>." // [GaruḍaP]
In the <s>Parameśvara</s> [Saṃhitā], in the thirteenth chapter, on the occasion of the distribution of purificatory rites:*{373}*
"One should worship those preceded by the accomplished (<s>āpta</s>), the ascetics preceded by renunciants,* //{374}* [PārameśvaraS 12.437cd]
the five [classes of] <s>Vaikhānasas</s>, and likewise the four [classes] beginning with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
those devoted to the five yogas and other <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> twice-born,* //{375}* [PārameśvaraS 12.438]
first among those who hear the teachings of the <s>Ekāyanī</s> branch.* //{376}*" [PārameśvaraS 12.439ab]

children.text: !{365}! PauṣkaraS: kartavyatvena ye viṣṇuṃ saṃyajanti phalaṃ vinā; der erste Halbvers ist auch als "Pauṣkarasaṃhitā" zitiert in DHN[D] 48.18, ähnlich als "Purātantra" in DHN[D] 37.1; der ganze Vers als "Pauṣkarasaṃhitā" in DHN[D] 24.7-8, 42.26-43.1 und 118.13-14.
! Dieser Halbvers ist auch zitiert in DHN[D] 43.2 und 118.15.
! MBh: khyātaṃ ca saindhavāraṇyaṃ puṇyaṃ dvijaniṣevitam; DHN[T] 183: khyātaṃ.
! MBh: etac candramasas tīrtham arpayanty ṛṣayas tathā; DHN[T] 184: arpayantsṛṣayas.

! Vgl. die folgende Stelle mit JayākhyaS 22.78-80: [pavitrotsavānte kṛtasya yatyādibhyo dānasya phalādhikyakathanam]: pañca vaikhānasāntāś ca yatipūrvāś ca nārada / āptādipañcabhedena catvāro brāhmaṇādayaḥ // pañca yogaratādyās tu śāstrasandhārakāntimāḥ <śāstrasaṃdhārakāntimāḥ> / asaṃkhyaṃ yataye dattaṃ vaiṣṇavāya prakīrtim <prakīrtitam> // viddhi koṭiguṇañ <koṭiguṇaṃ> caiva dattam ekāntine tu yat / tasmād daśaśatāṃśonaṃ dattaṃ yac chikhine tu vai //.
! PārameśvaraS: pañcavaikhānasasāntāṃś ca tathānyān vaiṣṇavān dvija.

children.translated_text: !{365}! PauṣkaraS: 'they who worship Viṣṇu as a duty, without [desire for] fruit'; the first half-verse is also cited as "<s>Pauṣkarasaṃhitā</s>" in DHN[D] 48.18, similarly as "<s>Purātantra</s>" in DHN[D] 37.1; the entire verse as "<s>Pauṣkarasaṃhitā</s>" in DHN[D] 24.7-8, 42.26-43.1, and 118.13-14.

children.text: nāradīye: "sāttvike tu sadādhikyaṃ pūjanaṃ mama nārada /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nāradīya</s> [Purāṇa]: "Worship given in the <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) mode is always supreme in my [estimation], O <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: viddhi vaikhānase dattaṃ dānaṃ brahmavidas tathā //"*{377}* [NāradaP]
children.translated_text: know that a gift given to a <s>Vaikhānasa</s> who knows <s>Brahman</s> [is likewise supreme]."*{377}* [NāradaP]
The worship of <s>Vaikhānasas</s> performed by <s>Śrī Rāma</s>
In the <s>Vāsiṣṭharāmāyaṇa</s>: "Having been consecrated [as king], contented, together with his ministers and well-wishers,

children.text: pūjayāmāsa dharmātmā rāmo vaikhānasān munīn //" iti [Vāsiṣṭharāmāyaṇa]
children.translated_text: the righteous <s>Rāma</s> worshipped the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> sages." // [Vāsiṣṭharāmāyaṇa]
The devotion of the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> to the five daily observances (<s>pañcakāla</s>)
The definition of devotion to the five daily observances (<s>pañcakālaparāyaṇa</s>)
In the <s>Śāṇḍilyasmṛti</s>: "Those who purify the earth with their feet, devoted to the five daily observances (<s>pāñcakālika</s>),
by merely seeing or touching them, all beings attain fulfillment. // [Śāṇḍilyasmṛti]

children.text: ijyāmadhye tathā home yoge ca japakarmaṇi /
children.translated_text: During sacrifice, during the fire-offering, in <s>yoga</s>, and in the practice of chanting (<s>japa</s>),
one who has arrived and knows the five daily observances should be worshipped and asked to recite the supreme [teaching]. // [Śāṇḍilyasmṛti]
Those who ceaselessly gratify those devoted to the five daily observances —

children.text: sakāmās tatphalaṃ yānti niṣkāmāḥ paramaṃ padam // [Śāṇḍilyasmṛti]
children.translated_text: if they have desires, they obtain the fruit thereof; if desireless, they attain the supreme state. // [Śāṇḍilyasmṛti]
Those who always maintain the sacred fires, who are tranquil, who abstain from food of <s>Śūdras</s>,

children.text: mām arcayanti madbhaktās tebhyo dattam ihākṣayam // [Śāṇḍilyasmṛti.]
children.translated_text: who worship me as my devotees — what is given to them here is imperishable. // [Śāṇḍilyasmṛti]
One who knows the truth of the twelve syllables (<s>dvādaśākṣara</s>), who understands the division of the four <s>vyūhas</s> (emanations),
who knows the unbroken five daily observances — that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> shall [cause others to] cross over.* //{378}*" [Śāṇḍilyasmṛti]
The <s>Vaikhānasas</s>' knowledge of the truth of the twelve syllables
As follows:
'One who knows the truth of the twelve syllables' — the twelve syllable-truths [are]:

"Consciousness (<s>cit</s>), the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Manas</s> (mind), <s>sattva</s> and the other <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),

children.text: vyomāgnimarutaś cāpo varṇānāṃ tattvam īritam* //{379}*" ity uktāni. [PādmaS caryāpāda 24.19]
children.translated_text: space (<s>vyoman</s>), fire (<s>agni</s>), wind (<s>marut</s>), and water (<s>āpas</s>) — these are declared to be the truths of the syllables.* //{379}*" Thus stated. [PādmaS caryāpāda 24.19]
The <s>Vaikhānasas</s>' knowledge of the division of the four <s>vyūhas</s>
'Who understands the division of the four <s>vyūhas</s>' — [means]:
The difference in nomenclature of the four <s>vyūhas</s> between the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> and <s>Pāñcarātra</s> traditions

children.text: "puruṣañ ca tatas satyam acyutañ ca yudhiṣṭhira / [MBh 14, App. 4.1659]
children.translated_text: "<s>Puruṣa</s>, then <s>Satya</s>, and <s>Acyuta</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, [MBh 14, App. 4.1659]

children.text: aniruddhañ ca māṃ prāhur vaikhānasavido janāḥ* //{380}* [MBh 14, App. 4.1660]
children.translated_text: and <s>Aniruddha</s> — thus do the knowers of the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> [tradition] call me.* //{380}* [MBh 14, App. 4.1660]

children.text: anye tv evaṃ vijānanti māṃ rājan pāñcarātrikāḥ / [MBh 14, App. 4.1661]
children.translated_text: But others know me thus, O king — the <s>Pāñcarātrikas</s>: [MBh 14, App. 4.1661]

children.text: vāsudevañ ca rājendra saṅkarṣaṇam athāpi vā* //{381}* [MBh 14, App. 4.1662]
children.translated_text: as <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O great king, and also as <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>,* //{381}* [MBh 14, App. 4.1662]

children.text: !{377}! Vgl. JayākhyaS 22.81: sātvatāya śatāṃśonaṃ daśāṃśonaṃ tu nārada / viddhi vaikhānase dattaṃ dānaṃ pratisarāvadhau.

! Vgl. PR 2, S. 52: dvādaśākṣaratattvajñaś caturvyūhavibhāgavit / achidrapañcakālajñaḥ sa tu bhāgavataḥ smṛtaḥ //. Vedānta Deśika gibt keine Quelle für diesen Vers an, zitiert aber im Anschluß "Śāṇḍilya" mit dem folgenden Vers: caturvyūhavibhāgajñaḥ pañcakālaparāyaṇaḥ / dvādaśākṣaraniṣṭho yaḥ sa vai bhāgavatottamaḥ.
! Dieser Halbvers ist ähnlich in DHN[D] 23.22 zitiert.
! Dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 23.23-24 zitiert.

children.translated_text: !{377}! Cf. JayākhyaS 22.81: 'to a Sātvata [one gives] less by a hundredth, and to [those on the path of] <s>Nārada</s> less by a tenth; know that a gift given to a Vaikhānasa [is measured] by the limit of a vessel.'

children.text: pradyumnañ cāniruddhañ ca*{382}* caturmūrtiṃ pracakṣate / [MBh 14, App. 4.1663]
children.translated_text: <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s>*{382}* — [thus] they speak of the four forms (<s>caturmūrti</s>). [MBh 14, App. 4.1663]

children.text: etāś cānyāś ca rājendra saṃjñābhedena mūrtayaḥ* //{383}* [MBh 14, App. 4.1664]
children.translated_text: And these and other forms, O best of kings, differ by their designations. [MBh 14, App. 4.1664]

children.text: viddhi me 'rcāntarāṇy eva mām evañ cārcayed budhaḥ //"*{384}* [MBh 14, App. 4.1665]
children.translated_text: Know them as varieties of my images; thus should the wise one worship me." [MBh 14, App. 4.1665]
Thus the division of the four <s>vyūha</s>s (emanations) stated above is to be understood.
The twofold nature of <s>Vāsudeva</s> as divine and human

children.text: evaṃ vaikhānase daivikamānuṣabhedena vāsudevo dvividhaḥ pratipādyate. yathā -
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> tradition, <s>Vāsudeva</s> is taught as twofold, through the distinction of divine (<s>daivika</s>) and human (<s>mānuṣa</s>). As follows:

children.text: khile: "athordhvaṃ vāsudevasya mānuṣasya vidhiṃ paraṃ". ity ārabhya "mānuṣyavapuṣaṃ devaṃ dvibhujaṃ śaṅkhacakriṇam" ityādinā rukmiṇīpradyumnāniruddhasāmbabrahmagaruḍādiyutaṃ mānuṣavāsudevaṃ nirvarṇya punaḥ:
children.translated_text: In the <s>Khila</s>: beginning with "Now the supreme rite of the human <s>Vāsudeva</s>," and describing by means of "the god in human form, two-armed, bearing conch and discus" and so forth, the human <s>Vāsudeva</s> together with <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Sāmba</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Garuḍa</s> and others; and then again:
"I shall declare the divine <s>Vāsudeva</s> in due order:
The <s>vimāna</s> (celestial chariot) may be of the <s>Somacchanda</s> type or the <s>Bṛhadvṛtta</s> type,
The god bearing four arms, supreme, bearing conch and discus,
The right hand in the gesture of fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>), the left hand resting on the hip,
Adorned with all ornaments including the crown and so forth,
The god wearing red garments, measured by ten <s>tāla</s>s in proportion,

children.text: ubhe devyāv ubhe pārśve pūrvavat kārayed budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise one should fashion both goddesses on both sides as described previously,
With <s>Balabhadra</s> and others as previously stated, either with weapons or without weapons,

children.text: tattad devībis hier tnoch telugu vergleichensamāyuktaṃ vinā vā samyag ācaret /
children.translated_text: Accompanied by the respective goddesses [note: compare Telugu here], or without them, one should properly perform the rite,
<s>Revatī</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and <s>Ramā</s>, and <s>Cendukarī</s>,

children.text: raktaṃ nīlaṃ tathā śyāmaṃ pītavarṇaṃ samācaret /
children.translated_text: One should make them red, blue, dark, and yellow in color respectively,
Wearing crowns, diadems and the like, adorned with all ornaments,

children.text: evaṃ puṣpadharaṃ kuryād ekañ caiva prasāritam /
children.translated_text: Thus one should make one holding a flower and one with hand extended,

children.text: devyā yuktaṃ vinā vāpi dvimārgaṃ samyag ācaret //"
children.translated_text: With or without the goddess, one should properly perform the two-path rite."

children.text: ity ārabhya "evaṃ daivikamārgan tu sthāpanārambham ācared" ityādinā daivikaḥ vāsudevaḥ*{386}* pradarśitaḥ.
children.translated_text: Beginning with this and continuing with "Thus one should commence the installation according to the divine path" and so forth, the divine <s>Vāsudeva</s> is demonstrated.

children.text: ! Dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 24.1-2 zitiert.
! Dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 24.3-4 zitiert; MBh: viddhy anarthāntarā eva.

children.translated_text: [Editorial note: See also MBh 16.4.43c.]
The absence of <s>pañcakālaparāyaṇatva</s> (devotion to the five daily observances) among those following sūtras other than <s>Vaikhānasa</s>

children.text: itthaṃ vāsudevādīnāṃ daivikamānuṣabhedena dvaividhyasya, "puruṣaṃ paramapuruṣaṃ paramātmānaṃ paraṃ brahmāṇam" ityādinā pratipāditānāṃ caturṇāṃ puruṣādīnāṃ mūrtivibhāgasya ca śrīvaikhānasaśāstre pratipādanāt, etas sarvavibhāgajña eva caturvyūhavibhāgavid ity anenocyate. ācchidrapañcakālajña iti:*{387}*
children.translated_text: Thus, since the twofold nature of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and others through the distinction of divine and human, and the division of the forms of the four beginning with <s>Puruṣa</s> as taught by "<s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Paramapuruṣa</s>, <s>Paramātman</s>, <s>Parabrahman</s>" and so forth, are established in the sacred <s>Vaikhānasa</s> teaching, it is said that only one who knows all these divisions is a knower of the fourfold <s>vyūha</s> division, and is one who knows the <s>pañcakāla</s> (five daily observances) without interruption:
"In the morning time, <s>abhigamana</s> (approaching the deity);
Then <s>upādāna</s> (gathering materials); at midday one should perform <s>ijyā</s> (worship);
And <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) in the afternoon; <s>yoga</s> (meditation) in the evening — these are declared as the five times." [<s>Vaikhānasāgama</s>]
With reference to the <s>pañcakālaparāyaṇa</s> (devotion to the five daily observances) taught in the section on dwelling, the following statements were made:

children.text: "ye pāvayanti dharaṇīṃ" "ijyāmadhye tathāhome" "ye toṣayanty avirataṃ" iti vacanāni, sāmanyena pañcakālaparāyaṇasya darśanasparśanādibhis sarveṣāṃ pāvanatāṃ kṛtārthatāṃ, ijyāyogādisamayeṣu cāgatasya tasya pūjanāntaraṃ śeṣakarmācaraṇañ ca pratipādayanti, etādṛśaḥ pañcakālaparāyaṇaḥ kīdṛśā ity ākaṅkṣāyāṃ "dvādaśākṣaratattvajña" ityādinā "acchidrapañcakālajña" ity antena tallakṣaṇam ucyate.
children.translated_text: The statements "Those who purify the earth," "In the midst of worship and in the fire-offering," and "Those who please without cessation" teach that the <s>pañcakālaparāyaṇa</s> purifies everyone through seeing, touching, and so forth, and that during the times of worship, <s>yoga</s>, and other observances, one who has arrived should perform remaining rites after the intermediate worship. As to what kind of person this <s>pañcakālaparāyaṇa</s> is, the definition is stated beginning with "one who knows the truth of the twelve-syllable mantra" and ending with "one who knows the five times without interruption."

children.text: īdṛśācchidrapañcakālaparāyaṇā vaikhānasā eva. vaikhānasaśāstra eva pañcakālavibhāgasya pratipāditatvāt. svasvasūtre 'nuktatvād āpastambīyādayas tu na. pañcakālapratipādanarahitasūtrāntaraniṣṭhānāṃ:*{389}*
children.translated_text: Such unbroken devotees of the five daily observances are only <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s, because the division of the five times is taught only in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> teaching. The followers of <s>Āpastamba</s> and others are not, since it is not stated in their respective <s>sūtra</s>s. For those established in other <s>sūtra</s>s that lack the teaching of the five times:

children.text: "brāhme muhūrte buddhyeta dharmārthāv anucintayan* /{390}*" ity ārabhya
children.translated_text: "One should awaken at the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> (auspicious pre-dawn hour), reflecting on <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>," beginning thus
"And in the second portion, the study of the <s>Veda</s>s is prescribed;
And in the third portion, reflection on the welfare of dependents;

children.text: bhāge caturthe kurvīta snānam ambhasy akṛtrime //
children.translated_text: In the fourth portion, one should bathe in natural water;

children.text: pañcame tu tathā bhāge saṃvibhāgo yathārhataḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the fifth portion, distribution according to what is proper;
The sixth and seventh portions one should spend with the <s>Itihāsa</s>s and <s>Purāṇa</s>s;

children.text: aṣṭame lokayātrāñ ca vicārya ca gṛhī tataḥ //"
children.translated_text: And in the eighth, the householder, having considered worldly affairs, then..."

children.text: !{387}! DHN[T] 188-189 statt DHN[D] 46.1-5: itthaṃ vāsudevādīnāṃ vyūhabhūtāṇāṃ daivikamānuṣabhedena vyūhacaturmūrtipratipādanāt "puruṣaṃ paramapuruṣaṃ paramātmānaṃ paraṃ brahmāṇam" ityādinā caturṇāṃ puruṣādīnāṃ mūrtivibhāgasya ca śrīvaikhānasaśāstre pratipāditatvāt. "acchidrapañcakālajñaḥ".
! DHN[T] 189 statt DHN[D] 46.9 iti vāsādhikāre pratipāditvāt.

! DHN[T] 189-190 statt DHN[D] 46.10-17: "ye pāvayanti dharaṇīṃ" "ijyāmadhye viśeṣataḥ" "ye toṣayanty avirataṃ" pañcakālaparāyaṇān iti sāmānyena pañcakālaparāyaṇasya darśanasparśanādibhis sarveṣāṃ pāvanatāṃ kṛtārthatāṃ, coktvā ijyāyogādisamayeṣu cāgataṃ pañcakālajñaṃ saṃpujyānantaraṃ śeṣakarmācaraṇam uktvā etad guṇaviśiṣṭāḥ ka ity ākaṅkṣāyāṃ aviratapañcakālaparāyaṇā ity anenācchidrapañcakālaparāyaṇā? evety uktaṃ. acchidrapañcakālaparāyaṇa vaikhānasā eva. svaśāstre pratipāditatvāt. svasvasūtreṣv anuktatvād āpastambādīnām tu na.
! Diese Verszeile ist als "Manu" (ManuDhŚ 4.92ab) zitiert in TPC 14.16-17.

children.translated_text: [Editorial note: DHN[T] 188-189 instead of DHN[D] 46.1-5: variant reading of the passage on <s>vyūha</s>-division and <s>pañcakāla</s>.]

children.text: ity antena dakṣādismṛtyantareṣu brāhmaṇajāteḥ sāmānyena tattatkāleṣu kartavyatvena pratipāditakarmācaraṇa eva yathāyogyaṃ yogyatāsambhavāt.*{391}*
children.translated_text: By the end of these, since suitability is possible only through the performance of duties prescribed for the brāhmaṇa class in general for their respective times in the <s>smṛti</s>s of <s>Dakṣa</s> and others, as appropriate.
Otherwise,

children.text: "vidharmaḥ paradharmaś ca ābhāsa upa vā cchalaḥ*{392}* /
children.translated_text: "<s>Vidharma</s> (opposed dharma), <s>paradharma</s> (another's dharma), and <s>ābhāsa</s> (semblance), <s>upadharma</s> (subsidiary dharma), and <s>chala</s> (deception),
These are the five branches of <s>adharma</s> — the knower of <s>dharma</s> should abandon what is <s>adharma</s>.
<s>Vidharma</s> is that which obstructs <s>dharma</s>; <s>paradharma</s> is that enjoined for another;
<s>Upadharma</s> is heresy (<s>pāṣaṇḍa</s>); <s>chala</s> is hypocrisy and deceit (?);

children.text: yas tv icchayā kṛtaṃ pumbhir ābhāso hy āśramād bahiḥ //".
children.translated_text: And that which is done by men according to their own desire, outside the <s>āśrama</s> system, is <s>ābhāsa</s> (mere semblance)."
Thus the fault of resorting to another's <s>dharma</s> as stated in the words of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> is relevant here.
"Better is one's own <s>dharma</s>, though imperfectly performed, than the <s>dharma</s> of another well-performed;
Death in one's own <s>dharma</s> is preferable; the <s>dharma</s> of another is fraught with danger." [MBh 6.25.35]
And there would be a contradiction with the word of the Blessed Lord.
The status of <s>devalaka</s> (degraded temple priest) for those following other <s>sūtra</s>s and followers of <s>Pāñcarātra</s>

children.text: kiñca tatsūtreṣu dvādaśākṣaratattvādipratipādanam api nāsti. evaṃ "sati kuḍye citrakarme"ti nyāyena yajñopavītadhāraṇasandhyopāsanabhagavadārādhanādividhipratipādanarahitasūtrāntaraniṣṭhānāṃ, tathā śrīmannārāyaṇasya samānatvena rudrādidevatāntarārādhanavidhipratipādakasūtraniṣṭhānāñ ca caturvyūhavibhāgajñānāsambhavāt bhagavadārādhanasvarūpajñānābhāvena pañcakālaparāyaṇatvādigandhaleśo 'pi na sambhavati. sūtrāntaroktamārgeṇa vā pañcarātroktamārgeṇa vā bhagavadārādhanaṃ kurvato 'nadhikāriṇo devalakatvaṃ pratipādyate.*{397}*
children.translated_text: Moreover, in those <s>sūtra</s>s there is no teaching of the truth of the twelve-syllable mantra and the like. Thus, by the maxim "when there is a wall, then painting on it," for those established in other <s>sūtra</s>s that lack the teaching of the rites of wearing the sacred thread, <s>sandhyā</s> worship, worship of the Lord, and so forth, and likewise for those established in <s>sūtra</s>s that teach the worship of other deities such as <s>Rudra</s> on an equal footing with the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, since knowledge of the fourfold <s>vyūha</s> division is impossible, and since there is no knowledge of the true nature of the worship of the Lord, not even a trace of <s>pañcakālaparāyaṇatva</s> is possible. The status of <s>devalaka</s> (degraded priest) is declared for one who performs worship of the Lord without proper authority, whether by the method stated in other <s>sūtra</s>s or by the method stated in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>.
The teaching of worship of other deities such as <s>Durgā</s> in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>

children.text: tathā hi - pañcarātre viṣvaksenasaṃhitāyāṃ nāradaṃ prati viṣvaksenoktiḥ:
children.translated_text: For in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, in the <s>Viṣvaksenasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>'s speech to <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: "idan tu tava vakṣyāmi guhyād guhyatamaṃ mune /
children.translated_text: "I shall now tell you, O sage, the most secret of the secret:

children.text: yo 'sau nārayaṇas*{398}* sākṣāt sa hi vighneśa ucyate* //{399}* [ViṣvaksenaS 10.114]
children.translated_text: He who is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself is called the Lord of Obstacles (<s>Vighneśa</s>). [<s>Viṣvaksenasaṃhitā</s> 10.114]

children.text: yo vai vighneśa ity uktas sa vai nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // [Viṣvaksena.S 10.115ab]
children.translated_text: He who is called <s>Vighneśa</s> is indeed held to be <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; [<s>Viṣvaksenasaṃhitā</s> 10.115ab]

children.text: naiva bhedaṃ vijānanti munayas tattvadarśinaḥ* //{400}*" ity ārabhya [ViṣvaksenaS 10.116ab]
children.translated_text: The sages who see the truth perceive no difference between them." Beginning thus, [<s>Viṣvaksenasaṃhitā</s> 10.116ab]

children.text: !{391}! DHN[T] 191 statt DHN[D] 47.1-2: ity pañcakālapratipādanarahita sūtrāntaraniṣṭhānāṃ brāhmaṇajāti sāmānyatvena dakṣādismṛtyantareṣu yathāyogyaṃ kālāntareṣu pratipāditakarmācaraṇa yogyatāsaṃbhavāt.
! DHN[T] 192: bhayāvaha; dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 67.7-8 zitiert.

! DHN[T] 192-193 statt DHN[D] 47.13-19: kiñca sarvasūtreṣu dvādaśākṣaratattvādipratipādanābhāvāt evaṃ "sati kuḍye citrakarme"ti nyāyena yajñopavītadhāraṇasandhyopāsanabhagavadārādhanādividhipratipādanarahitasūtrāntaraniṣṭhānāṃ, caturvyūhavibhāgajñānāsambhavāt bhagavadārādhanasvarūpapratipādanābhāve pañcakālaparāyaṇatvādigandhaleśāsaṃbhavāt. bhagavatā śrīmannārāyaṇena samānatvena rudrādidevatāntarārādhanavidhipratipādakasūtraniṣṭhasya pañcakālaparāyanatvāsaṃbhavāt sūtrāntaroktamārgeṇa vā pañcarātroktamārgeṇa vā bhagavadārādhanaṃ kurvato 'nadhikāriṇaḥ devalakatva pratipādanāt.
! ViṣvaksenaS: idaṃ tu tava vakṣyāmi guhyād guhyataraṃ mune.
! ViṣvaksenaS: naiva jānanti tadbhedaṃ munayas tatvadarśinaḥ.

children.translated_text: [Editorial note: DHN[T] 191 variant reading for DHN[D] 47.1-2.]
"One may make a noose and goad, or else a conch and discus;

children.text: ākhuṃ vāpi khagendraṃ vā tasya vāhanam ācaret* //{402}* [ViṣvaksenaS ]
children.translated_text: One should make a mouse or the king of birds as his vehicle; [<s>Viṣvaksenasaṃhitā</s>]
Because he is a portion of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and because he is non-different, O great sage,

children.text: vīśas tadvāhanaṃ proktaṃ ākhuṃ vāpi samācaret // [Viṣvaksena.S ]
children.translated_text: His vehicle is declared to be as stated; one may also make a mouse. [<s>Viṣvaksenasaṃhitā</s>]

children.text: tasmāc chriyañ ca durgāñ ca vāṇīṃ vighneśam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s> (Sarasvatī), and <s>Vighneśa</s> (Gaṇeśa),

children.text: svatantreṇārcayed dhīmān sarvakāryārthasiddhaye //" ityādi ca dṛśyate. [ViṣvaksenaS ]
children.translated_text: The wise one should worship independently for the accomplishment of all aims." And so forth is seen. [<s>Viṣvaksenasaṃhitā</s>]

children.text: devatāntarāṇāṃ aṅgabhāvenārcanaṃ na niṣiddhyate. "svatantrabuddhyā kurvan vai brāhmaṇo narakaṃ vrajet" ityādi vacanaiḥ aṅgatvena vinā svātantryeṇāṅgivyatiriktadevatāntarārādhanaṃ niṣiddhyate. tathāvidhaniṣiddhadevatāntarārcanapratipādakaśāstraniṣṭhasya pañcakālaparāyaṇatvaṃ na sambhavati.*{404}*
children.translated_text: The worship of other deities as subsidiary parts is not prohibited. By statements such as "a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who does so with the notion of independence goes to hell," the independent worship of deities other than the principal deity, without their being subsidiary, is prohibited. <s>Pañcakālaparāyaṇatva</s> is not possible for one established in a teaching that prescribes such prohibited independent worship of other deities.
Only supreme exclusive devotees (<s>paramaikāntin</s>s) can have <s>pañcakālaparāyaṇatva</s>
"By those who know the five times, exclusive devotees (<s>ekāntin</s>s), who have worshipped <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: nūnaṃ tatra mato devo yathā tair vāgudīritaḥ //" ity uktarītyā
children.translated_text: Surely the god is pleased there, as declared by their words." In accordance with this statement,
The absence of <s>paramaikāntitva</s> (supreme exclusive devotion) among non-<s>Vaikhānasa</s>s

children.text: paramaikāntitvāsambhave tad(pañcakālaparāyaṇatvā)sambhavāt. paramaikāntitvañ ca bhagavadekaparatvam eva. tac ca svātantryeṇānyadevatāyājināṃ vaikhānasavyatiriktānāṃ hi na sambhavati.*{405}*
children.translated_text: Since <s>pañcakālaparāyaṇatva</s> is impossible without <s>paramaikāntitva</s>. And <s>paramaikāntitva</s> is exclusively being devoted to the Lord alone. And that is not possible for those other than <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s, who independently worship other deities.

children.text: atra "yair iṣṭaḥ pañcakālajñair" ity anena pañcakālavyatiriktakālāntarapratipādakaśāstraniṣṭhānāṃ*{406}* vyavṛttiḥ. "ekāntibhir narair" ity anena
children.translated_text: Here, by the phrase "by those who know the five times," those established in other teachings that prescribe different time-divisions are excluded. By the phrase "by exclusive devotees,"

children.text: "viprā vaikhānasākhyā ye te bhaktās tattvam ucyate* //{407}* [PauṣkaraS 36.260cd]
children.translated_text: "The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s called <s>Vaikhānasa</s> — their devotion is declared to be the truth; [<s>Pauṣkarasaṃhitā</s> 36.260cd]
Exclusive, established in pure <s>sattva</s>, until death they worship no other deity. [<s>Pauṣkarasaṃhitā</s> 36.261ab]

children.text: ityādi pauṣkarasaṃhitāvacanānusāreṇa*{409}* svātantryeṇa durgādidevatāntarārcanapratipādakapāñcarātraśāstraniṣṭhānāṃ*{410}* vyāvṛttiḥ. "nūnam atra mato deva" ity anena - "yatra vaikhānasā viprā yatra santi gavāṃ gaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, in accordance with the statements of the <s>Pauṣkarasaṃhitā</s>, those established in <s>Pāñcarātra</s> teachings that prescribe independent worship of other deities such as <s>Durgā</s> are excluded. By the phrase "surely the god is pleased there" — "Where <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s are, where herds of cows are,

children.text: yatra bilvāḥ palāśāś ca tatra sannihito hariḥ* //{411}*"
children.translated_text: Where <s>bilva</s> and <s>palāśa</s> trees are, there <s>Hari</s> is present" —

children.text: ity asyārtho jñāpyate iti "yair iṣṭa" iti kṛtsnam api vacanaṃ vaikhānasaparam ity evāvagamyate.*{412}*
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is made known, and thus the entire statement beginning with "by whom worshipped" is understood to refer to <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s alone.

children.text: !{401}! DHN[T] 193: cakraśaṅkhāv; vgl. ViṣvaksenaS 11.294: evaṃ cakrādisaṃproktam aparaṃ cādhunā śṛṇu / dakṣiṇe paraśuṃ nyasya hy adhaḥ pāśāṅkuśaṃ nyaset.
! Vgl. ViṣvaksenaS 11.297cd: ākhus tadvāhanaṃ proktaṃ garuḍaṃ vāgrataḥ smaret.
! Vgl. ViṣvaksenaS 11.298ab: nārāyaṇāṃśakatvāc ca proktas tatra khageśvaraḥ /; DHN[T] 193: nārāyaṇāṃśakatvāc ca vyāvṛtatvān?.

! DHN[T] 194 statt DHN[D] 48.6-10: iti tatra aṅgabhāvena devānāṃ arcanam na niṣiddhyate. "svatantrabuddhyā kurvan vai brāhmaṇo narakaṃ vrajet" ityādi vacanaiḥ aṅgatvena vinā svatantryeṇāṅgivyatiriktadevatāntarārādhanavidhipratipādakaśāstraniṣṭhasya pañcakālaparāyaṇatvābhavādidoṣasaṃbhavāt.

! DHN[T] 194-195 statt DHN[D] 48.13-15: paramaikāntitvāsambhave pañcakālaparāyaṇatvāsambhavāt. (pañcakālasya) bhagavadekaparatvāc ca pañcakālasyācchidrapañcakālaparāyaṇatvaṃ śrīmadvaikhānasavyatiriktānāṃ na sambhavati.
! PauṣkaraS: viprā ekāyanākhyā ye te bhaktās tattvato 'cyute; dieser Halbvers ist als "Pauṣkarasaṃhitā" ähnlich zitiert in 24.6, 42.25, 48.18, 118.12, als "Purātantra" ähnlich in DHN[D] 36.24.
! Dieser Halbvers ist auch zitiert in DHN[D] 43.1, 48.19, 118.13, als "Purātantra" in DHN[D] 37.1.
! Dieser Vers ist auch als "Varāhapurāṇa" zitiert in DHN[D] 118.8-9 und als "Purāṇa" in DHN[D] 42.16-17.
! DHN[T] 196: ity asyārtho jñāpitaḥ iti vākyatrayam api vaikhānasaparatvenāvagamyate.

children.translated_text: [Editorial note: DHN[T] 193 variant: cakraśaṅkhāv; cf. <s>Viṣvaksenasaṃhitā</s> 11.294.]

children.text: pāñcarātriṇām api pañcakālaparāyaṇatvam ity ākṣepaḥ parihāraś ca
children.translated_text: The objection and its refutation regarding whether <s>Pāñcarātrika</s>s also have <s>pañcakālaparāyaṇatva</s>
Objection:
<s>Brahmā</s>: "O Lord, here the excellence of knowledge of the five-time ritual procedure

children.text: kathitaṃ pañca ke kālā vidhayaś cāpi pañca ke* //{414}* [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.1]
children.translated_text: Has been declared; what are the five times and what are the five ritual procedures? [<s>Pādmasaṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.1]
Tell me, who am desirous of knowing, as it truly is;

children.text: na ced rahasyam atyantaṃ yad ahaṃ pṛṣṭavān iha* //{415}* [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.2]
children.translated_text: If what I have asked here is not extremely secret." [<s>Pādmasaṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.2]
The Blessed Lord said:
The <s>abhigamana</s> (approaching) as taught in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>
The first rite is <s>abhigamana</s> (approaching the deity); then <s>upādāna</s> (gathering materials) is next,

children.text: ijyā tapaś ca svādhyāyas tathā yogaḥ prakīrtitaḥ* //{417}* [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.3]
children.translated_text: Worship (<s>ijyā</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and likewise <s>yoga</s> are proclaimed. // {417} // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.3]

children.text: pañcaite vidhayas teṣāṃ kālāḥ pañcaiva te kramāt /
children.translated_text: These five are the observances; their times are five, in order:
Whatever class of actions extends up to the auspicious conduct, O <s>Caturmukha</s> (Four-Faced One, i.e. <s>Brahmā</s>). // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.4]
This, beginning with arising and so forth in order, is called 'approach' (<s>abhiyāna</s>).

children.text: brāhme muhūrte buddhyeta dhyāyan nārāyaṇaṃ param // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.5]
children.translated_text: One should awaken at the <s>Brāhma muhūrta</s> (pre-dawn hour), meditating upon the supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.5]
Having arisen, one should sit upon the bed, chanting the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> name.

children.text: krameṇa sṛṣṭvā tattvāni deham utpādya tattvavit // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.6]
children.translated_text: Having sequentially emanated the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) and produced the body, the knower of truth // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.6]

children.text: svasya*{418}* dehe ṣaḍaṅgāni mantram uccārya mānasam //" [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.7]
children.translated_text: should utter mentally the <s>mantra</s> of the six limbs (<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>) upon one's own body." // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.7]
Having thus commenced with <s>abhigamana</s> (approach),
"With collyrium, ointments, garlands, garments, and ornaments likewise, // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.29ab]
With lac-dye, betel (<s>tāmbūla</s>), mouth-cleansers, and the like,

children.text: upeto maṅgalair anyair nayed abhigamakriyām //" [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.30]
children.translated_text: Furnished with these and other auspicious things, one should perform the rite of approach (<s>abhigama</s>)." // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.30]
Thus <s>abhigamana</s> (approach) has been stated.
The <s>upādāna</s> (gathering of materials) as taught in <s>Pāñcarātra</s>
"Then one should gather the implements for worship as they truly are, // {420}

children.text: puṣpāṇi phalamūlāni vividhāny oṣadhīr api // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.31]
children.translated_text: Flowers, fruits, roots, and various herbs as well, // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.31]

children.text: dadhyādi ca haviryogyaṃ taṇḍulādi guḍādi ca*{421}* /
children.translated_text: And curds and the like suitable for oblation, unhusked rice, jaggery, and the like, // {421}

children.text: snānīyāni ca vastrāṇi svādūni salilāni ca // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.32]
children.translated_text: And bathing materials, garments, and pleasant waters. // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.32]

children.text: ! PādmaS: vihitaṃ (kathitaṃ v.l.) pañca ke kāle.
! PādmaS: ijyā ca paścāt svādhyāyas tato yogas tataḥ paraṃ; DHN[T] 196: ijyā ca paścāt svādhyāyas tato.

children.translated_text: {413} <s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>: 'The knowledge of the five-time observance is praised here, O <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
<s>Darbha</s> grass, leaves, and sacrificial sticks, according to one's ability and means,

children.text: āhṛtya yājñiyān daivān pūjāsthāne niveśayet* //{422}* [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.33]
children.translated_text: Having gathered the sacrificial and divine [implements], one should place them at the site of worship. // {422} // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.33]
Having brought [these to complete] the time of gathering (<s>upādāna</s>), one should then worship accordingly."
Thus <s>upādāna</s> (gathering) has been stated.
The <s>ijyā</s> (worship) as taught in <s>Pāñcarātra</s>
"When the midday time has arrived, one should perform bathing according to prescribed rules." // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.34]
Beginning from this,
"Having completed all the ritual actions appropriate to the midday time, // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.41cd]

children.text: kṛtvā yajeta deveśaṃ homāntaṃ kamalāsana // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.42ab]
children.translated_text: Having performed [them], one should worship the Lord of Gods, concluding with the fire-offering, O <s>Kamalāsana</s> (Lotus-Seated One). // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.42ab]

children.text: ijyāyās samayas tasyāḥ kathitaḥ kamalāsana //" [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.66ab]
children.translated_text: The time of that worship has been stated, O <s>Kamalāsana</s>." // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.66ab]
Having thus stated the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
The <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) as taught in <s>Pāñcarātra</s>

children.text: "mandire vā harer nadyās tīre vāmarabhūmiṣu*{423}* // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.66cd]
children.translated_text: "In the temple of <s>Hari</s>, or on the bank of a river, or on <s>Amara</s> grounds, // {423} // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.66cd]

children.text: vivikte vipine vāpi parvate vā gṛhe 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: Or in a secluded forest, or on a mountain, or even at home,

children.text: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni vidyamānāny anekadhā* //{424}* [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.67]
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛc</s> verses, <s>Yajus</s> formulas, <s>Sāman</s> chants -- the various existing ones, // {424} // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.67]
Through the divisions of branches, the root branch called <s>Ekāyana</s>, // {425}
The triple <s>Veda</s> in essence -- one should study, seated comfortably and concentrated." // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.68]
Having stated <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study),
The <s>yoga</s> as taught in <s>Pāñcarātra</s>
"Then when the evening <s>sandhyā</s> (junction time) has arrived, what is prescribed there: // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.72cd]
Having performed all the <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>homa</s> (fire-offering), and the rest,
Having worshipped the Supreme Person according to proper rule, as before, completely, // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.73]
Having eaten food and retired to bed, // {426} // having risen at the great midnight,

children.text: ācamya prayato bhūtvā dhyātvā paramapūruṣam // [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.74]
children.translated_text: Having sipped water and become purified, having meditated upon the Supreme Person, // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.74]
Seated in the <s>yoga</s> posture, one should yoke the self by the self, // {427}
In the manner prescribed, according to one's ability, O <s>Caturmukha</s>. // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.75]
Following the order of withdrawal (<s>saṃhāra</s>), one should withdraw the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) into the self,

children.text: ātmānañ cāpi hṛtpadme paramātmani niṣṭhite // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.76]
children.translated_text: And the self also into the lotus of the heart, established in the Supreme Self. // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.76]

children.text: ! PādmaS: bhidyamānāny anekadhā; so auch DHN[T] 198.

children.translated_text: {422} <s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>: 'Having gathered [them] with sacrificial implements, or...'

children.text: saṃhared itthato*{429}* yogāt svāpaṃ kleśāpahaṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: One should withdraw thus through <s>yoga</s> and enter sleep that removes afflictions.

children.text: ity eṣa kathito brahman yogaḥ kālaś ca pañcamaḥ // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.77]
children.translated_text: Thus has been stated, O <s>Brahman</s>, <s>yoga</s> and the fifth time-period." // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.77]
These five time-periods and five observances have been shown in them.

children.text: ittham eteṣu kāleṣu darśitaiḥ karmabhir naraḥ // [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.78]
children.translated_text: Thus, through the actions shown at these times, a man // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.78]
Who performs the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s> does not fail.

children.text: varṣeṣu dvādaśasu*{431}* evam anutiṣṭhan samāhitaḥ // [Pādma.S caryāpāda 13.79]
children.translated_text: Practicing thus with concentration for twelve years, // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.79]
The entire collection of ritual actions leads to the attainment of <s>sāyujya</s> (union [with the Lord]).

children.text: ṣaṭsu varṣeṣu sārūpyaṃ sāmīpyaṃ triṣu niścitam* //{432}* [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.80]
children.translated_text: <s>Sārūpya</s> (having the same form) [is attained] in six years, <s>sāmīpya</s> (proximity) in three -- this is certain. // {432} // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.80]

children.text: sālokyaṃ phalam ekasmin vatsare nātra saṃśayaḥ //" [PādmaS caryāpāda 13.81ab]
children.translated_text: <s>Sālokya</s> (residing in the same world) is the fruit in one year -- there is no doubt about this." // [<s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>, <s>caryāpāda</s> 13.81ab]

children.text: iti pādme caryāpāde trayodaśe 'dhyāye avicchinnatayā pañcakālānāṃ*{433}* pratipāditatvāt teṣām apy acchidrapañcakālaparāyaṇatvaṃ sambhavatīti cet*{434}* - tad asat.
children.translated_text: Thus, since the five time-periods are taught continuously in the thirteenth chapter of the <s>caryāpāda</s> of the <s>Pādma</s> [-<s>Saṃhitā</s>], it is possible for them also to have unbroken devotion to the five time-periods without gaps.
The non-fixed, limited, gap-permitting devotion to the five time-periods of the <s>Pāñcarātrikas</s>
In the same [text]:
"The time before dawn (<s>pūtyūṣa</s>), midnight, and morning, midday, and
These five time-periods are declared; then, in the four time-periods,
Those who are deficient [should practice] at pre-dawn -- this is to be understood, O <s>Caturānana</s> (Four-Faced One)."

children.text: ity abhigamanādīnām ekarūpeṇa vinā nyūnātiriktakālatvenoktatvāt "kālaṃ madhyandinacchidra*{438}*pañcakālaparāyaṇair" ity āgamasiddhānte "sāntarālam anuṣṭhānaṃ pañcakāloditaṃ tathā" iti tantrasiddhānte ca chidrapañcakālaparatvasyoktatvāt*{439}*, kālacatuṣṭayapratipādanena niyatapañcakālaparāyaṇatvābhāvāt, dvādaśavarṣam ārabhya ekavarṣaparyantaṃ parimitapañcakālaparatvasyoktatvāt*{440}* dvādaśavarṣād ūrdhvaṃ pañcakālaparatvābhāvāc ca.*{441}*
children.translated_text: Since <s>abhigamana</s> and the rest, with the exception of one form [i.e. one time-period], are stated as having reduced or extended times, the statement in the <s>Āgamasiddhānta</s> "the time for those devoted to the five time-periods with a gap at midday"...
Likewise, in the <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]:
"The great midnight is to be known as the middle of the night, of the second [watch]. // {442}

children.text: tasyāṃ snānaṃ na kurvīta samyag ācamanaṃ tathā //" [MarkaṇḍeyaP]
children.translated_text: At that time one should not perform bathing nor proper <s>ācamana</s> (sipping of water)." // [<s>Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa</s>]
{429} <s>Pādma-Saṃhitā</s>: 'having risen'; so also DHN[T] 199.
Because of the prohibition of <s>ācamana</s> (sipping) at the great midnight. // {443}
"But one who sleeps for two watches becomes fit for absorption into <s>Brahman</s>."

children.text: iti dharmaśāstroktanidrākāle yogasyāyuktatvāc ca. yogakālasyārdharātrikatve svādhyāyakālād vyavahitatvena chidrapāñcakālikatvāpātāc ca.*{444}*
children.translated_text: And because <s>yoga</s> is improper during the time of sleep prescribed in the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>. And because, if the time for <s>yoga</s> were at midnight, it would be separated from the time of <s>svādhyāya</s>, resulting in a gap in the five-time-period observance. // {444}

children.text: kālacatuṣtvāsyaivoktatvena abhigamanādiṣv ekasya lopasambhavena aniyatapañcakālaparasya pañcakālaparāyaṇaśabdābhilāpāsambhavāc ca.*{445}*
children.translated_text: And because, since only four time-periods are stated [as required], with the possibility of the omission of one among <s>abhigamana</s> and the rest, the designation by the word 'devoted to the five time-periods' is not possible for one devoted to [only] an unspecified [number of] five time-periods. // {445}
Likewise:
"The sense organs of those who are deeply asleep become afflicted and deteriorate,

children.text: aṅgāni samatāṃ yānti uttamāny adhamais saha* //{446}*"
children.translated_text: And the limbs reach a state of equality, the superior together with the inferior. // {446}"

children.text: iti dharmaśāstreṣu prātar ārabhya sāyaṅkālaparyantam eva karmācaraṇakālatvena pratipādanāt.
children.translated_text: Because in the <s>Dharmaśāstras</s> the time for performing ritual actions is taught as extending from morning up to the evening time only.
Likewise: // {447}
"The body is extremely impure, endowed with nine openings,

children.text: sravaty eva divārātraṃ prātas snānaṃ viśodhanam //
children.translated_text: It flows constantly day and night; morning bathing is the purifier.
Without bathing, one should not perform any ritual action such as <s>japa</s> or <s>homa</s>;

children.text: snātvādhikārī bhavati daive pitrye ca karmaṇi //"
children.translated_text: Having bathed, one becomes authorized for divine and ancestral rites."

children.text: iti smṛteḥ snānāt pūrvaṃ tattvasṛṣṭer ayuktatvāc ca. pretaprāyasya saṃhṛtatattvasya svāpayogyatāsambhavāc ca. tasmāt "abbhakṣo vāyubhakṣa" ityādiśabdavadavadhāraṇagarbhasya pāñcakālikaśabdasya aniyataparimitapāñcakālikeṣu pāñcarātrikeṣu prayogāsaṃbhavād aniyataparimitachidrapāñcakālikāḥ pāñcarātriṇo na niyatāchidrapañcakālaparāyaṇavaikhānasatulyā bhavitum ahantīti*{448}* siddham.*{449}*
children.translated_text: Because, according to this <s>smṛti</s>, the emanation of <s>tattvas</s> before bathing is improper. And because sleep is not possible for one who has withdrawn the <s>tattvas</s> and is like a departed soul. Therefore, 'whether subsisting on water or subsisting on air'...
Refutation of the objection that a worshipper of the deity is a mere temple-servant (<s>devalaka</s>)
Now, [an objection:]
"A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who worships a deity for three years seeking wealth,
He indeed is called a <s>devalaka</s> (temple-servant), excluded from oblations to gods and ancestors. // {450}"

children.text: iti devatāpūjakasya devalakatvaṃ sambhavatīti cet - tad asat. sāmānyataḥ devatārādhanaṃ ye kurvanti te devalakā iti vā? uta śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇādiṣu mukhyādhikāritvena pratipāditā apīti vā?. sāmānyataḥ devatārādhanaṃ ye kurvanti te iti cet - tarhi gṛhadevatāpūjakānām api devalakatvaprasaṅgaḥ. kiñca:*{451}*
children.translated_text: If it be said that worshippers of the deity are thus [classified as] <s>devalakas</s> -- that is wrong. [The question is:] is it that those who perform worship of the deity in general are <s>devalakas</s>? Or is it according to <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>...

children.text: ! DHN[T] 201: yogasyāyuktatvāt. yogakālasya vyavahitatvāt tatrāpi chidrapāñcakālikatvāt.
! DHN[T] 201 statt DHN[D] 52.5-6: kālacatuṣṭaye 'bhigamanādiṣv ekasya lopasambhavād aniyamitacchidrapañcakālaparasya pāñcakālikasya parāyaṇaśabdā(bhilāpā)sambhavāt.
! DHN[T] 201 führt diesen Vers erst einige Sätze später an (s.u.).
! DHN[T] 201: sāyaṅkālaparyantānām eva (kālānāṃ) ācaraṇakālatvena pratitatvāt. (yathā): hier wird der Śloka, der mit kliśyantīha beginnt, in DHN[T] 201 angeführt.

! DHN[T] 202 statt DHN[D] 52.16-20: ti snānāt pūrvaṃ tattvasṛṣṭer ayuktatvāt. pretaprāyasya saṃhṛtatattvasya svāpayogyatāsambhavāt. "abbhakṣo vāyubhakṣa" ityādi śabdāvadavadhāraṇagarbhasya pāñcakālika(pañcakāla)śabdasya ... aniyamitaparimita pāñcakālikeṣu pāñcarātrikeṣu saṃbhavayogyatābhāvāc cāniyataparimitaviṣam acchidrapāñcakālikāḥ pāñcarātriṇo niyatāchidrapañcakālaparāyaṇo vaikhānaso iti (ca) siddham.

! DHN[T] 234: havyakavyabahiṣkṛta; Kane, HD 2.1, S. 109, Anm. 232, gibt an, daß dies ein Zitat von Devala in Smṛticandrikā II (S. 396) und bei Aparārka (S. 450 und 923) sei. Dort liest er allerdings: devārcanaparo vipro vittārthī vatsaratrayam / asau devalako nāma havyakavyeṣu garhitaḥ //. Vgl. Colas, 1996, S. 135, Anm. 2. Dieser Vers wird im Text Devalakanirṇaya einem Gautama zugeschrieben.

! DHN[T] 234 statt DHN[D] 52.24-53.2: iti devatāpūjakasya devalakatvaṃ sambhavatīti cet - tad asat. sāmānyatvena devatārādhanaṃ ye kurvanti te devalako iti vā? uta śrutismṛtisūtrapurāṇādiṣu mukhyādhikāritvena pratipāditāḥ. sāmānyatvena kurvantīti cet - tarhi gṛhadevatāpūjakānām api devalakatvaprasaṅgaḥ. kiñca.

children.translated_text: {443} DHN[T] 201 omits 'because of the prohibition of <s>ācamana</s> at the great midnight.'
The absence of <s>devalaka</s>-status for <s>Vaikhānasas</s>
"The <s>brahmacārin</s>, the householder, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and likewise the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, // {452}

children.text: kurvanti*{453}* nijakarmāṇi viṣṇum eva yajanti te //"
children.translated_text: They perform their own prescribed duties -- they worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone."

children.text: iti sandhyopāsanādīnāṃ bhagavadārādhanarūpatvoktyā*{454}* teṣāñ ca tyāgas sambhavati. atas sāmānyataḥ iti*{455}* vaktum ayuktam. śrutismṛtipurāṇādiṣu*{456}* mukhyādhikāritvena pratipāditā devalakāḥ*{457}* iti cet - tad asat. "'agnir vai devānām avamo viṣṇuḥ paramas tadantareṇa sarvā anyā devatā'; iti brāhmaṇam. tasmād gṛhe paramaṃ viṣṇuṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sāyaṃ prātar homānte 'rcayati" iti vaikhānasasūtre*{458}*, "pravaḥ pāntam andhaso dhiyāyate maheśūrāya viṣṇave cārcata"*{459}* iti ṛgbrāhmaṇam anusṛtya*{460}* viṣṇupradhānatayā "sa vā eṣa puruṣaḥ pañcadhā pañcātmā" ityādiśrutyuktaviṣṇvādipañcamūrtīnām*{461}* ārādhanasya pratipāditatvāt*{462}*.
children.translated_text: Since by the statement that <s>sandhyā</s> worship and the like are of the nature of worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, their abandonment is possible. Therefore it is improper to say 'in general'...

children.text: āśvamedhike "kathaṃ tvam arcanīyo 'sī"*{463}*tyādeḥ, vṛddhamanau "vedāntavedibhir"*{464}* ityādeś coktatvāt.
children.translated_text: Because of the statements in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> [section]: 'How are you to be worshipped?' // {463} // and in the <s>Vṛddhamanu</s>: 'By those who know the <s>Vedānta</s>' // {464} // and so forth.

children.text: evam eva pāñcarātraśaivaśilpajyautiṣādiṣu utkṛṣṭamukhyādhikāripratipādakānāṃ vacanānāṃ vaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt tanmūlabhūtaśrutismṛtipurāṇādīnām aprāmāṇyaprasaṅgo duṣpariharaḥ.*{465}*
children.translated_text: Likewise, because there would be the unwanted consequence of meaninglessness of the statements that teach the superior and primary qualified persons in <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, <s>Śaiva</s>, architecture, astrology, and the like, and of the <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and other texts that form their basis...
The absence of fault in the enjoyment of materials belonging to the <s>Bhagavān</s> for <s>Vaikhānasas</s>

children.text: evaṃ ca pramāṇabhūteṣu śrutismṛtipurāṇādiṣu pratipāditānām ācārādīnāṃ tyāgaḥ prasajyet, niṣphalatvāt. nanu paradravyoṇālayārcanaṃ*{466}* kurvatāṃ devalakatvam iti cet na.*{467}*
children.translated_text: And thus there would be the unwanted consequence of the abandonment of the practices and the like taught in the authoritative <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and other texts, because they would be fruitless. Now, [regarding] the worship of the temple image with another's materials...

children.text: śrutismṛtipurāṇādiṣu tattacchāstreṣu ca ālayārcakānāṃ*{468}* mukhyādhikāritvena taddravyopabhogārhatvena ca pratipādanāt.*{469}*
children.translated_text: Because in <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and other texts, as well as in the respective <s>śāstras</s>, it is established that temple priests (<s>ālayārcakas</s>) are the primary qualified persons and are entitled to enjoy the materials offered to the deity.
As follows — in the <s>Ānandasaṃhitā</s> spoken by <s>Marīci</s>, after setting forth the origin and so on of <s>Vikhanasa</s>:
"Similarly, while living dependent on you and enjoying your materials,

children.text: yad bhaved doṣa utpanna iti cintākulo 'smy aham* //{470}*" [ĀS 4.77]
children.translated_text: should any fault arise — thus I am troubled with anxiety." [ĀS 4.77]

children.text: iti bhagavaddravyopajīvanadoṣabhīroḥ vikhanasaḥ*{471}* bhagavantaṃ prati praśne -
children.translated_text: When <s>Vikhanasa</s>, fearful of the fault of subsisting on the Lord's materials, thus questioned the Lord —
"Then <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> spoke to that fearful, best among sages: [ĀS 4.78ab]
For the <s>Vaikhānasas</s>, who perform my rites, that fault does not exist. [ĀS 4.83ab]

children.text: !{452}! Dieser Halbvers ist ähnlich in DHN[D] 21.2 zitiert.
! DHN[T] 235 om. vaikhānasasūtre. Bezug auf VaikhSmS 4.10, darin ist AitareyaBr 1.1.1 als "Brāhmaṇaṃ" zitiert.
! DHN[T] 235: śrutyanusāreṇa viṣṇvādipañcamūrtīnām ārādhanaṃ pratipāditaṃ statt ityādi śrutyaktaviṣṇvādipañcamūrtīnām ārādhanasya pratipāditatvāt.
! MBh App. 4.1652a; auch zitiert in DHN[D] 23.15.
! Bezug auf den in DHN[D] 23.12-13 zitierten Vers.

! DHN[T] 236 statt DHN[D] 53.14-15: evam eva pañcarātraśaivaśilpajyotiṣādiṣu mukhyādhikāritvena utkṛṣṭatvena ca pratipādita?vacanānāṃ vaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt tanmūlabhūtaśrutismṛtipurāṇādīnām aprāmāṇyaprasaṅgo duṣpariharaḥ.
! DHN[T] 236 statt DHN[D] 53.16-17: kiṃ ca, apramāṇabhūteṣu śrutismṛtipurāṇādiṣu pratipāditānām ācārādīnāṃ tyāgaḥ kartavyaḥ niṣphalatvāt. paradravyeṇālayārcanaṃ kurvatāṃ devalakatvam iti cen na.

! ĀS: tavānujīvane caiva tvad dravyānubhavād api / utpatsyate doṣo iti bhṛśaṃ cintākulosmy ahaṃ; vgl. ĀS 16.43cd/44ab: sadā tvad anujīvitvāt tvaddravyānubhavād vibho // doṣābhaveyu.s sarveṣām iti cintākulo 'smy ahaṃ.
! ĀS: ity ukto munisattamaṃ; DHN[T] 237: athovāca hṛṣīkeśa ity uktaṃ munisammataṃ.
! ĀS: vaikhānasānāṃ tad doṣo nāsti matkṛtajanmanāṃ; vgl. ĀS 16.45cd: vaikhānasānāṃ tad doṣo nāsti matkṛtakarmaṇāṃ.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 452] This half-verse is similarly cited in DHN[D] 21.2.
My materials, for the purpose of <s>havya</s> (oblations to gods) and <s>kavya</s> (oblations to ancestors), for gifts, and for honoring guests, [ĀS 4.84cd]

children.text: mukhyam evāstu bhavatāṃ sadā matkarma kurvatām // [Ā.S 4.85ab]
children.translated_text: shall indeed be the primary [entitlement] for you who always perform my rites. [ĀS 4.85ab]
There is no fault for <s>Vaikhānasas</s> even in the sale of the Lord's images

children.text: kim ebhir bahubhir vākyair anyat te kathayāmy aham* //{474}* [ĀS 4.85cd]
children.translated_text: What need is there for many words? I shall tell you something else. [ĀS 4.85cd]
Regarding my materials, fields, images, and temples, in times of distress,
in matters of selling and the like, there is no fault by my command. [ĀS 4.87]

children.text: tasmād bhavān abhimatas sarvaṃ karma sadā kuru // [ĀS ]
children.translated_text: Therefore, you who are dear to me, always perform all rites. [ĀS]
Through the enjoyment of my wealth, [and] through the omission of my rites on your part,
since [you exist] in truth as my body, there is no offense." [ĀS 4.86]
Thus, by citing the words of the Lord, the absence of fault in the enjoyment of the Lord's materials and the like is established.

children.text: atra "ahaṃ bhaktaparādhīno hy asvatantra iva dvija" ityādivacanānusāreṇārcakaparādhīnatāṃ darśayituṃ, bhagavatprītiviṣayīkṛtānāṃ vaikhānasānāṃ taddravyopabhogādiṣu doṣagandho nāstīti pratipādanāvasare "maddravyaṃ kṣetrabimbādī"tyādinā kaimutikanyāyam abhipretya bhagavadvigrahavikraye kṛte 'pi doṣo nāstīty ucyate. tāvatā na tad abhipretam.*{479}*
children.translated_text: Here, in accordance with statements such as "I am dependent on my devotee, as if not self-sovereign, O twice-born," in order to show [the Lord's] dependence on the priest, and on the occasion of establishing that for <s>Vaikhānasas</s> who are objects of the Lord's affection there is not even a trace of fault in the enjoyment of his materials and the like — by the words "My materials, fields, images, etc.," intending the argument a fortiori, it is stated that there is no fault even when the Lord's image is sold. But that much is not the intended [permission].

children.text: nanv evam api devadravyopabhogadoṣas sāmānyataḥ mukhyāmukhyādhikāriṣu sarveṣv āpadyate eva iti cet na.*{480}*
children.translated_text: Now, if it is objected that even so, the fault of enjoying temple property applies in general to all qualified persons, both primary and secondary — no.
Falling into hell through meat-eating
"Those who eat the flesh of living beings who desire to live,

children.text: bhakṣyante te 'pi tais sarvair iti brahmābravīt svayam* //{482}* [MBh 13.117.33]
children.translated_text: they too are eaten by all of those — thus <s>Brahmā</s> himself declared." [MBh 13.117.33]

children.text: māṃ sa bhakṣayitām utra yasya māṃsam ihādmy aham /
children.translated_text: "He will eat me in the next world, whose flesh I eat here —
this is the 'flesh-ness' of flesh, so declare the wise." [MBh 13.117.34]

children.text: na hi māṃsaṃ tṛṇāt kaṣṭhād upalād vāpi jayate /
children.translated_text: "For flesh does not arise from grass, wood, or stone;

children.text: hatvā jantuṃ bhaven māṃsaṃ tasmāt tat parivarjayet* //{484}* [MBh 13.116.26]
children.translated_text: flesh comes from killing a creature, therefore one should avoid it." [MBh 13.116.26]

children.text: hantā caivānumantā ca viśas tā krayavikrayī /
children.translated_text: "The killer, the approver, the one who cuts up, the buyer and seller,

children.text: saṃskartā copakartā ca khādakaś cāṣṭa ghātukāḥ* //{485}* [MBh 13.116.47]
children.translated_text: the preparer, the server, and the eater — these are the eight slaughterers." [MBh 13.116.47]

children.text: !{474}! Vgl. ĀS 16.47ab: kiṃ ebhir bahubhir vākyais satyam eva vadāmy ahaṃ.
! ĀS: maddravyaṃ kṣetrabimbādīn vālayāni yathāpadi; vgl. ĀS 16.49ab: maddravyaṃ kṣetrabiṃbāni ālayāni ? yathāpadi; DHN[T] 237: maddravyakṣetrabimbādisālayāni yathāpadi.
! Vgl. ĀS 16.49cd: vikrīṇanādikāryeṣu nāsti doṣo mamājñayā; DHN[T] 237: yadājñayā.
! Vgl. ĀS 16.50: madīyadhanabhogena matkriyālāpanena ca / maccharīratayā satyam apacāro na vidyate //.

! DHN[T] 237-8 statt DHN[D] 54.10-14: "ahaṃ bhaktaparādhīnā hy asvatantra iva dvije"tyādivacanānusāreṇārcakādhīnatāṃ darśayituṃ, bhagavatprītiviṣayākṛtānāṃ vaikhānasānāṃ taddravyopabhogādiṣu doṣagandhatāpi nāstīti jñāpayituṃ kaimutikanyāyābhiprāyeṇa maddravyaṃ kṣetrabiṃbādītyādinā bhagavadvigrahe vikraye kṛte 'pi doṣo nāstīty uktaṃ.
! DHN[T] 238 statt DHN[D] 54.15-16: kiṃ ca devaddravyopabhogadoṣas sāmānyatvena sarveṣv āpādyate cet tarhi.
! MBh: bhūtair iti me nāsti saṃśayaḥ.
! MBh: māṃ sa bhakṣayate yasmād bhakṣayiṣye tam apy aham / etan māṃsasya māṃsatvam ato budhyasva bhārata.
! MBh: hatvā jantuṃ tato māṃsaṃ tasmād doṣo 'sya bhakṣaṇe.
! MBh: āhartā cānumantā ca viśastā krayavikrayī / saṃskartā copabhoktā ca ghātakāḥ sarva eva te.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 474] Compare ĀS 16.47ab: kiṃ ebhir bahubhir vākyais satyam eva vadāmy ahaṃ.
The buyer kills with wealth, the eater through enjoyment,

children.text: ghātuko vadhabandhābhyām ity eṣa trividho vadhaḥ* //{486}* [MBh 13.116.38]
children.translated_text: the slaughterer through killing and binding — thus this is a threefold killing." [MBh 13.116.38]
"He who wishes to increase his own flesh with the flesh of another —

children.text: nāradaḥ prāha dharmātmā narake sa vipacyate* //{487}*" [MBh 13.117.10]
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s>, the righteous-souled, declared: he is cooked in hell." [MBh 13.117.10]

children.text: kutracid dharmasyāpy adharmaṃ, adharmasyāpi dharmatvañ ca
children.translated_text: In some cases <s>dharma</s> becomes <s>adharma</s>, and <s>adharma</s> becomes <s>dharma</s>

children.text: ityādi vacanaiḥ māṃsabhakṣaṇena narakapatanasmaraṇāt bhagavatprītyarthaṃ kriyamāṇeṣu yajñeṣv api māṃsabhakṣaṇasattvāt yājñikānām*{488}* api narakapatanaṃ sambhavatīti yāgasyāpi tyāgaprasaṅgāt*{489}*.
children.translated_text: From such statements, since falling into hell through meat-eating is remembered, and since meat-eating exists even in sacrifices performed for the Lord's pleasure, the falling into hell of sacrificers too would be possible — which would lead to the absurd consequence that sacrifice itself should be abandoned.
"Therefore, let scripture be your authority in determining what should and should not be done;
having known what is ordained by scriptural injunction, you should perform action here." [MBh 6.38.24]

children.text: iti bhagavadvacanāt śāstroktānāṃ karmaṇāṃ doṣo nāstīti cet. "maddravyopabhogādau doṣo nāstī"ti bhagavatā pratipāditvāt prakṛte 'pi doṣo nāsty eva. "vacanāt pravṛttir vacanān nivṛttir" iti khalu śiṣṭoktiḥ. evaṃ kutracid dharmo 'dharmaḥ adharmaś ca dharmo bhavati.*{491}*
children.translated_text: If it is said: from this word of the Lord, there is no fault in actions ordained by scripture — [then likewise,] since the Lord has established that "there is no fault in enjoying my materials and the like," there is certainly no fault in the present case either. "Activity proceeds from [scriptural] statement, cessation [proceeds] from [scriptural] statement" — this is indeed the declaration of the learned. Thus, in some cases <s>dharma</s> becomes <s>adharma</s>, and <s>adharma</s> becomes <s>dharma</s>.
As for example:
"If by speaking an untruth there would be some protection of the lives of living beings,

children.text: anṛtaṃ tatra satyaṃ syāt satyam atrānṛtaṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: untruth in that case becomes truth, and truth in that case becomes untruth.
In matters of women, in marriages, when the life of cows is at stake,
in the protection of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and in oaths — there is no sin."

children.text: "yadbrāhmaṇaś cābrāhmaṇaś ca praśnam eyātāṃ brāhmaṇāyādhibrūyāt yadbrāhmaṇāyādhyātmane*{493}* 'dhyāha yad brāhmaṇaṃ parāhātmānaṃ parāha tasmād brāhmaṇo na parocyaḥ" ity śrutiś ca.
children.translated_text: "If a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> come to a dispute, one should decide in favor of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. When one decides in favor of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, one decides for oneself; when one speaks for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, one speaks for oneself. Therefore, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not be spoken against." — thus the <s>śruti</s> also [states].

children.text: śrautasūtre ca: "sarva evam abhivādayanti nābhivādayati na juhoty anyatra somāṅgebhyaḥ" ityādi pratipādyate.*{494}*
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Śrautasūtra</s>: "Everyone greets thus, but he does not greet [in return], nor does he offer oblations except at the <s>Soma</s> limbs" — and so forth is set forth.
"In the seizure of all property, [in matters of] wife and courtesan (?), when life is in danger,

children.text: godvijārthe vivāde ca śapathe nāsti pātakam //"
children.translated_text: for the sake of cows and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, in disputes, and in oaths — there is no sin."
Thus the <s>smṛti</s> also [states].

children.text: evaṃ ca śāstroktaprakāreṇa bhagavadarcanaṃ kurvatāṃ taddravyopabhoge*{496}* na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: And thus, for those who perform worship of the Lord in the manner prescribed by scripture, there is no fault in the enjoyment of his materials.

children.text: ! MBh: svamāṃsaṃ paramāṃsair yo vivardhayitum icchati / nāsti kṣudrataras tasmān na nṛśaṃsataro naraḥ.

! DHN[T] 239-240 statt DHN[D] 55.9-12: iti bhagavadvacanāt śāstroktānāṃ doṣo nāstīti cet. "maddravyopabhogādidoṣo nāstī"ti bhagavatā pratipāditvāt "vacanāt pravṛttir vacanān nivṛttir" iti vihitasya doṣo nāsty eva. kutracid dharmo 'dharmaḥ adharmaś ca dharmo bhavati.
! DHN[T] 241 om. pratipādyate und ins. (adharmarūpāyā hiṃsāyā māṃsabhakṣaṇasya ca kratuṣu dharmatvaṃ mahāvrate brahmacāripuṃścalyos saṃparkādikaṃ).

children.translated_text: [Footnote 486] MBh reads: ghātako.
Examination of the definition of being a temple-priest (<s>devalaka</s>)

children.text: kiñca - kiṃ devalakatvaṃ jātiparam, uta karmaparam? jātiparam iti vaktuṃ na śakyate. tathānuktatvāt*{497}*. icchayā kalpitum aśakyatvāc ca.*{498}*
children.translated_text: Furthermore — is the status of being a <s>devalaka</s> (temple-priest) based on birth (<s>jāti</s>) or based on action (<s>karma</s>)? It cannot be said to be based on birth, because it is not stated as such, and because it cannot be arbitrarily fabricated.
The status of <s>devalaka</s> consists precisely in performing unprescribed actions

children.text: atha karmaparam iti cet. vihitakarmaparam, uta avihitakarmaparam?*{499}* vihitakarmaparam iti vaktum aśakyam - śrutismṛtītihāsasūtrapurāṇādīnām*{500}* apramāṇyaprasaṅgāt.
children.translated_text: If then it is based on action — is it based on prescribed action or unprescribed action? It cannot be said to be based on prescribed action — for that would lead to the absurd consequence that <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, and other texts would be invalid.
Because it is not stated as being based on prescribed <s>dharma</s>.
"<s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> are my commands; whoever transgresses them

children.text: ājñāc chedī mama drohī madbhakto 'pi na vaiṣṇavaḥ* //{502}*"
children.translated_text: is a breaker of my command, hostile to me — even if my devotee, he is not a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>."
The faultlessness of worship performed even with another's materials

children.text: iti bhagavadājñābhaṅgadoṣāc ca. evaṃ ca avihitakarmaparam iti hi pariśiṣyate.*{503}*
children.translated_text: And because of the fault of violating the Lord's command. Thus, it remains that [the status of <s>devalaka</s>] is based on unprescribed action.

children.text: nanu - paradravyeṇa kṛtaṃ bhagavadārādhanaṃ kratuvat parārtham eva bhavatīti cet maivam.*{504}*
children.translated_text: Now, if it is objected that worship of the Lord performed with another's materials, like a sacrifice, benefits only the other person — that is not so.
"A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> devoted to the <s>dharma</s> of another falls and goes to a lower destiny;
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> devoted to my rites does not fall downward anywhere."
Thus from the word of the Lord.
In another <s>Purāṇa</s>: "Merely by an act offered to him, by whatever action,

children.text: tuṣṭo dadāti svapadam aho vatsalatā*{506}* hareḥ //" iti.
children.translated_text: he is pleased and gives his own abode — oh, the tender affection of <s>Hari</s>!" Thus.
Furthermore:
The absence of fault in receiving <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fees)
"One should give twenty-one <s>niṣkas</s> (gold coins) as the teacher's fee;

children.text: ṛtvijān tu tadardhaṃ syāt tadardham itarasya ca //"
children.translated_text: for the officiating priests, half of that; and for the remaining [attendants], half of that."
Thus the giving of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is established.

children.text: nanu - "pratigraheṇa viprasya brāhmaṃ tejo vinaśyati* //{508}*" iti manuvacanāt*{509}* [ManuDhŚ 4.186cd]
children.translated_text: Now — since from the words of <s>Manu</s>: "By accepting gifts, the <s>brahmic</s> splendor of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is destroyed," [<s>Manu Dharmaśāstra</s> 4.186cd]

children.text: "pratigraheṇa tejo hi viprāṇāṃ śāmyate" ity ānuśāsanikavacanāc ca pratigraheṇa brahmatejonāśanaṃ smaryate. śrūyate pratigrahe prāyaścittam api. "yo yājayati prati vā gṛhṇāti yājayitvā pratigṛhya vānaśnaṃs tris svādhyāyam adhīyīta trirātraṃ sāvitrīṃ gāyatrīm anvatirecayati varo dakṣiṇā vareṇaiva varaṃ spṛṇoty ātmā hi varaḥ" iti.
children.translated_text: and from the statement in the <s>Ānuśāsanika</s> [parvan]: "By accepting gifts, the splendor of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> is extinguished," the destruction of <s>brahmic</s> splendor through acceptance of gifts is remembered. An expiation for acceptance of gifts is also heard: "He who officiates at a sacrifice or accepts [gifts], having officiated or having accepted, should study the <s>svādhyāya</s> (sacred recitation) three times while fasting; he exceeds the <s>Sāvitrī Gāyatrī</s> by three nights. The boon is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; through the boon alone one touches the boon; for the Self is the boon." Thus.
Therefore, if it is said that there is fault in accepting gifts — no.

children.text: ! Dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 65.13-14 zitiert.
! DHN[T] 243: iti bhagavadājñābhaṅgadoṣāś ca. (tathā vaktum ayuktam). (avihitakarmaparam iti hi pariśiṣyate.)
! ManuDhŚ: pratigraheṇa hy asyāśu brāhmaṃ tejaḥ praśāmyati.

! DHN[T] 244-245 statt DHN[D] 56.21-25: "pratigraheṇa tejo hi viprāṇāṃ śāmyate" na tu? ity ānuśāsanikavacanāc ca pratigraheṇa brahmatejonāśanaṃ, prāyaścittam api śrūyate. "yo yājayati prati vā gṛhṇāti yājayitvā pratigṛhya vānaśnaṃs tris svādhyāyam adhīyīta trirātrīṃ sāvitrīṃ gāyatrīm anvātirecayati varo dakṣiṇā vareṇaiva varaṃ spṛṇoty ātmā hi vara" iti. prāyaścittasmaraṇāc ca doṣāstīti cet.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 497] DHN[T] 242: anuktatvāt.
The power of remembering <s>Hari</s> to grant liberation
"Other <s>dharmas</s>, even when properly performed, do not ultimately save;

children.text: api matkarma viguṇaṃ trāyate mahato bhayāt //
children.translated_text: but even my rite, though defective, saves from great fear.
Even a heap of sinful <s>karma</s> equal to <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mandara</s> [mountains],

children.text: keśavaṃ vaidyam āsādya ab hier noch Telugu vergleichendurvyādhir iva naśyati //
children.translated_text: upon reaching <s>Keśava</s> as physician, perishes like a dire disease.

children.text: nidhisthānaṃ khanan dveṣāt mṛdarthaṃ vāpnuyān nidhim /
children.translated_text: One who digs the site of a treasure out of hatred or for the sake of clay may obtain the treasure;

children.text: ajñaḥ kāmāc ca doṣāc ca smṛtvaivaṃ mokṣabhāktathā //
children.translated_text: [so too] an ignorant person, [even] out of desire or fault, merely by remembering [<s>Hari</s>], attains liberation.
Fire thrown by an enemy or without effort would burn the brushwood;

children.text: katham abhyarcito viṣṇuḥ na dahet sarvakilbiṣam //
children.translated_text: how then would <s>Viṣṇu</s>, when properly worshipped, not burn all sins?

children.text: yathājño vajrakāyas syāt spardhann api sudhāṃ piban /
children.translated_text: Just as an ignorant person becomes diamond-bodied even while competing, [merely] by drinking nectar,

children.text: evaṃ viruddhabhāvo 'pi mucyaty eva hariṃ smaran //" iti
children.translated_text: so too, even one of hostile disposition is liberated merely by remembering <s>Hari</s>." Thus.

children.text: nāradīye: "kṛtāpi dambhahāsyādyair yat sevā tārayej janān /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nāradīya</s> [Purāṇa]: "Even worship performed out of deceit, mockery, and the like delivers people;
it is not fruitless like other rites — who is more compassionate than he? [<s>Nārada Purāṇa</s>]
Even <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) performed toward you through mockery, disrespect, or deceit
gives the status of <s>Indra</s> to people — what need to speak of the <s>sāttvika</s> (pure-minded) ones? [<s>Nārada Purāṇa</s>]
This is the very nature of reality: that remembrance of <s>Hari</s> leads to liberation,
like the sun for the destruction of darkness, like fire for the removal of cold. [<s>Nārada Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: saiṣā harismṛtiṛ daityaṃ krodhād api kṛtā satī /
children.translated_text: This very remembrance of <s>Hari</s>, even when done out of anger toward a <s>daitya</s> (demon),

children.text: ānayet sadgatiṃ vipraṃ sānugaṃ kimu varṇyate // [NāradaP.]
children.translated_text: brings a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> together with his followers to the good destination — what more need be said? [<s>Nārada Purāṇa</s>]
Just as for the gods striving for nectar in the churning of the ocean,
the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree and other fruits came unasked, [<s>Nārada Purāṇa</s>]
so too for those whose minds are set solely on liberation, striving in the remembrance of the Lord,

children.text: bhavanti siddhayo divyāḥ puṇya*{511}* puṇyānubandhi yat //" ityādi [NāradaP]
children.translated_text: divine accomplishments arise — for what is meritorious follows upon merit." And so on. [<s>Nārada Purāṇa</s>]
In that same text: "For the purpose of worshipping the gods, honoring guests, and for the sake of the teacher and servants,

children.text: sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyāt na tu duṣyet svayaṃ tataḥ //" [NāradaP]
children.translated_text: one may accept [gifts] from all sources, and one is not thereby defiled." [<s>Nārada Purāṇa</s>]
[Footnote 511] Read: puṇyaṃ.

children.text: iti ca smaraṇāt. ataḥ śāstroktamārgeṇa bhagavadyajanavidhau pravṛttānāṃ tattatkarmasu dakṣiṇāpratigrahe kṛte 'pi na doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus it is also remembered. Therefore, for those engaged in the rite of worshipping the Lord according to the path prescribed by scripture, even when <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is accepted for the respective rites, there is no fault.
The approval of temple worship in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and other texts
Temple worship (<s>ālayārcanā</s>), distinct from home worship (<s>gṛhārcanā</s>), is seen to be established in the <s>Bhārata</s> and other texts. As follows:

children.text: mahābhārate āśvamedhike "kathaṃ tvam arcanīyo 'sī"ty ādi. [MBh 14 App. 4.1652pr]
children.translated_text: In the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, in the <s>Āśvamedhika</s> [parvan]: "How are you to be worshipped?" and so on. [MBh 14 App. 4.1652pr]
In the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s>, in the sixth chapter:
"He who would construct an enclosure-wall for the purpose of a temple of the deity

children.text: sa tu svargaṃ samāsadya vimānādhipatir bhavet // [Viṣṇudharmottara.P ]
children.translated_text: He indeed, reaching heaven, becomes the lord of a celestial vehicle. // [<s>Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: yas tu devālayasyāgre śilādārubhir eva vā /
children.translated_text: He who, in front of the temple of the god, with stone or wood,

children.text: karoti toraṇaṃ ramyaṃ sa tu svargādhipo bhavet // [Viṣṇudharmottara.P ]
children.translated_text: makes a beautiful gateway — he indeed becomes the lord of heaven. // [<s>Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: yas tu devālayaṃ viṣṇor dāruśailamṛdā tathā /
children.translated_text: He who makes a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whether of wood, stone, or clay,

children.text: iṣṭakākalpitaṃ vāpi kuryāt tasya phalaṃ bahu // [Viṣṇudharmottara.P ]
children.translated_text: or even of bricks — the fruit of that is great. // [<s>Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa</s>]
He who daily performs thousands of <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice) [attains merit equal to]

children.text: prāpnoti maṇḍapaṃ viṣṇoḥ yaḥ kārayati mānavaḥ // [Viṣṇudharmottara.P ]
children.translated_text: the man who has a pavilion for <s>Viṣṇu</s> constructed. // [<s>Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa</s>]
He attains the imperishable world of <s>Keśava</s>.
One should procure the finest stone for an image of great <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // [<s>Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa</s>]
For sixty thousand years he is honored in the heavenly world." Thus. [<s>Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: eteṣāṃ ca prākāratoraṇamaṇḍapavigrahaśilādīṇāṃ gṛhadevatāsvasaṃbhavaḥ śrīvaikhānasasaṃhitāsu pratipāditaḥ. prasaṅgād arcakamahimādīha kathyate.
children.translated_text: The inapplicability of these — enclosure walls, gateways, pavilions, images, stones, etc. — to household deities has been established in the <s>Śrīvaikhānasa Saṃhitās</s>. Incidentally, the greatness of the temple priest (<s>arcaka</s>) and other matters are discussed here.
The greatness of the temple priest (<s>arcaka</s>)
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s> [Purāṇa]: 'That greatly sinful one, resembling Death to living beings,' // [<s>Bṛhannārada Purāṇa</s>]
beginning thus,
'Seeing the beautiful temple of <s>Keśava</s> situated in the midst of a grove,

children.text: chāditaṃ hemakavacaiḥ dṛṣṭvā vyādho mudā yayau // [BṛhannāradaP]
children.translated_text: covered with golden plates, the hunter went with delight.' // [<s>Bṛhannārada Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: harāmy atra suvarṇāni bahūnīti sa niścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I shall steal many golden pieces from here' — having resolved thus,
the hunter, greedy for theft, a lowly person, went to the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // [<s>Bṛhannārada Purāṇa</s>]
There he saw the best of twice-born, peaceful, learned in the meaning of truth,
devoted to the service of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — <s>Udaṅka</s>, a treasure of austerities. // [<s>Bṛhannārada Purāṇa</s>]
One-pointed, compassionate, free from desire, absorbed in meditation,
seeing him, the hunter considered [the priest] an obstacle to his purpose. // [<s>Bṛhannārada Purāṇa</s>]
Intending to steal the wealth belonging to the deity at night,' // [<s>Bṛhannārada Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: ityādināpṛthagālayārcakasadbhāvādikaṃ uktvā svakāryāntarāya bhūtārcakahiṃsāyāṃ pravṛttasya tasya maraṇam api pratipādya.
children.translated_text: Thus, having narrated the existence of a dedicated temple priest and so forth separately, and having also described the death of [the hunter] who had undertaken to harm the priest who was an obstacle to his purpose,
The greatness of the water from the Lord's feet (<s>viṣṇupādodaka</s>)
'<s>Udaṅka</s>, seeing the fallen [hunter], compassionate as he was,
that great sage sprinkled him with the water from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s feet.' //
'By the touch of the water from <s>Hari</s>'s feet, the hunter, freed from all sin,
mounting a divine aerial vehicle, then spoke to the sage:' //
Thus the greatness of the water from the Lord's feet has also been established.
