children.translated_text: Having prescribed the mode of worship — not stated in other <s>Sūtra</s>s — with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as supreme, (the <s>Sūtra</s>) has also prescribed therein the procedure of the five forms, following the <s>Śruti</s> passage: 'That Person is indeed fivefold, of five selves.'

children.text: āghārādiṣu śrautavad eveti pratyakṣasiddham iti pūrvam evoktam. evam anyatrāpi draṣṭavyam.
children.translated_text: That in the <s>Āghāra</s> and other (rites), everything is just as in the <s>Śrauta</s> (procedure) — this is directly established, as already stated. This should be observed in other (contexts) as well.

children.text: śrutimārgānusāritve ko viśeṣa iti cet - ucyate. śrutimūlatve hi prāmāṇyātiśayasambhavaḥ. yathāha

Examination of the Fourth Reason
The <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>Sūtra</s>'s teaching of all rites accompanied by mantras

Now, in order to make known that by the performance of the <s>dharma</s>s prescribed in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>Sūtra</s>, one attains infinite and permanent fruit, noble family-status, and abundance of results, the fourth reason — 'because it teaches all rites accompanied by mantras' — is examined. Thus:

children.text: idānīṃ tāvat vaikhānasasūtroktadharmānuṣṭhānena anantasthiraphalaprāptiḥ satkulīnatvaṃ phalabhūyastvam api bhavatīti jñāpayituṃ "samantrakasarvakriyāpratipādakatvād" iti caturtho hetu nirūpyate. tad yathā:

children.translated_text: Herein, in the <s>Sūtra</s>, in the section on daily obligatory rites, beginning with 'I am <s>Indra</s>, by both [hands]

children.text: atra sūtra*{620}* nityānuṣṭhānavidhau "indro 'ham ubhābhyām" ity ārabhya karaprakṣālanādīni samantrakatvenoktāni. brahmayajñe "ṛtañ ca satyañ ce" ty ādi viśeṣaḥ. puṇyāhe samantrakatvaṃ spaṣṭam. sūtrāntareṣv anuktam aupāsanāgnikuṇdavidhānaṃ pratipāditam. āghāravidhau samantrakatvaṃ siddham. antahome tathaiva. nāndīmukhapūrvakopanayanādiṣu śārīreṣu saṃskāreṣu samantrakatvaṃ pratyakṣam. sthālīpākādiṣu "pūrvavad" ity anena pūrvaṃ vistareṇa pratipāditasyāghāravidheḥ prayogasaukaryārthaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa pratipādanam.
children.translated_text: ,' the washing of hands and other [rites] are prescribed as accompanied by mantras. In the <s>Brahmayajña</s> (daily Vedic recitation), the special feature is 'Truth and right...' etc. In the auspicious ceremony (<s>puṇyāha</s>), the mantra-accompaniment is manifest. The procedure for the <s>Aupāsana</s> fire-pit, which is not taught in other <s>Sūtra</s>s, is set forth [here]. In the <s>Āghāra</s> (oblation) procedure, the mantra-accompaniment is established. In the final oblation (<s>antahoma</s>), likewise. In the bodily <s>saṃskāra</s>s such as <s>Upanayana</s> preceded by <s>Nāndīmukha</s>, the mantra-accompaniment is directly evident. In the <s>Sthālīpāka</s> and other [rites], by the phrase 'as before,' the <s>Āghāra</s> procedure previously taught in detail is concisely indicated for ease of performance.
Mantra-accompaniment in the funeral rites as well

In the funeral rites (<s>aparakriyā</s>) too, there is mantra-accompaniment. Therein, since in some places 'silently' (<s>tūṣṇīm</s>) is stated, one might suspect that there is no mantra-accompaniment — but this objection is self-raised and refuted by showing mantra-accompaniment through another method. Thus it is understood that even where there is no fitness for a mantra in some particular case, there is mantra-accompaniment everywhere in the prescribed subjects. In other <s>Sūtra</s>s, since mantra-accompaniment is not stated even in the prescribed subjects, they do not have all rites accompanied by mantras. Therein, in the funeral rites too, independence from other <s>Sūtra</s>s is observed.

Examination of the Fifth Reason: The <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>Sūtra</s>'s teaching of <s>saṃskāra</s>s beginning with <s>Niṣeka</s> (conception)
Now begins the examination of the fifth reason.

Now, in order to make known that the possession of <s>saṃskāra</s>s beginning with <s>Niṣeka</s>, which is not principally established for adherents of other <s>Sūtra</s>s, is principally established only for this <s>Sūtra</s> — for establishing the supremacy of this <s>Śrīvaikhānasa</s> <s>Sūtra</s> and also the supreme distinction of the practitioners of the <s>dharma</s>s prescribed therein — the fifth reason, 'because it begins with the <s>Niṣeka</s> <s>saṃskāra</s>,' is examined. Thus:

children.translated_text: The primacy of <s>Niṣeka</s> among the <s>saṃskāra</s>s
Beginning with 'Now we shall explain the <s>saṃskāra</s>s beginning with <s>Niṣeka</s> — at the time of seasonal intercourse,'
and ending with 'the grasping of the hand (<s>Pāṇigrahaṇa</s>)' — the bodily <s>saṃskāra</s>s are taught as preceded by the <s>Niṣeka</s> <s>saṃskāra</s>.
The impossibility of birth without <s>Niṣeka</s>

Objection: Since <s>Niṣeka</s> is intermediate between <s>Jātakarma</s> (birth-rite), <s>Upanayana</s>, and marriage, how can its primacy be asserted? Moreover, from <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> passages such as 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was his mouth' and '<s>Dakṣa</s> formerly created beings by mind alone,' where birth without <s>Niṣeka</s> is seen — why is the primacy of <s>Niṣeka</s> asserted? And the primacy of <s>Jātakarma</s> is understood from the <s>Śrībhārata</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śrutismṛtiṣu sṛṣṭikālād ārabhya niṣekād evotpar*{662}* iti śravaṇāt niṣekena vinā utpādanasāmarthyābhāvāc ca niṣekādimatvād ity uktam.*{663}*
children.translated_text: Thus, since in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> it is heard that from the time of creation, birth occurs only from <s>niṣeka</s> (impregnation), and since there is no capacity for generation without <s>niṣeka</s>, it is stated that [the sacraments begin] with <s>niṣeka</s> as the first.
Determination of the meaning of the word <s>niṣeka</s>

children.text: atrāpastambīyā evam āhuḥ. "niṣeko nāma garbhādhānam eva, niṣekagarbhādhānayoḥ paryāyatvāt garbhādhānātirekeṇa niṣekaśabdasyārthāntarāsambhavāc ca.*{664}* garbhādhānaśabdasyārthe vicāryamāṇe 'garbho 'sminn ādhīyate'*{665}* iti vyutpattyā 'indriyaṃ vai garbha'*{666}*
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Āpastambīya</s>s say thus: "<s>Niṣeka</s> is indeed <s>garbhādhāna</s> (impregnation rite), since <s>niṣeka</s> and <s>garbhādhāna</s> are synonymous, and because there is no possibility of a different meaning for the word <s>niṣeka</s> beyond <s>garbhādhāna</s>. When the meaning of the word <s>garbhādhāna</s> is examined, from the etymology 'the embryo is placed in this,' and in accordance with the <s>śruti</s> 'the semen indeed is the embryo,'

children.text: iti śrutyanusāreṇa retassecanam eva garbhādhānam ity avagateḥ*{667}* niṣekāditvam asmākam apy astī"ti.
children.translated_text: Since it is understood that <s>garbhādhāna</s> is precisely the depositing of semen, we too have <s>niṣeka</s> as the first [sacrament]." Thus they say.

children.text: atra baudhāyanīyaḥ pratyavatiṣṭhante. "yad uktaṃ 'niṣeko nāma garbhādhānam niṣekagarbhādhānayoḥ paryāyatvād'; iti - tadasat. niṣekagarbhādhānayoḥ pṛthaktvena pratipādanāt paryāyatvaṃ na ghaṭate. yathā - 'caturthyāṃ snātāyāṃ niśāyām alaṅkṛtya śayane 'bhimantrayate 'viṣṇur yonim'; ity upakramya 'athainām upaiti'; - 'tvāṃ pūṣann ...'*{668}* iti.
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Baudhāyanīya</s>s object: "What was said — '<s>niṣeka</s> is indeed <s>garbhādhāna</s>, since <s>niṣeka</s> and <s>garbhādhāna</s> are synonymous' — that is wrong. Since <s>niṣeka</s> and <s>garbhādhāna</s> are taught separately, synonymity is not tenable. As follows: 'On the fourth [night], when she has bathed, at night, having adorned [her], on the bed he addresses [her with the mantra] "<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the womb";' beginning thus, 'Then he approaches her' — '<s>Tvāṃ Pūṣan</s>...' and so forth."

children.text: evaṃ niṣeka uktaḥ. 'atha garbhādhānavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ. pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre brāhmaṇān annena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ*{669}* vācayitvā atha devayajanaprabhṛtyāgnimukhāt kṛtvā pakvāj juhoti - pravedhase kavaye medhyāye'*{670}*ti. iti garbhādhānam uktam. evaṃ niṣekagarbhādhānayoḥ pṛthaktvena kīrtanāt*{671}* niṣeka eva garbhādhānam iti vaktum ayuktam.
children.translated_text: Thus <s>niṣeka</s> is stated. 'Now we shall explain the procedure of <s>garbhādhāna</s>. On a bright fortnight, under an auspicious constellation, having fed <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s with food, having had them pronounce the auspicious blessing, then from the sacred fire-place beginning with the ritual ground, he makes offerings from cooked food — "To the piercing one, to the wise one, to the pure one."' Thus <s>garbhādhāna</s> is stated. Since <s>niṣeka</s> and <s>garbhādhāna</s> are thus mentioned separately, it is improper to say that <s>niṣeka</s> is simply <s>garbhādhāna</s>.

children.text: kiñca āpastambasūtre*{672}* niṣekapūrvakatvenānuktatvāt catvāriṃśat saṃskāraparigaṇane agṛhītatvāc ca teṣāṃ niṣekādyās saṃskārā na bhavantīti.*{673}*"
children.translated_text: Moreover, since in the <s>Āpastamba</s>-<s>sūtra</s>, <s>niṣeka</s> is not stated as being the first, and since it is not included in the enumeration of the forty <s>saṃskāra</s>s (sacraments), the <s>saṃskāra</s>s beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> do not belong to them."

DHN[D] 83.5.

children.text: atra āpastambīyā ūcuḥ. "yady asmākaṃ niṣekādyāḥ saṃskārā na bhavantīty ucyate tarhi yuṣmākam api tathaiva, bhavat sūtre 'pi*{674}* >yato etad dhutaḥ prahutaḥ*{675}* āhutaḥ śūlagavo baliharaṇaṃ pratyavarohaṇam aṣṭakā pārvaṇahoma itī
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Āpastambīya</s>s said: "If it is said that the <s>saṃskāra</s>s beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> do not belong to us, then the same applies to you as well, since in your <s>sūtra</s> also, beginning with 'from this the offering, the secondary offering, the oblation, the spitted ox, the bringing of tribute, the descent, the <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, the <s>pārvaṇa</s> fire-offering'

children.text: <*{676}*ty ārabhya vivāhādyevoktam - na tu niṣekāditvena. kiñca sūtropakrame*{677}* saṃskāragaṇanāyām api niṣekas tu saṃskāratvena vā śabdamātreṇa vā na pratipāditaḥ. kiñca >caturyyāṃ snātāyom<*{678}* ityādinā pṛthaktvena vidhīyamānasya garbhādhānasya lakṣaṇapratipādanābhāvāt viśiṣya kālanirūpaṇābhāvāc ca.*{679}*>
children.translated_text: and so forth, only the marriage rite and the like are stated — but not as beginning with <s>niṣeka</s>. Moreover, in the enumeration of <s>saṃskāra</s>s at the beginning of the <s>sūtra</s>, <s>niṣeka</s> is not established either as a <s>saṃskāra</s> or even by mere word. Furthermore, since the definition and specific time-determination of <s>garbhādhāna</s>, which is prescribed separately by 'on the fourth [night] when she has bathed,' are not provided.
Only <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s have the <s>saṃskāra</s>s beginning with <s>niṣeka</s>

children.text: (vaikhānase sūtre eva niṣekāditvena uktatvāc ca vaikhānasānām niṣekāditvam),
children.translated_text: (Since it is stated as beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> only in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>niṣeka</s>-first status belongs to <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s),

children.text: āvayoḥ*{680}* ubhayor api niṣekādyās saṃskārā na bhavanti iti. ayam eva siddhāntaḥ.*{681}*
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃskāra</s>s beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> do not belong to either of us two. This indeed is the established conclusion.
Others have <s>saṃskāra</s>s beginning with <s>garbhādhāna</s>

children.text: tathā ca: "niṣekādyāḥ śmaśānāntās teṣāṃ vai mantrataḥ kriyāḥ / [YājñavalkyaDhŚ 1.10cd]
children.translated_text: And accordingly: "Beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> and ending with the cremation ground, for them the rites are performed with <s>mantra</s>s. [<s>Yājñavalkya Dharmaśāstra</s> 1.10cd]
<s>Garbhādhāna</s> is at the fertile period; <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for a male child) is before the quickening." [<s>Yājñavalkya Dharmaśāstra</s> 1.11ab]

children.text: iti yājñavalkyoktau teṣām iti śabdena "mukhye sambhavaty amukhyakalpanāyogād" iti nyāyena mukhyatvena śrīvaikhānasasūtre eva niṣekāditvasya vidyamānatvāt vaikhānasā eva parāmṛśyante iti - teṣām eva niṣekāditvam, itareṣāṃ niṣekāditvaṃ na sambhavati. api tu garbhādhānāditvam eva. ayam eva yājñavalkyābhiprāyaḥ.*{683}*
children.translated_text: In this statement of <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, by the word 'their,' since by the principle 'when a primary meaning is possible, a secondary interpretation is not warranted,' and since <s>niṣeka</s>-first status exists primarily only in the sacred <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>sūtra</s>, only the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s are referred to — the <s>niṣeka</s>-first status belongs to them alone. <s>Niṣeka</s>-first status is not possible for others; rather, they have only <s>garbhādhāna</s>-first status. This indeed is the intended meaning of <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: athocyete*{684}*. garbhādhānalakṣaṇam anuktaṃ viśiṣya kālaś cānukta iti yad uktam tatrocyate - sarveṣāṃ kāraṇabhūtena paramācāryeṇa vikhanasā praṇīte śrīvaikhānasasūtre "atha gṛhītagarbhāliṅgāni śarīrāṭopaḥ sakthisīdanaṃ dveṣo bhartur arucir āhāre lālāprakopaḥ kharatā vācaḥ sphuraṇaṃ yoner iti garbhasya daivānubandhaṃ jñātvā āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye punnāmni śubhe nakṣatre"*{685}* ityādinā garbhādhānalakṣaṇakālayor api vaikhānasasūtre pratipāditvāt:*{686}*
children.translated_text: Now it is said: What was stated — that the definition of <s>garbhādhāna</s> is not given and its specific time is not stated — to that it is replied: In the sacred <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>sūtra</s> composed by <s>Vikhanasa</s>, the supreme teacher who is the cause of all, beginning with "Now the signs of a conceived embryo: bodily swelling, weakness of the thighs, aversion, displeasure toward the husband, dislike of food, excess of saliva, harshness of speech, trembling of the womb — having ascertained the divine connection of the embryo, during the bright fortnight, under an auspicious male-named constellation," both the definition and time of <s>garbhādhāna</s> are taught in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>sūtra</s>.
"Whatever <s>dharma</s> is declared in the <s>Veda</s>, in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text: sarvaiḥ sa dharmo 'nuṣṭheyo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā* //{687}*"
children.translated_text: That <s>dharma</s> is to be practiced by all; no deliberation is needed here."

children.text: iti bhṛguṇoktatvāt "anuktam*{688}* anyato grāhyam" iti nyāyāt vikhanasaḥ*{689}* ācāryatvena
children.translated_text: Since this was stated by <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and by the principle 'what is not stated should be taken from elsewhere,' and since <s>Vikhanasa</s>'s status as the teacher

children.text: bhāratādiṣu pratipāditavyāc ca "anuktāṃśeṣu vaikhānasoktaprakāreṇa asmābhir api kartuṃ yuktam" iti. etad eva yuktataram. Tathāhi:*{690}*
children.translated_text: is established in the <s>Bhārata</s> and other texts, "it is proper for us too to perform according to the procedure stated in that <s>sūtra</s> in matters not stated [in our own]." This indeed is more appropriate. For:

children.text: ! Bezug auf den ersten Satz im BaudhGṛS (1.1.1): yatho etad dhutaḥ prahuta āhutaś śūlagavo baliharaṇaṃ pratyavarohaṇam aṣṭakāhoma iti pākayajñasaṃsthā iti. S.a. DHN[D] 85.15.
! Lies: caturthyāṃ snātāyām. Bezug auf BaudhGṛS 1.7.37ff.; s.a. DHN[D] 82.18-19.
! DHN[T] 403 statt DHN[D] 83.7-8: niṣekāditvena śrīvaikhānase sūtre uktatvāc ca ubhayor api niṣekādyās saṃskārā na bhavanti.
! Dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 85.3-4 zitiert.

! DHN[T] 404 statt DHN[D] 83.11-14: yājñavalkyena teṣām ity uktatvāt "mukhye sambhavaty amukhyakalpa nāyogād" iti nyāyena mukhyatvena śrīvaikhānasasūtre vidyamānatvāc ca itareṣāṃ niṣekāditvaṃ na sambhavati.

! Bezug auf VaikhSmS 3.10: atha gṛhītagarbhāliṅgāni śarīrāṭopaḥ sakthisīdanaṃ dveṣo bhartur arūcirāhāro lālāprakopaḥ kharatā vācaḥ spuraṇaṃ yoner iti garbhasya daivānubandhaṃ jñātvāpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye puṃnāmni śubhe nakṣatra ājyenāghāraṃ hutvā tāṃ maṅgalayuktām upaveśya pariṣicya dhātādi pañca vāruṇaṃ mūlahomaṃ sviṣṭākāraṃ ca hutvā vṛṣo 'sīti yavān dadāti.

! DHN[T] 405 statt DHN[D] 83.15-20: athocyate. garbhādhānalakṣaṇam apy anuktaṃ viśiṣya kālaś cānukta iti tat sarveṣāṃ kāraṇabhūtena paramācāryeṇa vikhanasā praṇīte vaikhānasasūtre "atha gṛhītagarbhāliṅgāni śarīrāṭopaḥ sakthisīdanaṃ dveṣā bhartur arucir āhāro lālāprakopaḥ kharatā vācaḥ sphuraṇaṃ yoner iti garbhasya daivānubandhaṃ jñātvāpūryamāṇapakṣe punnāmni śubhe nakṣatre" ityādinā garbhādhānalakṣaṇakālayor api pratipāditvāt.
! DHN[T] 406: vicāraṇeti; dieser Vers ist als "Purātantra" zitiert in DHN[D] 35.2-3 und als "Ānandasaṃhitā" (ĀS 4.49) zitiert in DHN[D] 14.11-12.
! DHN[T] 407: bhārate: "vaikhānasavikhanasācārye"ty ādi statt etad eva yuktataram. tathāhi.

children.translated_text: The non-synonymity of <s>niṣeka</s> and <s>garbhādhāna</s>

children.text: āpastambādīnām ācāryeṇa bodhāyanena svaśiṣyān prati*{691}* "athātra pākayajñānāṃ prāyaścittir" ity ārabhya "vyāhṛtīnāṃ prayoge ayathākṛtaṃ yathākṛtaṃ*{692}* bhavatīty ācāryā bruvate. tatrāpy udāharanti"*{693}* iti, "caturthīprabhṛtyā ṣoḍaśīm uttarām uttarām*{694}* upaiti. prajāniḥśreyasam ṛtugamanam ity ācāryāḥ. sarvāṇy upagamanāni mantravanti bhavantīti bodhāyanaḥ. yac cādau yac cartāv iti śālīkir"*{695}* iti - "athāsyātithayo bhavanti guros samānavṛttir vaikhānasaḥ snātako rājā vā dharmayuktaḥ. teṣām abhyutthāyāsanaṃ pādyam arhaṇam arghyaṃ vā prajuñjīta"*{696}* iti - "ekam agnihotraṃ sāyam upakramaṃ prātar apavargam ācāryā bruvate tatrodāharanti" iti, "vaikhānasānāṃ na druhyet" ityādi sūtreṣu "ācāryā bruvate" iti nirdiṣṭaḥ ācāryaḥ vaikhānasa eveti vaktuṃ yuktam*{697}* - manvādīnāṃ śārīrasaṃskāravaktṛtvābhāvāt, bodhāyanena pratipāditasya vaikhānasasūtre vidyamānatvāt,
children.translated_text: <s>Baudhāyana</s>, the teacher of the <s>Āpastambīya</s>s and others, addressing his own disciples, beginning with "Now here is the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) for the <s>pākayajña</s>s (domestic sacrifices)," and "In the use of the <s>vyāhṛti</s>s (sacred utterances), what was done improperly becomes properly done, say the teachers. And thereto they cite examples" — and "From the fourth [night] onwards up to the sixteenth, each succeeding night, he approaches her. Going to the wife during her fertile period is for the welfare of progeny, say the teachers. All approaches should be accompanied by <s>mantra</s>s, says <s>Baudhāyana</s>. What is at the beginning and what is at the proper time, says <s>Śālīki</s>" — and "Now his guests are: one of equal conduct with the teacher, the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, the <s>snātaka</s> (graduated student), or a king engaged in <s>dharma</s>. For them, having risen, one should offer a seat, foot-water, and an honorable reception or <s>arghya</s>" — and "The <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-offering), one, beginning in the evening, ending in the morning, say the teachers; thereto they cite" — in these <s>sūtra</s>s including "one should not harm the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s" and so forth, it is proper to say that the teacher referred to by "the teachers say" is indeed the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> — since <s>Manu</s> and others do not teach the bodily <s>saṃskāra</s>s, and since what <s>Baudhāyana</s> teaches is found in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> <s>sūtra</s>,
Since "one of equal conduct with the teacher is the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>" is stated by <s>Baudhāyana</s> himself, and since "<s>Vikhanasa</s> is the teacher."

children.text: bhārate pratipāditvāc ca. tathā ca sarveṣāṃ kāraṇabhūtena vikhanasā praṇītatvāt tatsūtroktaprakāreṇa sarvaiḥ*{700}* kartuṃ yuktam eva. kiñca araṇyādipātralakṣaṇam api tatraiva pratipāditam.
children.translated_text: And since this is established in the <s>Bhārata</s> and other texts. Thus, since all was composed by <s>Vikhanasa</s> who is the cause of all, it is indeed proper for all to perform according to the procedure stated in that <s>sūtra</s>. Moreover, the definition of the vessel for the <s>āraṇya</s> (forest) and other [rites] is also taught therein.

children.text: anye 'py āhuḥ. "asmākam api niṣekāditvaṃ*{701}* samānam" iti. tad apy asat.
children.translated_text: Others also say: "We too have <s>niṣeka</s>-first status equally." That too is wrong.

children.text: garbhādhānaśabdasyārthe vicāryamāṇe "yoniṃ praviśad indriyaṃ garbho jarāyuṇā vṛta"*{702}* iti
children.translated_text: When the meaning of the word <s>garbhādhāna</s> is examined, "the semen enters the womb, the embryo is covered by the membrane" —

children.text: pramāṇena garbhagole praviṣṭasya retasa eva garbhaśabdavācyatvam avagamyate. na tv itarasya kevala retasaḥ. tathā - "āsiñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu" iti niṣekakriyānantarabhāvitvāt garbhādhānasya, niṣekasya tu pratyārtavaṃ kartuṃ vyogyatāsambhavāt adhṛtaretasaḥ srāvadoṣaprasaṅgāt śrutismṛtivirodhāt pratyakṣavirodhāṅ ca niṣeka eva garbhādhānam iti vaktum ayuktam.*{703}*
children.translated_text: By this authority it is understood that only semen that has entered the embryonic sac is denoted by the word <s>garbha</s> (embryo), not mere semen alone. Furthermore, since the <s>garbhādhāna</s> rite follows immediately after the <s>niṣeka</s> act, as shown by "May <s>Prajāpati</s> pour in, may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place the embryo," and since <s>niṣeka</s> cannot properly be performed at every menstrual period, and because of the fault of emission of unreceived semen, and because of contradiction with <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, and because of contradiction with direct perception — it is improper to say that <s>niṣeka</s> is simply <s>garbhādhāna</s>.
The superiority of those whose first <s>saṃskāra</s> is <s>niṣeka</s>

children.text: atha niṣekāditve ko viśeṣa iti cet - ucyate*{704}*. niṣekādikriyāvatām eva
children.translated_text: Now, if it be asked what distinction there is in having <s>niṣeka</s> as the first — it is replied: Only those who have the rites beginning with <s>niṣeka</s>

children.text: śrotriyatvaṃ dharmaśāstrādhikāritvaṃ brahmaśarīritvañ*{705}* ca bodhāyanādibhir uktam. yathā:
children.translated_text: are declared by <s>Baudhāyana</s> and others to have the status of <s>śrotriya</s> (learned in <s>Veda</s>), authority in <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>, and the status of being embodied by <s>Brahman</s>. As follows:
"Those sanctified according to the proper rites with <s>mantra</s>s at the <s>niṣeka</s>, the embryonic <s>saṃskāra</s>, and the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite) ceremonies,
Having completed [all rites] from the <s>vrata</s> (vow) until its conclusion,

children.text: śrotriyā iti vijñeyāḥ śākhāpārāś ca ye dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: Should be known as <s>śrotriya</s>s — those <s>dvija</s>s (twice-born) who have mastered their <s>Vedic</s> branch;

children.text: vidhivat gṛhyate pāṇim ṛtau cīrṇavratās tu te*{706}* //
children.translated_text: Whose hand is taken according to the proper rites, and who have completed their vows during the fertile period,

children.text: !{691}! DHN[T] 407 bodhāyanaḥ statt āpastambādīnām ācāryeṇa bodhāyanena svaśiṣyān prati.

! Bezug auf BaudhGṛS 4.4.1-4: atha pākayajñānāṃ prāyaścittiḥ (1). tad yathā: dravyahavir mantrakarmādīnām atipannaskannabhinnabhagnanaṣṭaduṣṭaviparītadagdhāśṛtyanikṛtānām anāmnā teṣu juhuyāt: 'mano jyotiḥ, ayāś cāgne, yadāsmin karmāṇi, svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ'; iti. vyāhṛtibhiś ca (2). vyāhṛtīnāṃ prayoge yathākṛtaṃ yathāvad bhavatīty ācārya bruvate (3). tatrodāharanti: bhūr ity ṛco bhuva iti yajuṃṣi suvar iti sāmāni (4).

! Bezug auf BaudhGṛS 1.7.45-48: sa evam eva caturthīprabhṛtyā ṣoḍaśīm uttarām uttarāṃ yaugmām upaiti (45). prajāniśśreyasam ṛtugamanam ity ācāryāḥ (46). sarvāṇy upagamanāni mantravanti bhavantīti bodhāyanaḥ (47). yac cādau yac cartāv iti śālikiḥ (48).

! Bezug auf BaudhGṛS 2.9.17-18: athāsmā atithir bhavati guros samānavṛttir vaikhānaso vā gṛhastho vānaprasthaḥ parivrājako gataśrīs snātako rājā vā dharmayuktaḥ (17). teṣām abhyutthāyāsanaṃ pādyam arhaṇam arghyaṃ vā prayuñīta (18); s.a. DHN[D] 10.6.

! DHN[T] 408: ityādibhir āpastambādīnām ācāryeṇa bodhāyanena svaśiṣyān "pratyācāryā bruvata" iti vaktum yuktatvāt statt ityādi sūtreṣu "ācāryā bruvate" iti nirdiṣṭaḥ ācāryaḥ vaikhānasa eveti vaktuṃ yuktam.

! DHN[T] 411-412 statt DHN[D] 84.16-20: garbhagole praviṣṭasya retasa eva garbhaśabdavācyatvam na tv itarasya tathā "āsiñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu" iti niṣekakriyāntarbhāvitvāt pratyārtavaṃ kartavyayogyatā sambhavāt adhṛtaretasaḥ srāvadoṣaprasaṅgāc chrutismṛtivirodhāt pratyakṣavirodhāṅ ca niṣeka eva garbhādhānam iti vaktum ayuktam.
! DHN[T] 412: niṣekādir vā astu ko viśeṣaḥ iti cet statt atha niṣekāditve ko viśeṣa iti cet - ucyate.

children.translated_text: [Editorial note: DHN[T] 407 reads 'Baudhāyana' instead of 'by Baudhāyana, the teacher of the Āpastambīyas and others, to his own students.']
Through union accompanied by <s>mantra</s>s they placed the embryo in a <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (brāhmaṇa woman);
The auspicious rites beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> and ending at the cremation ground are dependent on the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>." Thus.

children.text: yājñavalkya: "niṣekādyāḥ*{708}* śmaśānāntāḥ teṣāṃ vai mantrataḥ kriyāḥ / [YājñavalkyaDhŚ 1.10cd]
children.translated_text: <s>Yājñavalkya</s>: "Beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> and ending at the cremation ground, for them the rites are performed with <s>mantra</s>s; [<s>Yājñavalkya Dharmaśāstra</s> 1.10cd]

children.text: garbhādhānam ṛtau puṃsassavanaṃ spandanāt purā* //{709}*" iti [YājñavalkyaDhŚ 1.11ab]
children.translated_text: <s>Garbhādhāna</s> is at the fertile period; <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for a male child) is before the quickening." [<s>Yājñavalkya Dharmaśāstra</s> 1.11ab]
<s>Manu</s>: "He for whom the rites beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> and ending at the cremation ground are declared with <s>mantra</s>s,

children.text: tasya śāstre 'dhikāro 'smin jñeyo nānyasya kasyacit //" iti [ManuDhŚ 2.16]
children.translated_text: His authority in this teaching is to be known, and of no one else." [<s>Manu Dharmaśāstra</s> 2.16]

children.text: atra manuvākye "yasya - tasya - kasyacit" ityādi śabdānāṃ vaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt "sarveṣāṃ niṣekāditvaṃ samānam" iti vaktum ayuktam.
children.translated_text: In this statement of <s>Manu</s>, since there would be meaninglessness of the words 'whose — his — of anyone else' and so forth, it is improper to say 'everyone equally has <s>niṣeka</s>-first status.'

children.text: āśvamedhike bhagavān: "vaidikaiḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyaiḥ niṣekādir dvijanmanām* /{711}*
children.translated_text: In the <s>Aśvamedha</s> [section], the Blessed Lord says: "Through meritorious <s>Vedic</s> rites, beginning with <s>niṣeka</s>, for the twice-born,

children.text: kāryaḥ śarīrasaṃskāraḥ pāvanaḥ pretya ceha ca // [MB.h 14, App. 4.2513]
children.translated_text: The bodily <s>saṃskāra</s> (purificatory rite) should be performed, which is sanctifying both here and hereafter. [MBh 14, App. 4.2513]

Through the prenatal fire-offerings, the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite), the naming ceremony, the <s>cūḍā</s> (tonsure), and the <s>upanayana</s> (investiture with sacred thread), [MBh 14, App. 4.2514]

children.text: svādhyāyaiś ca tapobhiś ca*{713}* vivāhasnātakavrataiḥ // [MBh 14, App. 4.2515]
children.translated_text: And through self-study and austerities, through the marriage and <s>snātaka</s> (graduation) vows. [MBh 14, App. 4.2515]

children.text: mahāyajñaiś ca yajñaiś ca brāhmīyaṃ kriyate tanuḥ /" iti [MBh 14, App. 4.2516]
children.translated_text: 'Through the great sacrifices and [other] sacrifices, a body fit for <s>Brahman</s> is fashioned.' // [<s>Mahābhārata</s> 14, App. 4.2516]
Thus it should be understood elsewhere also.

children.text: bodhāyanena "yato etad dhutam*{714}*" ityādinā sūtrādau vivāhapūrvakatvenoktam.
children.translated_text: By <s>Bodhāyana</s>, beginning with 'from this which is offered' and so forth, marriage is stated as a prerequisite at the beginning of the <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: āpastambena "atha karmāṇy ācārādyāni gṛhyante*{715}*" ity ārabhya "upanayanaṃ vyākhyāsyāma" iti. bhāradvājasatyāṣāḍhābhyām āśvalāyanena ca "uktāni vaitānikānī"*{716}*ty ārabhya vaiśvadevapūrvakatvena. drāhyāyaṇena*{717}* "athāto gṛhyakarmāṇi, udagayanapūrvapakṣa"*{718}* ity ārabhya ācārāditvena. kātyāyanaś ca "athāto gṛhyasthālīpākānāṃ karme"*{719}*ty ārabhya pratipāditavān. "atha niṣekādisaṃskārān vyākhyāsyāma"*{720}* ity ārabhya niṣekapūrvakatvena bhagavatā vikhanasaiva*{721}* pratipāditam.
children.translated_text: By <s>Āpastamba</s>, beginning with 'Now the ritual actions beginning with proper conduct are taken up,' [and proceeding to] 'We shall expound the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation).' By <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, <s>Satyāṣāḍha</s>, and <s>Āśvalāyana</s> as well...

children.text: evaṃ ca niṣekapūrvakatvenoktatvād*{722}* asya sarvasūtrottamatvaṃ etatsūtroktadharmānuṣṭhānenaiva tatsūtriṇāṃ sarvotkṛṣṭatvañ copapadyate iti śrutismṛtipurāṇādimukhena pratipāditam iti nirūpitaḥ pañcamo hetuḥ.
children.translated_text: And thus, since it is stated as having the rite of conception (<s>niṣeka</s>) as a prerequisite, the supremacy of this [<s>Vaikhānasa</s>] <s>sūtra</s> over all other <s>sūtras</s>, and the supreme excellence of those who follow that <s>sūtra</s> through the practice of the <s>dharmas</s> taught in it, is established...
Thus concludes the examination of the fifth reason.

children.text: ! Dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 83.9-10 zitiert; DHN[T] 413 ins. (bahir iti).
! DHN[T] 413 mit ManuDhŚ: mantrair yasyodito vidhiḥ.
! Bezug auf BaudhGṛS 1.1.1, auch in DHN[D] 83.1-3 zitiert (s.o.). DHN[T] 414 : dhuta.
! Bezug auf ĀśvalāyanaGṛS 1.1.1: uktāni vaitānikāni gṛhyāni vakṣyāmaḥ.

children.translated_text: {707} DHN[T] 413: 'mantravatsaṃprayoge tau.'
Examination of the Sixth Reason
The <s>Vaikhānasa-sūtra</s>'s teaching of the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacramental rites)
Now, the examination of the sixth reason.

children.text: athedānīṃ śrīvaikhānasasūtroktadharmānuṣṭhātṝṇām eva sarvebhyaḥ śreṣṭhamatvaṃ sūtrāntareṣv anuktaṃ śrutisiddhāṣṭādaśasaṃskāravatvaṃ kriyābāhulyañ ca sambhavatīti jñāpayituṃ "aṣṭādaśasaṃskārapratipādakatvād" iti ṣaṣṭho hetur nirūpyate. tathā hi:
children.translated_text: Now, the supreme status of those who practice the <s>dharmas</s> taught in the <s>Śrī Vaikhānasa-sūtra</s> over all others, [established by] the abundance of ritual actions that possess the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> established in <s>śruti</s>, which are not taught in other <s>sūtras</s>...

children.text: "atha niṣekādisaṃskārān vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ṛtusaṅgamana-garbādhāna-puṃsavana-sīmanta-viṣṇubali-jātakarmotthāna-nāmakaraṇānnaprāśana-pravāsāgamana-piṇḍavardhana-caulopanayana-pārāyaṇa-vratabandhavisargopākarma-samāvartana-pāṇigrahaṇānīty aṣṭādaśa-saṃskārāś śārīrāḥ"*{723}* iti aṣṭādaśasaṃskārāḥ sūtre pratipāditāḥ. ete ca
children.translated_text: 'Now we shall expound the <s>saṃskāras</s> beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> (conception): seasonal intercourse, impregnation, <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for a male child), <s>sīmanta</s> (parting of the hair), <s>Viṣṇubali</s> (offering to <s>Viṣṇu</s>), birth rites, arising, name-giving, first feeding, return from travel...'
Examination of the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>: 'the inferior action spoken of as eighteen'

children.text: śrutisiddhāḥ. yathā muṇḍopaniṣadi - "plavā hy ete adṛḍhā yajñarūpā aṣṭādaśoktam avaraṃ yeṣu karma. etac chreyo ye 'bhinandanti mūḍhā jarāmṛtyuṃ te punar evāpi yanti"*{724}* iti.
children.translated_text: They are established in <s>śruti</s>. As in the <s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s>: 'These are indeed unsteady boats in the form of sacrifices, in which the action spoken of as eighteen is inferior. Those deluded ones who celebrate this as the highest -- they again undergo old age and death...'

children.text: atra kecid evam ūcuḥ: "yajñasya rtvijaṣ ṣoḍaśa sadasyassaptadaśaḥ yajamāno 'ṣṭādaśaḥ"
children.translated_text: Here some have said: 'The sixteen <s>ṛtvij</s> (priests) of the sacrifice, the seventeenth being the assessor (<s>sadasya</s>), and the eighteenth being the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>).'

children.text: iti śrutyanusāreṇa "aṣṭādaśoktam avaraṃ yeṣu karme"*{725}*ty atra yajamānādaya eva vivakṣitā iti. tad asat. "aṣṭādaśoktam avaraṃ karmayeṣu" ity uktatvāt. ṛtvigyajamānādayo hi yāgakartāraḥ na tu karma. "yeṣu" ity asya padasya yeṣu sūtreṣv ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: According to this <s>śruti</s>, in 'the inferior action spoken of as eighteen,' the <s>yajamāna</s> and the rest alone are intended. That is wrong. [The phrase] 'the inferior action in which eighteen is spoken of'...

children.text: 'avaraṃ karma'; jātakādayaḥ, smārtakarmatvāt. ātmaguṇarahitā yāgadayaḥ jātakarmādayaś ca. 'adṛḍhāḥ plavāḥ'; saṃsārottārakā na bhavanti. tathā ca atra adṛḍhaplavatvena ninditā saṃskārāḥ yāgādayaś ca ātmaguṇarahitā eva vivakṣitāḥ. tat sahitānāṃ teṣāṃ mokṣasādhakatvam. yathā:
children.translated_text: 'Inferior action' -- the birth rites and the like, because they are <s>smārta</s> (based on <s>smṛti</s>) ritual actions. Sacrifices and the like, and birth rites and the like, that are devoid of the qualities of the self. 'Unsteady boats' -- they do not carry one across <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore...
The binding nature of <s>saṃskāras</s> devoid of the qualities of the self

children.text: gautamadharme: "yasya tu khalu catvāriṃśatsaṃskārā na cāṣṭāvātmaguṇāḥ na sa brahmaṇas sāyujyaṃ sālokyañ ca gacchati. yasya khalu catvāriṃśatsaṃskārāṇām ekadeśo py aṣṭāv ātmaṇāḥ atha sa brahmaṇas sāyujyaṃ sālokyañ ca gacchati gacchatī"*{726}*ti.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Gautama-dharma</s> [-<s>sūtra</s>]: 'But he who possesses the forty <s>saṃskāras</s> yet lacks the eight qualities of the self -- he does not attain <s>sāyujya</s> (union) and <s>sālokya</s> (co-residence) with <s>Brahman</s>. But he who possesses the forty...'
The characteristics of the eight qualities of the self

children.text: 'aṣṭāv ātmaguṇāḥ': "dayā samastabhūteṣu kṣāntir anasūyā śaucam anāyāso maṅgalyam akārpaṇyam aspṛhe"*{727}* ti. tallakṣaṇāni tu:
children.translated_text: 'The eight qualities of the self': 'Compassion (<s>dayā</s>) toward all beings, forbearance (<s>kṣānti</s>), absence of envy (<s>anasūyā</s>), purity (<s>śauca</s>), freedom from exertion (<s>anāyāsa</s>), auspiciousness (<s>maṅgalya</s>), absence of miserliness (<s>akārpaṇya</s>), and absence of craving (<s>aspṛhā</s>).' Their definitions are:
Definition of compassion (<s>dayā</s>)

children.text: "abandhau bandhuvarge vā mitre dveṣṭari vā tathā /
children.translated_text: 'Whether toward one who is not a relative, or toward a group of kinsmen, or toward a friend, or toward an enemy,

children.text: āpanne rakṣaṇaṃ yat tu dayaiṣā parikīrtitā //
children.translated_text: Protection of one who is in distress -- this is declared to be compassion (<s>dayā</s>).

children.text: ! MuṇḍakaU 1.2.7: plavā hy ete adṛḍhā yajñarūpā aṣṭādaśoktam avaraṃ yeṣu karma. etac chreyo ye 'bhinandanti mūḍhā jarāmṛtyuṃ te punar evāpiyanti.

! Bezug auf GautamaDhS 1.8.25(8.24): yasyaite catvāriṃśatsaṃskārā na caāṣṭāv ātmaguṇā na sa brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyaṃ sālokyaṃ gacchati / und GautamaDhS 1.8.26(8.25): yasya tu khalu catvāriṃśataṃskārāṇām ekadeśo 'py aṣṭāv ātmaguṇā atha sa brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyaṃ sālokyaṃ ca gacchati.
! Bezug auf GautamaDhS 1.8.24(8.23): dayā sarvabhūteṣu kṣāntir anasūyā śaucam anāyāso maṅgalam akārpaṇyam aspṛheti.

children.translated_text: {723} <s>Vaikhānasa-smārta-sūtra</s> 1.1.
Definition of forbearance (<s>kṣamā</s>)

children.text: bāhye vā 'bhyantare vāpi duḥkha utpādite paraiḥ /
children.translated_text: When suffering is caused by others, whether external or internal,

children.text: na prakupyati no hanti sā kṣamā parikīrtitā //
children.translated_text: One who neither becomes angry nor retaliates -- that is declared to be forbearance (<s>kṣamā</s>).
Definition of absence of envy (<s>anasūyā</s>)

children.text: saguṇān guṇi*{728}* no hanti (?) stauti mandaguṇān api /
children.translated_text: One who does not disparage (?) the virtuous who possess qualities, and praises even those of lesser qualities,
Who does not delight in the faults of others -- that is proclaimed as absence of envy (<s>anasūyā</s>).
Definition of purity (<s>śauca</s>)
Avoidance of forbidden food, association only with the blameless,

children.text: svadharme ca vyavasthānaṃ śaucam etad udāhṛtam //
children.translated_text: And firm establishment in one's own <s>dharma</s> -- this is declared to be purity (<s>śauca</s>).
Definition of freedom from exertion (<s>anāyāsa</s>)
An action by which the body is tormented, even if it is very meritorious,
Should by no means be performed -- this is called freedom from [excessive] exertion (<s>anāyāsa</s>).
Definition of auspiciousness (<s>maṅgalya</s>)
Always engaging in praiseworthy conduct and abandoning what is not praiseworthy --

children.text: etad dhi maṅgalaṃ proktam ṛṣibhis tattvadarśibhiḥ //
children.translated_text: This indeed is declared to be auspiciousness (<s>maṅgala</s>) by the <s>ṛṣis</s> who perceive the truth.
Definition of absence of miserliness (<s>akārpaṇya</s>)
One should give, even if only a little, with an inner self that is not mean-spirited,
Something every day -- this is called absence of miserliness (<s>akārpaṇya</s>).
Definition of absence of craving (<s>aspṛhā</s>)
One should be content with wealth that has come of its own accord,
And should not covet the possessions of others -- this is declared to be absence of craving (<s>aspṛhā</s>).'
This was stated as a digression. We return to the main topic.
The <s>sāttvika</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s> <s>Purāṇas</s>

children.text: atha aṣṭādaśasmṛtyuktāni aṣṭādaśapurāṇeṣūktānīti vā muṇḍakaśrutyartho 'stu iti cet. tad apy asat. smṛtipurāṇādiṣu aṣṭādaśakarmeti viśiṣyānuktatvāt.
children.translated_text: Now, if it be said that the meaning of the <s>Muṇḍaka</s> <s>śruti</s> is 'those taught in the eighteen <s>smṛtis</s>' or 'those taught in the eighteen <s>Purāṇas</s>' -- that too is wrong. Because in the <s>smṛtis</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the like, the specific designation 'eighteen ritual actions' is not taught...

children.text: atra *{729}* "aṣṭādaśoktam avaraṃ karma yeṣv"*{730}* iti sāmānyenoktatvāt tatroktānāṃ yogādīnām apy apavargaprāpakatvābhāvāt punar api jarāmṛtyuprāpakatvāc ca na smṛtipurāṇeṣūktānīti vaktuṃ yuktaṃ kiñ ca
children.translated_text: Here, since it is stated in general terms 'the inferior action in which eighteen is spoken of,' and because even <s>yoga</s> and the like taught therein do not lead to final liberation, again old age and...

children.text: pādmapurāṇe: "vaiṣṇavaḥ*{731}* nāradīyañ ca tathā bhāgavataṃ śubhaṃ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>: 'The <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>], and the <s>Nāradīya</s>, and the auspicious <s>Bhāgavata</s>,

children.text: gāruḍañ ca tathā pādmaṃ vārāhaṃ śubhadarśane // [Padma.P uttarabhāga 236.19]
children.translated_text: And the <s>Gāruḍa</s>, and the <s>Pādma</s>, and the <s>Vārāha</s>, O fair-eyed one, // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.19]

children.text: ! Anm. des Herausgebers: atra aṣṭādaśapurāṇeṣu smṛtiṣu coktānāṃ śrautasmārtakarmaṇām eva avaram iti paryudāso na paryāptaḥ. tatroktayogādīnām api keṣāñcit jīrṇaplavatvasya siddhatvād iti bhāvaḥ.

children.translated_text: {728} Read: guṇī.
The supremacy of the <s>sāttvika Purāṇas</s>

children.text: sāttvikāni purāṇāni vijñeyāni ca ṣaṭ pṛthak* /{732}*
children.translated_text: These six are to be known as the <s>sāttvika</s> (sattvic) <s>Purāṇas</s>, separately. // {732}

children.text: brahmāṇḍaṃ brahmakaivartaṃ*{733}* mārkaṇḍeyaṃ tathaiva ca // [Padma.P uttarabhāga 236.20]
children.translated_text: The <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>, the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s>, and the <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> likewise, // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.20]

children.text: bhaviṣyad vāmanaṃ brāhmaṃ rājasāni ca ṣaḍvidhāḥ*{734}* / [PadmaP uttarabhāga 236.21ab]
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhaviṣya</s>, the <s>Vāmana</s>, and the <s>Brāhma</s> -- these are the six <s>rājasa</s> (rajasic) [<s>Purāṇas</s>]. // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.21ab]

children.text: mātsyaṃ kaurmaṃ tathā laiṅgaṃ śaivaṃ skāndaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>Mātsya</s>, the <s>Kūrma</s>, and the <s>Laiṅga</s>, the <s>Śaiva</s>, the <s>Skānda</s> likewise,

children.text: āgneyañ ca ṣaḍ etāni tāmasāni nibodha me //" iti [PadmaP uttarabhāga 236.18]
children.translated_text: And the <s>Āgneya</s> -- know from me that these six are the <s>tāmasa</s> (tamasic) [<s>Purāṇas</s>]." // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.18]

children.text: mātsye: "saṅkīrṇās tāmasāś caiva rājasās sāttvikās tathā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Mātsya</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]: 'Mixed, <s>tāmasa</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>sāttvika</s> likewise --

children.text: kalpāś caturvidhāḥ proktāḥ brahmaṇo divasāś ca te /
children.translated_text: The <s>kalpas</s> are declared to be of four kinds, and they are the days of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: yasmin kalpe tu yatproktaṃ purāṇaṃ brahmaṇā purā // [MatsyaP]
children.translated_text: In whichever <s>kalpa</s> a <s>Purāṇa</s> was formerly proclaimed by <s>Brahmā</s>, // [<s>Matsya Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: tasya tasya tu māhātmyaṃ tena rūpeṇa vartate /
children.translated_text: The greatness of that very [deity] endures in that form.
In the mixed [<s>kalpas</s>], the greatness of <s>Sarasvatī</s> and of the ancestors is proclaimed. // [<s>Matsya Purāṇa</s>]
In the <s>tāmasa</s> [<s>kalpas</s>], the greatness of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Śiva</s> is proclaimed.

children.text: rājaseṣu tu māhātmyam adhikaṃ brahmaṇo viduḥ // [MatsyaP]
children.translated_text: In the <s>rājasa</s> [<s>kalpas</s>], the wise know the greatness of <s>Brahmā</s> to predominate. // [<s>Matsya Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: sāttvikeṣv atha kalpeṣu māhātmyam adhikaṃ hareḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>sāttvika kalpas</s>, the greatness of <s>Hari</s> predominates.

children.text: teṣv eva yogasaṃsiddhā gamiṣyanti parāṃ gatiṃ //" iti [MatsyaP]
children.translated_text: In those very [<s>sāttvika kalpas</s>], those perfected in <s>yoga</s> will attain the supreme destination.' // [<s>Matsya Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: pādme: "vāsiṣṭhañ caiva hārītaṃ vyāsaṃ pārāśaraṃ tathā // [PadmaP uttarabhāga 236.23cd]
children.translated_text: In the <s>Padma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]: 'The <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, and the <s>Hārīta</s>, and the <s>Vyāsa</s>, and the <s>Pārāśara</s> likewise, // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.23cd]
The <s>Bhāradvāja</s> and the <s>Kāśyapīya</s> -- these six <s>smṛtis</s> are <s>sāttvika</s>.

children.text: mānavaṃ yajñavalkyañ ca ātreyaṃ dākṣyam eva ca* //{735}* [PadmaP uttarabhāga 236.24]
children.translated_text: The <s>Mānava</s>, the <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, and the <s>Ātreya</s>, and the <s>Dākṣya</s>, // {735} // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.24]
The <s>Kātyāyana</s> and the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> -- these six <s>smṛtis</s> are <s>rājasa</s>.

children.text: gautamaṃ bārhaspatyañ ca sāṃvartañ ca yamasmṛtiḥ* //{736}* [PadmaP uttarabhāga 236.25]
children.translated_text: The <s>Gautama</s>, the <s>Bārhaspatya</s>, the <s>Sāṃvarta</s>, and the <s>Yama-smṛti</s>, // {736} // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.25]

children.text: śāmbham auśanasañ caiva smṛtiṣaṭkantu tāmasam* //{737}*" iti [PadmaP uttarabhāga 236.26ab]
children.translated_text: The <s>Śāṃba</s> and the <s>Auśanasa</s> -- these six <s>smṛtis</s> are <s>tāmasa</s>.' // {737} // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.26ab]

children.text: tathā: "sāttvikā mokṣadā jñeyā rājasāḥ svargadāḥ smṛtāḥ* /{738}* [PadmaP uttarabhāga 236.21cd]
children.translated_text: And: 'The <s>sāttvika</s> are known to grant liberation, the <s>rājasa</s> are remembered as granting heaven, // {738} // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.21cd]
And the <s>tāmasa</s> likewise, O Goddess, are causes of attaining hell.' // [<s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>uttarabhāga</s> 236.22ab]

children.text: ityādi vacanasiddhasātvikapurāṇeṣu pratipāditānāṃ bhagavadārādhanādīnāṃ mokṣahetutvasmaraṇāt, sāmanyena aṣṭādaśapurāṇoktakarmaṇāṃ jīrṇaplavasādṛśyaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyam.
children.translated_text: Since the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the like, as taught in the <s>sāttvika Purāṇas</s> established by such statements, are remembered as causes of liberation, the general characterization of the actions taught in the eighteen <s>Purāṇas</s> as worn-out boats...

children.text: !{732}! PadmaP: sāttvikāni purāṇāni vijñeyāni śubhāni vai.
! PadmaP: bhaviṣyaṃ vāmanaṃ brāhmaṃ rājasāni nibodha me.
! PadmaP: bhāradvājaṃ kāśyapaṃ ca sātvikā muktidāḥ śubhāḥ / yajñavalkyaṃ tathātreyaṃ taittiriṃ dākṣam eva ca.
! PadmaP: kātyāyanaṃ vaiṣṇavañ ca rājasāḥ svargadāḥ śubhāḥ / gautamaṃ bārhaspatyañ ca sāṃvartañ ca yamasmṛtam.
! PadmaP: śāṅkhyaṃ cauśanasañ ceti tāmasā nirayapradāḥ.
! PadmaP: sāttvikā mokṣadāḥ proktā rājasāḥ sarvadā śubhāḥ; vgl. PadmaP uttarabhāga 236.25b: rājasāḥ svargadāḥ śubhāḥ.

children.translated_text: {732} <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>: 'the <s>sāttvika Purāṇas</s> should be known as auspicious indeed.'
The abundance of ritual actions in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> [system

children.text: anyathā svargamokṣanirayāṇām ekarūpatvāṅgīkārāpātāt. ataḥ śrīmadvaikhānasasūtroktāṣṭādaśasaṃskārā evety avagantavyam. bodhāyanasūtre saṃskārasaṅkhyā na kṛtā.
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of accepting that heaven, liberation, and hell are of one nature. Therefore, it should be understood that the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> are those taught in the <s>Śrī Vaikhānasa-sūtra</s> alone. In the <s>Bodhāyana-sūtra</s>, the <s>saṃskāras</s>...

children.text: āpastambādināpi pañcamahāyajñānāṃ nityahomasya ca pākayajñatvenāṅgīkārāt ete ṣoḍasaṃskārā iti vivicyānuktatvāt aparasaṃskārapratipādanābhāvāc ca na tatroktāḥ gṛhītuṃ śakyāḥ.
children.translated_text: Even by <s>Āpastamba</s> and others, since the five great sacrifices (<s>mahāyajñas</s>) and the regular fire-offering are accepted as belonging to the <s>pākayajña</s> class, these are [only] sixteen <s>saṃskāras</s> when distinguished; since additional <s>saṃskāras</s> are not specifically taught...

children.text: śrīvaikhānase tu kriyābāhulyam apy asti. tathā hi. aṣṭādaśasaṃskārāḥ pākayajñāś ca pṛthaktvenopapaditāḥ. varṣavardhanādyāstu viśeṣāḥ. pañcamahāyajñasahitā dvāviṃśadyajñāḥ - pañcamahāyajñānām ekatvam. aparaś cāṣṭādaśavyatirikta iti.
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Śrī Vaikhānasa</s> there is indeed an abundance of ritual actions. For the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> and the <s>pākayajñas</s> are established separately. And the <s>varṣavardhana</s> (annual growth rite) and the like are special features. The five...

children.text: kriyābāhulyena kim ādhikyam iti cet - ucyate. muṇḍopaniṣadi -
children.translated_text: If asked, 'What superiority comes from the abundance of ritual actions?' -- it is answered. In the <s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s>:

children.text: "kriyāvān eṣa brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ*{739}*" iti "kriyāvantaḥ śrotriyā brahmaṇiṣṭhāḥ svayaṃ juhvata
children.translated_text: 'This one, who is active in ritual, is the most excellent among the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>.' And: 'Those who are active in ritual, learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, established in <s>Brahman</s>, who themselves offer into the one <s>ṛṣi</s>

children.text: ekarṣiṃ śraddhayantaḥ. teṣām evaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta*{740}*" iti ca śrūyate.
children.translated_text: with faith -- to them alone should this knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> be taught.' // {740} // Thus it is heard [in <s>śruti</s>].

children.text: bodhāyanaḥ: "tasmād yaḥ kaścana kriyāvān satām anumatācāras sa śrotriyas sa eva vijñeyas sa eva vijñeyaḥ" iti. kiñca - karmabhūyastvāt phalabhūyastvañ ca "yathopāsanaṃ phalam" iti nyāyāt siddhyati. ataḥ: aṣṭādaśasaṃskārāpratipādakatvād asya sūtrasya śreṣṭḥatvaṃ etas sūtriṇāṃ sarvotkṛṣṭatvañ copapadyata iti nirūpitaḥ ṣaṣṭho hetuḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhāyana</s> [says]: 'Therefore, whoever is active in ritual and follows the conduct approved by the virtuous -- he is a <s>śrotriya</s> (one learned in the <s>Vedas</s>); he alone is to be known [as such].' Moreover, because of the preponderance of ritual actions, the fruit...
Thus concludes the examination of the sixth reason.

children.text: !{739}! Bezug auf MuṇḍakaU 3.1.4: prāṇo hy eṣa yaḥ sarvabhūtair vibhāti vijānan vidvān bhavate nātivādī. ātmakrīḍa ātmaratiḥ kriyāvān eṣa brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ.
! Bezug auf MuṇḍakaU 3.2.10: tad etad ṛcābhyuktam. kriyāvantaḥ śrotriyā brahmaniṣṭhāḥ svayaṃ juhvata ekarṣiṃ śraddhayantaḥ. teṣām evaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta śirovrataṃ vidhivad yais tu cīrṇam.

children.translated_text: !{739}! Reference to MuṇḍakaU 3.1.4: 'For this is the <s>prāṇa</s> that shines forth with all beings. Knowing [this], the wise one does not talk excessively. Sporting in the Self, delighting in the Self, performing actions — he is the best among knowers of <s>Brahman</s>.'
Exposition of the seventh reason

children.text: atha śrīvaikhānasasūtrasya itarasūtrāpekṣābhāvāt svātantryam astīti jñāpayituṃ sāṅgakriyākalāpavattvād iti saptamo hetur nirūpyate. tathā hi: atrasūtre aṣṭādaśasaṃskārāḥ śārīrāḥ prasiddhās sāṅgāḥ eva pratipāditāḥ.
children.translated_text: Now, in order to show that the <s>Śrīvaikhānasasūtra</s> possesses independence due to its not requiring other <s>sūtras</s>, the seventh reason — namely, 'because it possesses a complete corpus of ritual actions with their subsidiary parts (<s>sāṅgakriyākalāpavattvāt</s>)' — is expounded. For in this <s>sūtra</s>, the eighteen bodily sacraments (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are well-known and have been taught as complete with all their subsidiary parts.

children.text: nanu - aṅkurārpaṇaśatābhiṣekāgnidvayasaṃsargaputraparigrahabrahmamedhavṛṣotsarjanādipratipādanābhavāt sāṅgakriyākalāpavattvaṃ nāstīti cet - tad asat. iyaṃ śaṅkā śrīvaikhānasasūtrasvarūpānabhijñatvakṛtā. idaṃ sūtram ekādaśapraśnātmakam. atra na pratipāditānīti uktiḥ, atiriktatvena gṛhyapariśiṣṭasadbhāvājñānāt. gṛhyapariśiṣṭasadbhāvaḥ katham avagamyate iti cet - ucyate.
children.translated_text: Now, if it be objected that the completeness of the ritual corpus does not exist because the rites of seedling-offering (<s>aṅkurārpaṇa</s>), hundred-fold consecration (<s>śatābhiṣeka</s>), union with the two fires (<s>agnidvayasaṃsarga</s>), adoption of a son (<s>putraparigraha</s>), <s>brahmamedha</s> (funeral rite for a knower of Brahman), and bull-release (<s>vṛṣotsarjana</s>) are not taught — that is wrong. This objection arises from ignorance of the true nature of the <s>Śrīvaikhānasasūtra</s>. This <s>sūtra</s> consists of eleven sections (<s>praśnas</s>). The claim that these are not taught therein results from ignorance of the existence of the <s>Gṛhyapariśiṣṭa</s> (Supplementary Domestic Ritual text) as an additional [component]. If asked how the existence of the <s>Gṛhyapariśiṣṭa</s> is known — it is stated:
Beginning from "Now we shall expound the procedure for seedling-offering (<s>aṅkurārpaṇa</s>)" — the seedling-offering is stated in two sections.

children.text: "sāyaṃ sthaṇḍile sahasraṃ piṣṭena somarūpāṇi karotī"ty atra viśeṣeṇa sthaṇḍilādipratipādanam.
children.translated_text: In the passage "In the evening, on the sacred ground (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), a thousand [figures] in the form of <s>Soma</s> are made with flour" — the sacred ground and other details are specifically taught.
Beginning from "The hundred-fold consecration (<s>śatābhiṣeka</s>) in the forenoon, the auspicious ceremony, the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>* //{741}*" — [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
"In the evening, on a sacred ground (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) plastered with cow-dung, elevated toward the east,
one should draw eastward lines numbering fifty-two, // [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]

children.text: udīcīś ca tathā rekhā dvatriṃśatsaṃkhyayā*{742}* likhet*{743}* //" [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
children.translated_text: and likewise northward lines numbering thirty-two*{742}* should be drawn.*{743}*" // [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
By this and other [passages], the procedure for the hundred-fold consecration (<s>śatābhiṣeka</s>) has also been stated.
Likewise, beginning from "The two [husband and wife] should wear washed garments" — [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
"In a house adorned with lamps and other [decorations], having spread rice grains there,

children.text: carmābhāve kaṭaṃ vāpi tad ūrdhve vastram āstared*{744}* //" iti [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
children.translated_text: in the absence of a [deer-]skin, a mat or else a cloth should be spread over it.*{744}*" // [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
"At the concluding <s>homa</s> (fire-offering), at the end of the inner <s>homa</s>, [the couple] seated there on the skin,*{745}*

children.text: visṛjāmi vratañ ceti tadvrataṃ carma santyajet //"*{746}* [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
children.translated_text: [saying] 'I release the vow' — they should relinquish the skin along with the vow.*{746}*" // [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
By this and other [passages], the manner of the union with the two fires (<s>agnidvayasaṃsarga</s>) has also been taught.

And the procedure for adoption of a son (<s>putraparigraha</s>) —
"In the [matters of] renunciation, sale, and gift, even when spoken of in <s>smṛti</s>,* /{747}*

children.text: ekaṃ na dadyān no gṛhyāt na strī bhartrananujñayā //"*{748}* ityādinā [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
children.translated_text: one should not give away the only [son], nor take [one]; nor [should] a wife [act] without the husband's permission."*{748}* By this and other [passages], [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
And the procedure for <s>brahmamedha</s> (funeral rite for a knower of Brahman) —
"The sacrament for those devoted to <s>Brahman</s> and of good conduct —
<s>brahmamedha</s> is of exceedingly great fruit, [but] not for all the twice-born."*{749}* By this and other [passages], [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]
And the procedure for bull-release (<s>vṛṣotsarga</s>) —
"I shall state the procedure for bull-release, by which there is liberation from the state of being a <s>preta</s> (departed spirit),
having bathed, then at the end of the house-consecration <s>homa</s>, for the liberation from the state of being a <s>preta</s>.* //{750}*" By these and other [passages], [GṛhyapariśiṣṭaS]

children.text: evaṃ atrānuktāni sarvāṇi gṛhyapariśiṣṭe proktāni iti veditavyam.
children.translated_text: Thus it should be understood that all [rites] not stated in the [main] <s>sūtra</s> are stated in the <s>Gṛhyapariśiṣṭa</s>.

children.text: bodhāyanādibhir apy ete sāṅgā eva pratipāditā iti cet - na. "sati kuḍye cikrakarme" ti nyāyena pradhānakarmāṇi pratipāditāni cet aṅgavicāraḥ kartavyaḥ. sandhyopāsane arghyapradānādikam anuktam. vānaprasthāśramasvīkaraṇādikam api na pratipāditam. vānaprasthāśramasvīkaraṇāsvīkaraṇāraṇyāharaṇapātralakṣaṇādiṣu vaikhānasasūtrāpekṣā asty eva. devatāpratiṣṭhādikam uktaṃ lakṣaṇam anuktam.
children.translated_text: If it be said that by <s>Bodhāyana</s> and others too these are taught as complete with subsidiary parts — no. According to the maxim 'when there is a wall, then [one thinks of] painting,' when the principal rites have been taught, the subsidiary parts must be examined. In their <s>sandhyā</s> worship, the offering of <s>arghya</s> and the like are not stated. The adoption of the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) stage and the like are also not taught. Regarding the adoption or non-adoption of the <s>vānaprastha</s> stage, the carrying of forest-fire, the characteristics of the vessel, and the like — dependence on the <s>Vaikhānasasūtra</s> certainly exists. The installation of deities is stated, but its characteristics are not stated.

children.text: āpastambādibhiḥ sandhyopāsanāṅkurapratisaradevatārādhanayajñopavītadhāraṇādikam apy anuktam. āpastambādīnām anyonyāpekṣā prasiddhā. anyonyāpekṣā nāma asvātantryam aṅgahīnavat.
children.translated_text: By <s>Āpastamba</s> and others, the <s>sandhyā</s> worship, seedling-offering, protective-thread (<s>pratisara</s>), deity-worship, investiture with the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), and the like are also not stated. The mutual dependence of <s>Āpastamba</s> and others is well-known. Mutual dependence means lack of independence — like being deficient in subsidiary parts.

children.text: manu: "yad yat paravaśaṃ karma tat tad yatnena varjayet // [ManuDhŚ 4.159cd]
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s>: "Whatever action is dependent on others, that should be carefully avoided. // [ManuDhŚ 4.159cd]

children.text: sarvaṃ paravaśaṃ duḥkhaṃ sarvam ātmavaśaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: All that is dependent on others is suffering; all that is self-dependent is happiness.
One should know this, in brief, as the distinguishing mark of happiness and suffering." // [ManuDhŚ 4.160]

children.text: anena anantasthiraphalaprāptir darśitā. ataḥ sūtrāntaranairapekṣyāt sarvasūtrottamatvaṃ svātantryañ ca ghaṭata iti nirūpitas saptamo hetuḥ.
children.translated_text: By this, the attainment of infinite and enduring fruit is shown. Therefore, because of its non-dependence on other <s>sūtras</s>, its supremacy over all <s>sūtras</s> and its independence are established — thus the seventh reason is expounded.
Thus ends the exposition of the seventh reason.

Now the exposition of the eighth reason
The acceptance of the <s>Vaikhānasasūtra</s> by all authoritative scholars

children.text: idānīṃ tāvat śrutismṛtipurāṇādibhiḥ sarvottaratvenāvagatasya śrīvaikhānasasūtrasya akhilaśiṣṭaparigṛhītatvam astīti darśayituṃ manvādyaiḥ svīkṛtatvād iti aṣṭamo hetuḥ nirūpyate. tathā hi
children.translated_text: Now then, in order to show that the <s>Śrīvaikhānasasūtra</s>, which has been recognized as supreme by <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like, has been accepted by all authoritative scholars (<s>akhilaśiṣṭaparigṛhītatvam</s>) — the eighth reason, namely 'because it was adopted by <s>Manu</s> and others,' is expounded. For:

children.text: manu: "ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmaṃ vaikhānasāśramam //"*{751}* ity ārabhya
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s>: Beginning from "Henceforth I shall declare the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> stage of life."*{751}*
"One should always subsist on flowers, roots, and fruits alone,

children.text: kālapakvaiḥ svayaṃ śīrṇair vaikhānasamate sthitaḥ* //{752}*" iti [ManuDhŚ 6.21]
children.translated_text: [on those] ripened by time and fallen by themselves, being established in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> doctrine.* //{752}*" [ManuDhŚ 6.21]

children.text: vyāsa: "mūlair eke phalair eke puṣpair eke dṛḍhavratāḥ / [MBh 12.236.13cd]
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāsa</s>: "Some [subsist] on roots, some on fruits, some on flowers — those of firm vows, [MBh 12.236.13cd]
they live according to proper rule, established in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> doctrine." // [MBh 12.236.14ab]
<s>Gautama</s>: '[The <s>vānaprastha</s>] having established the fire by the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> (ascetic) rite, not eating village food.'*{753}*

children.text: yama: śrāmaṇakena vidhānena sāyaṃ prātar upaspṛśet. iti
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>: 'By the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> procedure, one should perform ablutions morning and evening.'

children.text: śaṅkhalikhitau: śrāmaṇakenāgnim ādhāya kāle kuruvinda - veṇu - śyāmākanīvārādibhir vartayet.*{754}* iti.
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Likhita</s>: 'Having established the fire by the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> rite, one should subsist at the proper time on <s>kuruvinda</s>, bamboo, <s>śyāmāka</s>, <s>nīvāra</s> (wild rice), and the like.'*{754}*

children.text: hārīta: vānaprastho grāmyā oṣadhī parivarjayet. tretāgnīnāṃ sthāne śrāmaṇakaṃ vāgnim ādhāya valkalaśāṇacarmakuśamuñjavidalakaṃ vā vasāno vaikhānasaproktena vidhinā vānaprastho vikhanā bhavati. anujñāyiko 'nuprasthāyikaś" ceti
children.translated_text: <s>Hārīta</s>: 'The <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) should abstain from cultivated plants. In place of the three fires, having established the fire by the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> rite, wearing bark, hemp, skins, <s>kuśa</s>-grass, <s>muñja</s>-grass, or strips of fiber, following the procedure prescribed by <s>Vikhanas</s>, the <s>vānaprastha</s> becomes a <s>Vaikhānasa</s>. [There are two kinds:] the permitted one (<s>anujñāyika</s>) and the accompanying one (<s>anuprasthāyika</s>).'
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>: 'Having established the fire by the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> rite, the one who maintains the sacred fire dwells at the root of a tree.'*{755}* [VāsiṣṭhaDhŚ 9.10]
<s>Bodhāyana</s>: "The <s>vānaprastha</s> follows the customs of the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> scripture." [BaudhDhS 12.6.11.14]

children.text: āpastamba: "ekāgnir aniketaḥ syād"*{756}* iti. asya dharmakarpardī "gārhapatyādīnāṃ tretāgnīnāṃ sthāne yasyaiko 'gniḥ aupāsana eva - vaikhānasasūtre dṛṣṭatvāt, pāṇigrahaṇanimitvadvādaupāsanasya.
children.translated_text: <s>Āpastamba</s>: "He should have a single fire and no fixed abode."*{756}* On this, <s>Dharmakarpardī</s> [comments]: 'He whose single fire is only the <s>aupāsana</s> (domestic fire), in place of the three fires beginning with <s>gārhapatya</s> — because this is seen in the <s>Vaikhānasasūtra</s>, since the <s>aupāsana</s> fire has its cause in the marriage rite (<s>pāṇigrahaṇa</s>).'

children.text: jaiminīyasūtre saumikacāturmāsyaprakāraṇe. "bhāradvājapūrvaṃ yathā vaikhānasapūrvaṃ pañcaḥ" meti*{757}* (?)
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jaiminīya</s> sūtra, in the section on the <s>Saumika Cāturmāsya</s> rites: "Preceded by <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, just as preceded by <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, five."*{757}* (?)

The fact that acceptance by all authoritative scholars constitutes a reason for superior authority

children.text: atrobhayatra ātrivyākhyānam - ṣoḍaśartvijāṃ madhye bhāradvājasūtriṇaṃ prastotāraṃ vaikhānasasūtriṇaṃ pratihartāraṃ varayet" iti.
children.translated_text: Here, the commentary of <s>Ātri</s> on both [passages] is: 'Among the sixteen priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>), one should choose a follower of the <s>Bhāradvāja</s> sūtra as the <s>prastotṛ</s> (praiser) and a follower of the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> sūtra as the <s>pratihartṛ</s> (respondent).'
In the <s>Kapiñjalasaṃhitā</s>:
"Endowed with the performance of sacrifice and teaching, one who bestows grace upon disciples,
is to be known as an <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), devoted to <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>.* //{758}* [KapiñjalaS]
Whether in a hermitage or in the forest, devoted to wife and children,
always devoted to the eight-syllable [mantra] — he is called a <s>Vaikhānasa</s>.* //{759}* [KapiñjalaS]
A forest-dweller should avoid all village customs,*{760}*
clad in bark and deer-skin — he is called a <s>maunin</s> (silent sage)." // [KapiñjalaS]
In the <s>Pādma</s> [Purāṇa], in the section on the twelve syllables:
"...... accompanied by wife and children,

children.text: vane vā pattane vāpi japed vaikhānasaḥ śuciḥ //
children.translated_text: whether in the forest or in a town, the pure <s>Vaikhānasa</s> should chant. //

children.text: viyuktaḥ putradārādyaiḥ svayam eva vane sthitaḥ //" [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: Separated from wife, children, and the rest, dwelling alone in the forest." // [PadmaP]
Others have also stated the same.

children.text: akhilaśiṣṭaparigrahe ko viśeṣa iti cet - akhilaśiṣṭaparigrahāt prāmāṇyātiśayo 'stīty avagamyate.
children.translated_text: If asked what distinction there is in acceptance by all authoritative scholars — it is understood that from acceptance by all authoritative scholars there arises a superiority of authority.

children.text: āśvamedhike: "dharmaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ pramāṇaṃ prathamaṃ śrutiḥ / [MBh 14, App. 4.2492]
children.translated_text: In the <s>Aśvamedha</s> [section]: "For those seeking to know <s>dharma</s>, the first authority is <s>śruti</s> (revelation), [MBh 14, App. 4.2492]

children.text: dvitīyaṃ dharmaśāstraṃ hi*{761}* tṛtīyaṃ lokasaṅgrahaḥ* //{762}*" iti [MBh 14, App. 4.2493]
children.translated_text: the second is <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (law texts),*{761}* and the third is popular consensus (<s>lokasaṅgraha</s>).* //{762}*" [MBh 14, App. 4.2493]
<s>Manu</s>: "That which is properly practiced by the learned,*{763}* who are always free from hatred and attachment,

children.text: hṛdayenābhyanujñāto yo dharmas taṃ nibodhata //" iti [ManuDhŚ 2.1]
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> approved by the heart — know that [to be authoritative]." // [ManuDhŚ 2.1]

children.text: yājñavalkya: "catvāro vedadharmajñāḥ parṣat traividyam eva vā /
children.translated_text: <s>Yājñavalkya</s>: "An assembly of four who know the <s>Veda</s> and <s>dharma</s>, or even three who know the three <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: sā brūte 'yaṃ sa dharmaḥ syād eko vādhyātmavittamaḥ // [YājñavalkyaDhŚ 1.9]
children.translated_text: when it declares 'this is <s>dharma</s>' — that shall be <s>dharma</s>; or even a single one who is the greatest knower of the Self. // [YājñavalkyaDhŚ 1.9]

children.text: vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ smṛtayaḥ pramāṇaṃ dharmārthayuktaṃ vacanaṃ pramāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> are authority, the <s>smṛtis</s> are authority, a statement conforming to <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> is authority;

children.text: yasya pramāṇaṃ na bhavet pramāṇaṃ kas tasya kuryād vacanaṃ pramāṇaṃ //
children.translated_text: when the authority of one who is [himself] an authority does not hold, who would make his word an authority?
