children.text: na yasya vedā na ca dharmaśāstraṃ
children.translated_text: For one whose authority is neither the <s>Vedas</s> nor <s>dharmaśāstra</s>,
nor the words of the elders,
that evil-doer, slain by the wicked, of evil nature —
even his own self becomes his [only] authority (?)." // [YājñavalkyaDhŚ]
Three ways of establishing the Vedic basis of <s>smṛti</s>

children.text: smṛter api vedamūlatve tredhā nirvāhaḥ kṛtaḥ. nityānumeyaśrutimūlatvam prābhākarāḥ. "teṣām utsannāḥ pāṭhāḥ prayogād anumīyanta"*{764}* ity utsannaśākhāmūlatvam āpastambādyāḥ. tat prābhākarādhibhiḥ dūṣitaṃ bhāṣyakārānabhimatañ ca. prābhākarapakṣe 'pi nityānumeyaśrutimūlatve akṣaraśo vā ānupūrvīviśeṣaviśiṣṭatvena vā. akṣaraśa iti yady ucyate tarhi kaṭatapayādīnām api nityānumeyaśrutimūlatvāt smṛtitvaṃ syāt.
children.translated_text: Three ways of establishing the Vedic basis of <s>smṛti</s> have also been accomplished. The <s>Prābhākaras</s> [hold] that it is based on eternally inferable <s>śruti</s>. "Their recensions having been lost, [the rules] are inferred from practice"*{764}* — the position of <s>Āpastamba</s> and others is that it is based on lost Vedic recensions. That has been refuted by the <s>Prābhākaras</s> and others, and is not accepted by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (<s>Śaṅkara</s>). Even in the <s>Prābhākara</s> position, regarding the eternally inferable <s>śruti</s> basis — is it syllable by syllable, or as qualified by a specific sequence? If 'syllable by syllable' is said, then even [works like] <s>kaṭapayādi</s> and others would have the status of <s>smṛti</s>, since they too would have an eternally inferable <s>śruti</s> basis.

children.text: ānupūrvīviśeṣaviśiṣṭatveneti cet nityānumeyatvaṃ bhajyet iti. utsannaśākhāmūlatvam iti pakṣe śākhāsu tatratatrotsannā vā utaikā śākhā utsannā vā. tatratatreti cet na - padakramādirūpeṇādhīyamānatvād utsannaśākhāmūlatvaṃ na ghaṭate. ekaivotsanneti cet - na. viṣṇor aṃśāvatārasya tapoyogabalopetasya sarvavedasākṣāt kāravato vyāsasya ajñātāśāsaṃbhavena ekasyāpi śiṣyasya tad adhyāpanasāmarthyasambhavāt tathā vaktum ayuktatvād iti. ato viprakīrṇaśākhāmūlatvaṃ vaktavyam. tathoktam.
children.translated_text: If 'as qualified by a specific sequence' — [then one should say] it would partake of being eternally inferable. In the position of 'based on lost recensions' — are portions lost here and there among the recensions, or is one entire recension lost? If 'here and there' — no, because since [the Vedas] are studied in the forms of <s>pada</s> (word-by-word) and <s>krama</s> (sequential) recitation, the basis in lost recensions is not possible. If 'one entire [recension] is lost' — no, because since <s>Vyāsa</s>, an incarnation of a portion of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, endowed with the power of austerity and <s>yoga</s>, directly perceived all the <s>Vedas</s>, the non-existence of even a single disciple capable of learning it is impossible, and it would therefore be improper to say so. Hence, one should say it is based on scattered recensions. And so it has been stated.

children.text: "durbodhā vaidikāś śabdāḥ prakīrṇatvāc ca ye khilāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Vedic words that are difficult to understand, and those <s>Khila</s> (supplementary) texts that are scattered —

children.text: tadjñais ta eva sṣaṣṭārthāḥ*{765}* smṛtitantre pratiṣṭhitāḥ* //{766}*" iti
children.translated_text: those very [words], with their meanings elucidated by experts, are established in <s>Smṛti</s> and <s>Tantra</s>." Thus.

children.text: ataḥ śrutismṛtipurāṇādibhiḥ prāmāṇatvenāvagatasya śrīvaikhānasasūtrasya akhilaśiṣṭaparigrahāt prāmāṇyātiśayo 'stīti "manvādyais svīkṛtatvād" iti nirūpito 'ṣṭamo hetuḥ.
children.translated_text: Therefore, the authority of the <s>Śrī Vaikhānasa Sūtra</s>, known to be authoritative through <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and other texts, has a surplus of authority due to its acceptance by all the learned. Thus the eighth reason, "because it was accepted by <s>Manu</s> and others," has been determined.
Thus ends the determination of the eighth reason.

children.text: !{764}! Bezug auf ĀpastambaDhS 1.4.12.10: brāhmaṇoktā vidhayas teṣām utsannāḥ pāṭhāḥ prayogād anumīyante /.
! Dieser Vers ist auch in DHN[D] 3.14-15 zitiert.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 764] Reference to <s>Āpastamba Dharmasūtra</s> 1.4.12.10: The injunctions stated by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — their lost readings are inferred from practice.
Determination of the ninth reason
The exclusive devotion of the <s>Vaikhānasa Sūtra</s> followers to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: athedānīm āpastabādisūtrāntaraniṣṭhānāṃ sūtrakārād ārabhya avicchinnatvena paramparayā ekāntitvaṃ nāstīti jñāpayituṃ vaikhānasasūtriṇām eva tat sambhavatīti darśayituṃ.
children.translated_text: Now, in order to make known that for those who follow other <s>sūtras</s> such as <s>Āpastamba</s> and the like, exclusive devotion (<s>ekāntitvam</s>) has not existed in an unbroken succession from the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtra</s>) onward, and to show that this is possible only for the followers of the <s>Vaikhānasa Sūtra</s>:
"Perception, inference, and scripture of diverse traditions —
these three should be well-known and understood by one who desires the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s>." [<s>Manu Dharmaśāstra</s> 12.105]

children.text: iti manusmaraṇānusāreṇa pratyakṣādibhir avagamayituñ ca akhilajagadekakāraṇabhūtaśrīmannārāyaṇaikaparatvād iti navamo hetur nirūpyate.
children.translated_text: In accordance with this statement of <s>Manu</s>, in order to establish through perception and other means [of knowledge], the ninth reason is determined: because of exclusive devotion to <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is the sole cause of the entire world.
Regarding the exclusive devotion of this <s>sūtra</s> to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>:
The six marks of purport therein
"The opening and conclusion, repetition, novelty, fruit,
<s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passages), and reasoning — these are the marks for determining the purport."
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is denoted by the word <s>Parabrahman</s>

children.text: ity uktāni ṣaḍvidhāni tātparyaliṅgāni santi. tathā hi ādyapraśne prathamakhāṇḍe "nārāyaṇaparāyaṇa"*{768}* ity uktam. evaṃ "sadādhyātmarato dhyānayogī nārāyaṇaparaṃ brahma paśyan dhāraṇaṃ dhārayed akṣaraṃ paraṃ brahmāpnoti - "nārāyaṇaparaṃ brahmeti śrutiḥ" ity upasaṃhāre sannyāsavidhau pratipāditam. sandhyopāsanādi - puṇyāhāghārāntahoma - nāndīmukhopanayana - pāṇigrahaṇaparyanteṣu antakarmaṇi ca ato devādivaiṣṇavā mantrāḥ viniyuktāḥ. evaṃ āghāraprakaraṇe "śaro 'ṅgāre 'gnau juhuyād" iti sūtreṇa idhmādhānaṃ taittirīyabrāhmaṇavākyānusāreṇa parabrahmāgnau vihitam.
children.translated_text: Thus the six marks of purport have been stated. For in the first question, in the first section, it is said: "devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>." Similarly, "always delighting in the <s>Adhyātma</s> (Self), the <s>dhyāna</s>-yogin, seeing the supreme <s>Brahman</s> that is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, should practice the meditation (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) on the imperishable supreme <s>Brahman</s>" — thus in the conclusion, in the injunction of renunciation, it is established: "'The supreme <s>Brahman</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' — thus the <s>Śruti</s>." From the <s>Sandhyopāsanā</s> (twilight worship) and other rites through the <s>Puṇyāha</s>, <s>Āghāra</s>, concluding <s>homa</s>, <s>Nāndīmukha</s>, <s>Upanayana</s>, and <s>Pāṇigrahaṇa</s> (marriage), and in the concluding rites — throughout, <s>Vaiṣṇava mantras</s> relating to the deity are employed. Likewise, in the section on <s>Āghāra</s>, by the <s>sūtra</s> "one should offer into the fire on the coal with the arrow," the placing of fuel is prescribed in the fire of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, in accordance with the statement of the <s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: !{767}! ManuDhŚ: pratyakṣaṃ cānumānaṃ ca śāstraṃ ca vividhāgamam / trayaṃ suviditaṃ kāryaṃ dharmaśuddhim abhīpsatā.
! Bezug auf VaikhSmS 1.1: nārāyaṇaparāyaṇo nirdvandvo munir iti saṃskāraviśeṣāt pūrvāt pūrvāt parovarīyān iti vijñāyate.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 767] <s>Manu Dharmaśāstra</s> reads: pratyakṣaṃ cānumānaṃ ca śāstraṃ ca vividhāgamam / trayaṃ suviditaṃ kāryaṃ dharmaśuddhim abhīpsatā.
The share of <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others in the sacrifice is obtained through the Lord's grace

children.text: parabrahmaśabdābhidheyaś ca bhagavān nārāyaṇa eveti vedānteṣu nirṇītam. tathāhi: "sad eva somyedamagra āsīt, ekam evādvitīyam" ityādibhiḥ pratipannasya abhinnanimittopādānakāraṇasya "yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante - tadbrahme"tyādinā jagatkāraṇatvaṃ brahmaśabdavācyatvañ ca pratipādyate. tasya "satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahme" tyādinā śodhakavākyena svarūpaṃ nirūpyate. satyatvādiviśiṣṭasya tasya "ānando brahma" iti niratiśayānandarūpatvaṃ pratipādyate. etādṛśabrahmarūpaṃ vastu "nārāyaṇaparaṃ brahma" "tattvaṃ nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ" "eko ha vai nārāyaṇa āsīt" "apahatapāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ" ityādi vākyaiḥ śrīmannārāyaṇa eveti niyamyate. evañ ca "adhyūhante" iti taittirīyavākyaśeṣasthabrahmaśabdo 'pi nārāyaṇapara eveti prakṛtasūtroktedhmādhānam api nārāyaṇaparam eva.
children.translated_text: And it is determined in the <s>Vedānta</s> that the entity denoted by the word <s>Parabrahman</s> (supreme <s>Brahman</s>) is the Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone. For thus: by texts such as "Being alone, O dear one, was this in the beginning, one only without a second," the entity that is the non-different material and efficient cause is established as being denoted by the word <s>Brahman</s> and as being the cause of the world, through texts such as "That from which these beings are born — that is <s>Brahman</s>." Its essential nature is determined through the qualifying statement: "<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, and infinite." Of that entity, distinguished by truth and so on, the nature as unsurpassed bliss is established by "Bliss is <s>Brahman</s>." Such an entity of the form of <s>Brahman</s> is determined to be <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s> alone through texts such as: "The supreme <s>Brahman</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>," "<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the supreme reality," "<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone existed," and "Free from evil, divine, the one god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>." And thus, the word <s>Brahman</s> occurring in the continuation of the <s>Taittirīya</s> text "they superimpose" is also exclusively referring to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — and therefore the placing of fuel mentioned in the present <s>sūtra</s> is also exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: evam ādhāne - "dhyāyan nārāyaṇam upoṣya" iti, agnihotre - bhūmānaṃ viṣṇuṃ dhyāyet" iti, darśapūrṇamāse - "udita āditye dhyāyan nārāyaṇaṃ 'viṣṇor nu kam'; iti japitvā" iti, some ca - "nārāyaṇaparāyaṇas tūṣṇīm āste" iti ca sarvatrāpi abhyāsena nārāyaṇaparatvenoktatvāt idaṃ sūtraṃ nārāyaṇaparam eva.
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment): "Meditating on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, having fasted"; in the <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-offering): "One should meditate on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the All-pervading"; in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon sacrifices): "When the sun has risen, meditating on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, having recited '<s>Viṣṇor nu kam</s>'"; and in the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice: "Devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he sits in silence" — since everywhere through repetition it is stated as devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, this <s>sūtra</s> is exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: nanu - atra sūtre pravāsāgamane āśvayujyāñ ca "pradakṣiṇam arcanaṃ praṇāmo guhasya" - "bhavaṃ devam āvāhya" ity uktatvāt sarvatra nārāyaṇaparatvam asyeti kathaṃ vaktuṃ śakyate iti cet - ucyate. "aṅgāny anyā devatā" iti aṅgabhūtānāṃ brahmarudrādīnām api yajñāṃśabhāktvaṃ bhagavatprasādalabdham iti bhāratādināvagamyate - tathāhi
children.translated_text: Now, if it is objected: since in this <s>sūtra</s>, regarding the return from a journey and in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>, "circumambulation, worship, and prostration to <s>Guha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>)" and "having invoked the god <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)" are stated — how can it be said that this is exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>? — it is replied: "The other deities are limbs (<s>aṅga</s>)" — it is understood from the <s>Bhārata</s> and other texts that the share in the sacrifice of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others, who are subsidiary parts, was obtained through the grace of the Lord. For thus:

children.text: "tatas te surās sarve brahmā te ca maharṣayaḥ* //{769}* [MBh 12.327.48cd]
children.translated_text: "Then all those gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, and those great sages, [MBh 12.327.48cd]
commenced the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> sacrifice according to the rite seen in the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: tasmin satre tathā brahmā svayaṃ bhāgam akalpayat /
children.translated_text: In that sacrificial session, <s>Brahmā</s> himself appointed his own share,

children.text: devā mahārṣayaś caiva sarve bhāgān akalpayan* //{770}* [MBh 12.327.49]
children.translated_text: and the gods and great sages all appointed their shares. [MBh 12.327.49]
Those shares, characterized by the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>, supremely refined,

children.text: prāpur ādityavarṇaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ tamasaḥ param* //{771}* [MBh 12.327.50]
children.translated_text: reached that <s>Puruṣa</s> of sun-like brilliance, beyond darkness. [MBh 12.327.50]

children.text: śrībhagavān: yena yaḥ kalpito bhāgaḥ sa tathā samupāgataḥ* /{772}*
children.translated_text: The blessed Lord [said]: 'Whatever share was appointed by whomever, that has duly arrived;
I am pleased and bestow today the fruit characterized by non-return.' [MBh 12.327.52]

children.text: yajñīye cāpi yakṣyanti sarvalokeṣu vai surāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And the gods shall sacrifice in all worlds at the sacrificial [rites],

children.text: kalpayiṣyanti vo bhāgāṃs te narā vedakalpitān* //{773}* [MBh 12.327.54]
children.translated_text: and those humans shall apportion your shares as ordained by the <s>Vedas</s>.' [MBh 12.327.54]

children.text: !{769}! MBh: tatas te vibudhāḥ sarve brahmā te ca maharṣayaḥ.
! MBh: vedadṛṣṭena vidhinā vaiṣṇavaṃ kratum āharan / tasmin satre tadā brahmā svayaṃ bhāgam akalpayat / devā devarṣayaś caiva sarve bhāgān akalpayan.
! MBh: te kārtayugadharmāṇo bhāgāḥ paramasatkṛtāḥ / prāpur ādityavarṇaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ tamasaḥ param.
! MBh: yena yaḥ kalpito bhāgaḥ sa tathā samupāgataḥ.
! MBh: yajñair ye cāpi yakṣyanti sarvalokeṣu vai surāḥ / kalpayiṣyanti vo bhāgāṃs te narā vedakalpitān.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 769] MBh reads: tatas te vibudhāḥ sarve brahmā te ca maharṣayaḥ.
<s>Rudrī</s> and others are worthy of worship as limbs of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: yo me yathā kalpitavān bhāgam asmin mahākratau /
children.translated_text: 'He who has appointed for me a share in this great sacrifice,

children.text: sa mahāyajñabhāgārho vedasūtre mayā kṛtaḥ //"*{774}* iti [MBh 12.327.55]
children.translated_text: he has been made by me worthy of a share in the great sacrifice, through the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Sūtra</s>.' Thus. [MBh 12.327.55]
In the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>: "I, <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and the chief ones, the lords of creatures, lord of beings, lord of the gods, and others as foremost —

children.text: sarve vayaṃ yanniyamaṃ prapannā mūrdhnārpitaṃ lokadhuraṃ vahāmaḥ //"*{775}*
children.translated_text: all of us, having submitted to his ordinance, bear upon our heads the burden of the world."

children.text: evaṃ ca bhavādīnām api nārāyaṇāṅgatvena pūjārhatvāvagamāt.
children.translated_text: And thus, since it is understood that <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) and others too are worthy of worship by virtue of being limbs of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>:
"The worship of the gods as limbs is not prohibited;

children.text: svatantrabuddhyā kurvan hi brāhmaṇo narakaṃ vrajet //
children.translated_text: but a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who does so thinking them independent would go to hell.

children.text: brahmāṇam indram agniṃ vā harer āvaraṇaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, or [any deity] — without the surrounding worship of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: yas tu sampūjayed vipraḥ sa pāṣaṇḍī bhaved dhruvam //"
children.translated_text: a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who would worship [them independently] would certainly become a heretic."

children.text: ityādinā aṅgabhāvena teṣām arcanaṃ kurvato doṣābhāvasmaraṇāc ca sūtre tathoktiḥ.
children.translated_text: And because the absence of fault for one who worships them as limbs is remembered, such statements are found in the <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: tathā: "anyatra tvāṃ samāropya yady upāsā vidhīṃyate*{776}* /
children.translated_text: Likewise: "If worship is performed having superimposed [the deity's nature] upon something other [than <s>Viṣṇu</s>],

children.text: sā vṛttiḥ pracyutā proktā tava tattvaṃ tathaiva ca // [KJ.K ]
children.translated_text: that practice is declared to be 'fallen,' and your true nature [is lost] thereby. [KJK]

children.text: tvayi sarvaṃ samāropya yady upāsā vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: If worship is performed having superimposed everything upon you [<s>Viṣṇu</s>],

children.text: sā vṛttiḥ sakalā jñeyā tava tattvaṃ tavaiva hi //" [KJK ]
children.translated_text: that practice should be known as 'complete,' and your true nature is indeed yours." [KJK]

children.text: iti jñānakāṇḍe kaśyapenopāsanasvarūpabhedapradarśanāt "viṣṇor nityārcā sarvadevārcā bhavatī"*{777}*ti mukhyatvena sūtreṇa pratipāditatvāt pracyutiphalapradatvābhāvāc ca teṣām aṅgabhāvena pūjanaṃ yujyate. āpastambādisūtreṣu sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ sadvārakatvena pratipādanāt nārāyaṇaikaparatvena sakṛd api smaraṇābhavāt teṣāṃ na nārāyaṇaikaparatvam.
children.translated_text: Thus, since in the <s>Jñānakāṇḍa</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s> demonstrates the distinction in the nature of worship; since it is established by the <s>sūtra</s> as the primary [principle] that "the eternal worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> constitutes the worship of all the gods"; and since there is no production of the fruit of 'falling' — it is fitting to worship those [other deities] as limbs. In the <s>sūtras</s> of <s>Āpastamba</s> and others, since all rituals are established as being mediated through [various deities], and since there is not even a single mention of exclusive devotion to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, their [tradition] does not have exclusive devotion to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
The absence of exclusive devotion to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in the <s>sūtras</s> of <s>Āpastamba</s> and others

children.text: nanu bodhāyanenāpi "athāto viṣṇupratiṣṭhākalpaṃ vyākhyasyāmo dvādaśyām ekādaśyāṃ śroṇāyāṃ vā yāni cānyāni śubhanakṣatrāṇi"*{778}* ity ārabhya "dvādaśanāmabhiḥ amuṣmai svāhā amuṣmai svāhā"*{779}* ityādinā homādikam uktā.
children.translated_text: Now, [it may be objected that] even by <s>Baudhāyana</s>, beginning with "Now we shall explain the method of establishing <s>Viṣṇu</s> — on the twelfth, the eleventh, or on the <s>Śroṇā</s> [asterism], or on other auspicious asterisms," and through "with the twelve names: to such-and-such one <s>svāhā</s>, to such-and-such one <s>svāhā</s>," the <s>homa</s> and other rites are prescribed.
"We worship you, the one, primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, the ancient,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the creator of the universe;
you are the sacrifice ordained and to be performed,
you yourself, O Self, accept the oblation." [<s>Baudhāyana Gṛhya Śeṣa Sūtra</s> 2.13.36]

children.text: !{774}! MBh: yo me yathā kalpitavān bhāgam asmin mahākratau / sa tathā yajñabhāgārho vedasūtre mayā kṛtaḥ.
! BhāgavataP 9.4.54: ahaṃ bhavo dakṣabhṛgupradhānāḥ prajeśabhūteśasureśamukhyāḥ / sarve vayaṃ yanniyamaṃ prapannā mūrdhnyārpitaṃ lokahitaṃ vahāmaḥ.
! Bezug auf VaikhSmS 4.10: athāgnau nityahomānte viṣṇor nityārcā sarvadevārcanā bhavati.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 774] MBh reads: yo me yathā kalpitavān bhāgam asmin mahākratau / sa tathā yajñabhāgārho vedasūtre mayā kṛtaḥ.
The devotion of <s>Āpastamba</s> and others to multiple deities

children.text: iti nārāyaṇaikaparatvena pratipādanāt kathaṃ teṣāṃ nārāyaṇaikaparatvaṃ nāstīty ucyata iti cet - satyam. āpastambādīnām ācāryeṇānena bodhāyanena nārāyaṇaikaparatvena pratiṣṭhādikam anuktam. kintu. "atha rudrapratiṣṭhāvidhiṃ*{780}* vyākhyāsyāmaḥ. caturthyām aṣṭamyām ārdrāyām apabharaṇyāṃ vā*{781}* yāni cānyāni śubhanakṣatrāṇi" iti prakṛtya "bhavāya devāya svāhe"tyādibhiḥ "bhavasya devasya patnyai svāhe"*{782}*tyādibhiś ca homādikam uktvā [BaudhGṛŚeṣS 2.16.1-2]
children.translated_text: If it is asked: since [<s>Baudhāyana</s>] establishes [the rite] as exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, how can it be said that they do not have exclusive devotion to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>? — True [he does so]. But by this same teacher <s>Baudhāyana</s> of <s>Āpastamba</s> and others, the establishment and other rites are not stated exclusively in devotion to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Rather: beginning with "Now we shall explain the method of establishing <s>Rudra</s> — on the fourth, the eighth, on <s>Ārdrā</s> or <s>Apabharaṇī</s>, or on other auspicious asterisms," and through [mantras] such as "to <s>Bhava</s> the god <s>svāhā</s>" and "to the wife of <s>Bhava</s> the god <s>svāhā</s>," the <s>homa</s> and other rites are stated, [<s>Baudhāyana Gṛhya Śeṣa Sūtra</s> 2.16.1-2]
"We worship you, the one, primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, the ancient,
<s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the creator of the universe;
you are the sacrifice ordained and to be performed,
you yourself, O Self, accept the oblation." [<s>Baudhāyana Gṛhya Śeṣa Sūtra</s> 2.16.39]

children.text: iti śivapratiṣṭhā, evaṃ "athāto mahādevasyāharahaḥ paricaryāvidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ"*{783}*
children.translated_text: Thus the establishment of <s>Śiva</s> [is prescribed]. Likewise, "Now we shall explain the method of daily worship of <s>Mahādeva</s>,"

children.text: ity ārabhya "mahādevam āvāhayet - āyātu bhagavān mahādeva"*{784}* iti pṛthaktvena rudrapūjā ca pratipāditā. tathā - anyatra "athāto 'rdhamāse 'rdhamāse 'ṣṭamyāṃ brāhmaṇāḥ striyaś cāhuḥ" ity ārabhya "atha pradoṣe rudraṃ virūpākṣaṃ sapanīkaṃ*{785}* sasutaṃ sapārṣadam" ityādibhiḥ rudrāvāhanam uktam. evaṃ "ādityam ambikāṃ viṣṇuṃ gaṇanāthaṃ maheśvaram"*{786}* iti pañcapūjā ca. ataḥ bodhāyanasūtraṃ nārāyaṇaikaparaṃ na bhavati.
children.translated_text: beginning thus, and "one should invoke <s>Mahādeva</s> — may the blessed <s>Mahādeva</s> come" — the worship of <s>Rudra</s> is also separately established. Likewise, elsewhere: beginning with "Now, every fortnight, on the eighth, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and women recite," and through "Then at dusk, <s>Rudra Virūpākṣa</s> with his retinue, with his son, with his attendants" — the invocation of <s>Rudra</s> is stated. Similarly, "<s>Āditya</s>, <s>Ambikā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Gaṇanātha</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>" — the <s>pañcapūjā</s> (fivefold worship) [is also prescribed]. Therefore, the <s>Baudhāyana Sūtra</s> is not exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: atha āpastambādayaḥ kiṃ nārāyaṇaikaparaḥ - ata rudraparāḥ āhosvit nānādevatāparāḥ?. nārāyaṇaikaparā iti cen na. jātikulācārādiṣv āgotraprathamād ārabhya:
children.translated_text: Now then — are <s>Āpastamba</s> and others exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, or devoted to <s>Rudra</s>, or devoted to multiple deities? If [it is said they are] exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — no. [They follow diverse practices,] beginning from the first of the lineage in matters of caste, family, custom, and so forth:
"His mother-in-law practices the <s>Digambara</s> (naked ascetic) vow; his relatives are Buddhists;

children.text: mātā cāsya pitā ca pāśupatinau vaiśeṣiko deśikaḥ /
children.translated_text: his mother and father are <s>Pāśupatas</s> (<s>Śaiva</s>s); his teacher is a <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>;
his brother stands in the <s>Sāṅkhya-Yoga</s> school; his friend is a pupil of the <s>Cārvākas</s> (materialists);
called by the name 'False-conduct' himself, he is a subverter of the Vedic [path]."

children.text: ! Bezug auf BaudhGṛŚeṣS 2.16.35: kṛsaram ājyamiśraṃ juhuyāt - 'bhavāya devāya svāhā'; ity aṣṭābhiḥ 'bhavasya devasya patnyai svāhā'; ityādibhiḥ.

! Bezug auf BaudhGṛŚeṣS 2.17.1: snātaś śucis same śucau deśe gomayenopalipya devasya pratikṛtiṃ kṛtvākṣatapuṣpair yathālābham arcayitvā saha puṣpodakena mahādevam āvāhayet - 'oṃ bhūḥ puruṣaṃ āvāhayāmi'; ityādi 'āyātu bhagavān mahādevaḥ'; iti.
! Dieser Halbvers ist auch zitiert in DHN[D] 64.12.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 780] <s>Baudhāyana Gṛhya Śeṣa Sūtra</s> reads: rudrapratiṣṭhākalpaṃ.

children.text: ity uktarītyā eteṣāṃ śaivapāśupatavaiṣṇavādyākariṇa vidyamānatvāt āpastambādisūtrāṇy api nārāyaṇaikaparāṇi na bhavanti. bhagavato nārāyaṇasya samārādhanavidhipratipādanābhāvāc ca. nārāyaṇaikaparañ ced āpastambādisūtraṃ tarhi tatsūtroktadharmānuṣṭhātāraḥ sarve 'pi nārāyaṇaikaparā eva syuḥ. na ca tathā dṛśyate. pāñcarātrādyuktamārgeṇa vaiṣṇavasaṃpādane "svasūtre vidyamāne tu" - "svasūtrasya parityāgāt" - "yas svadharmaṃ parityajya" "vidharmaḥ paradharmaś ca" - śreyā svadharmo viguṇaḥ" - ityādi vacanapratipāditasvasūtraparityāgaparadharmasvīkāraśākhāraṇḍatvādidoṣāḥ prasajyeran.
children.translated_text: In the manner stated above, since followers of <s>Śaiva</s>, <s>Pāśupata</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, and other [traditions] exist among those [who follow the <s>Āpastamba</s> and other <s>sūtras</s>], the <s>Āpastamba</s> and other <s>sūtras</s> also are not exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. And because there is no teaching in them of the method of the complete worship of the Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. If the <s>Āpastamba</s> and other <s>sūtras</s> were exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, then all practitioners of the <s>dharmas</s> prescribed by those <s>sūtras</s> would also be exclusively devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. But this is not observed. If one were to become a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> through the path prescribed by the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> and other [texts], then the faults of abandoning one's own <s>sūtra</s>, adopting another's <s>dharma</s>, and becoming a branch-deserter would follow — as established by such statements as 'when one's own <s>sūtra</s> exists,' 'from abandoning one's own <s>sūtra</s>,' 'he who abandons his own <s>dharma</s>,' '<s>vidharma</s> (false dharma) and <s>paradharma</s> (another's dharma),' and 'better is one's own <s>dharma</s>, however imperfect.'

children.text: "svaśāstranirṇaye satye satyāḥ syur lokanirṇayā" iti svasūtrasya prāmāṇyabuddhiś ca teṣām avarjanīyā.
children.translated_text: 'When the determination of one's own scripture is true, the determinations of the world would be true.' Thus, the conviction in the authoritativeness of their own <s>sūtra</s> is unavoidable for them.
The unbroken devotion of the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: vaikhānasānāṃ sūtrakārād ārabhya avicchinnatvena śrīmannārāyaṇaikaparatvenārādhanādikaṃ pratyakṣasiddham. tathā ca sūtram, "gṛhe devāyatane vā bhaktyā bhagavantaṃ nārāyaṇam arcayet tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ gacchatīti vijñāyate" iti*{787}*.
children.translated_text: For the <s>Vaikhānasas</s>, from the author of the <s>sūtra</s> onward, the unbroken exclusive devotion to <s>Śrīmannārāyaṇa</s> in worship and other matters is established by direct perception. And thus the <s>sūtra</s> [states]: 'Whether at home or in a temple, one should worship the Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with devotion. It is known that [such a person] goes to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'

children.text: itareṣv āpastambādiṣu pitṛ pitāmaha mātula mātāmaha putra pautra bhrātṛ sambandhiṣu kecic chaivāḥ kecid pāśupatāḥ kecic chāktāḥ nānādevatāparāś cetyevamākāreṇa dṛśyate.
children.translated_text: Among the others — those following <s>Āpastamba</s> and other [<s>sūtras</s>] — among their fathers, grandfathers, maternal uncles, maternal grandfathers, sons, grandsons, and brothers, some are seen to be <s>Śaivas</s>, some <s>Pāśupatas</s>, some <s>Śāktas</s>, and some devoted to various deities.
'In thousands of subsequent births, through austerity, knowledge, and <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption),
devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> arises in men whose sins have been exhausted.' //

children.text: iti keṣāñcit svakṛtapūrvapuṇyaviśeṣān nārāyaṇaparatvasambhave 'pi svasūtrakāram ārabhya svaparyantam avicchinnatvena tad astīti vaktuṃ na śakyate. ataḥ -
children.translated_text: Thus, although it is possible for some to become devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> through the special merit of their past good deeds, it cannot be said that such [devotion] exists in an unbroken line from the author of their <s>sūtra</s> down to themselves. Therefore —
'Those whose knowledge has been destroyed by various desires, who worship various deities,

children.text: narā bhagavat aikantye na sthāsyanti kalau yuge // [VāyuP]
children.translated_text: such men will not remain steadfast in exclusive devotion to the Lord in the <s>Kali Yuga</s>.' // [<s>Vāyu Purāṇa</s>]
'Through scripture, inference, direct perception, and reasoning,
having examined carefully with the intellect, it should be accepted with faith by the wise.' // [<s>Vāyu Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: iti vāyupurāṇādivacanād āgamādibhir nipuṇaṃ parīkṣya nirṇīta evārthaḥ vipaścidbhiḥ anuṣṭheyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, from statements in the <s>Vāyu Purāṇa</s> and other texts, the matter that has been carefully examined and determined through scripture and other means should be practiced by the wise.
The supremacy of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: nanu - kiṃ arthaṃ nārāyaṇaikaparatvena sūtraṃ praṇītam iti cet - ucyate. nārāyaṇa*{788}* akhilajagadekakāraṇatvāt paraṃbrahmaparamātmādiśabdavācyatvāt apavargādiphalapradatvāt samābhyadhikarahitatvāc ca nārāyaṇaikaparatvena praṇītam. atra - "nārāyaṇād ru*{789}* jāyate. nārāyaṇād indro jāyate. nārāyaṇād dvādaśādityāḥ rudrā vasavas sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni. nārāyaṇād eva samudpadyante. nārāyaṇāt pralīyante" ityādyāḥ "nārāyaṇaparaṃ brahme"ty ārabhya "antarbahiś ca tatsarvaṃ vyāpya nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ" ity ādyāḥ, "tam eva vidvān amṛta iha bhavati. nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyate" "utāmṛtatvasyeśānaḥ" ityādyāḥ, "na tasya kāryaṃ karaṇañ ca vidyate" "na tatsamaścābhyadhikaś ca dṛśyate" "parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca" ityādyāḥ, "eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ" ityādyāḥ, "eko ha vai nārāyaṇa āsīt" ityādyāḥ, "yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante. yena jātāni jīvanti. yatprayanty abhisaṃviśanti. tadvijijñāsasva. tad brahme"ti "patiṃ viśvasyātmeśvaram" ityādyāś ca śrutayaḥ pramāṇam.
children.translated_text: Now — if it is asked: for what purpose was the <s>sūtra</s> composed with exclusive devotion to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>? — it is stated: because <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the sole cause of the entire world, because he is denoted by the words <s>Parabrahman</s> (Supreme <s>Brahman</s>) and <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), because he bestows <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) and other fruits, and because he is devoid of equals and superiors. Here, the following <s>Śruti</s> texts are the authority: 'From <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Rudra</s> is born. From <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Indra</s> is born. From <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and all beings [are born]. From <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone they arise. In <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> they dissolve.' And beginning with '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' through to '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> stands pervading all that, both within and without.' And 'The wise one who knows Him becomes immortal here; there is no other path for going [to liberation].' 'He alone is the lord of immortality.' And 'No work or instrument of his is found,' 'nothing is seen equal to or greater than Him,' 'His supreme power is heard to be of various kinds — knowledge, strength, and action are inherent [in Him].' And 'This is the inner Self of all beings, the divine god, the one <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.' And 'Only <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> existed [before creation].' And 'That from which these beings are born, by which once born they live, into which they enter at dissolution — seek to know That, That is <s>Brahman</s>.' And 'The lord of the universe, the ruler of the Self.'

children.text: !{787}! Bezug auf VaikhSmS 4.12: dvijātir atandrito nityaṃ gṛhe devāyatane vā bhaktyā bhagavantaṃ nārāyaṇam arcayet. tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ gacchatīti vijñāyate.
children.translated_text: [Footnote 787] Reference to <s>Vaikhānasasmārtasūtra</s> 4.12: 'A twice-born person, unwearied, should always worship the Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with devotion, whether at home or in a temple. It is known that [such a person] goes to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'
The absence of supremacy-of-<s>Rudra</s> doctrine in the <s>Śvetāśvatara</s> and other texts

children.text: nanu - śvetāśvatare - "eko hi rudro na dvitīyāya tasthe - ya imān lokān īśata īśanībhiḥ*{790}* - viśvādhiko rudro maharṣiḥ*{791}* - hiraṇyagarbhaṃ janayāmāsa pūrvaṃ sa no buddhyā śubhayā saṃyunaktu*{792}* - "umāsahāyaṃ paramaṃ maheśvaraṃ triyambakaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ praśāntam. jñātvā munir gacchati bhūtayoniṃ samastasākṣiṃ tamasaḥ parastāt" ityādibhiḥ rudrasyāpi jagatkāraṇatvādi pratipādyata iti cet - ucyate. āpātato rudraparatvenāvagamyamāne 'pi vicāryamāṇe nārāyaṇaparatvam eva. eka eva rudra ity anupapannam. "sahasrāṇi sahasraśo ye rudrā" ityādi śrutibhiḥ "ekādaśarudrā" ityādibhiś ca anekarudrāṇāṃ vidyamānatvāvagamāt krūrasya rudraśabdavācyasya "bṛhattvāt bṛṃhaṇatvāc ca tadbrahmeti prakīrtitam" iti brahmaśabdavācyatvāsambhavāt, "teṣām asurāṇāṃ tisraḥ pura āsann" ity ārabhya, "idam asiṣyatīti rudram abruvan rudro vai krūras so 'syatviti. so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai aham eva paśūnām adhipatirasāv iti tasmād rudraḥ paśūnām adhipatir iti" "rudro vā akāmayata paśumān syām iti - "mātā rudrāṇāṃ duhitā vasūnām" iti. paśupatitvayācakatvāt. "naiva devo na martyaḥ. na rājā varuṇo vibhuḥ. nāgnirnendro na pavamānaḥ.
children.translated_text: Now — if it is objected that in the <s>Śvetāśvatara</s> [Upaniṣad], by statements such as '<s>Rudra</s> is indeed one; they do not stand for a second — he who rules these worlds with his ruling powers,' 'The great sage <s>Rudra</s>, superior to the universe,' '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> he brought forth first; may he unite us with auspicious intelligence,' and 'Having known the supreme great Lord (<s>Paramamaheśvara</s>), companion of <s>Umā</s>, the three-eyed, blue-throated, peaceful one — the sage goes to the source of beings, the witness of all, beyond darkness' — <s>Rudra</s> too is established as the cause of the world, etc. — it is stated: Even though at first glance it may be understood as teaching the supremacy of <s>Rudra</s>, upon careful examination it [teaches] the supremacy of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone. [The statement] '<s>Rudra</s> is indeed one' is untenable, because the existence of many <s>Rudras</s> is understood from <s>Śruti</s> texts such as 'thousands upon thousands of <s>Rudras</s>' and 'the eleven <s>Rudras</s>.' It is impossible for the cruel one denoted by the word <s>Rudra</s> to be denoted by the word <s>Brahman</s>, since 'Because of [its] greatness and because [it] causes to grow, it is called <s>Brahman</s>.' [Further,] beginning from 'Those <s>Asuras</s> had three cities' through to 'They called him <s>Rudra</s>, saying "this one will be feared." He said: "I choose a boon — I alone shall be the lord of animals." Therefore <s>Rudra</s> is the lord of animals,' and '<s>Rudra</s> desired: may I possess animals,' and 'the mother of the <s>Rudras</s>, the daughter of the <s>Vasus</s>' — because he begged for lordship over animals. 'Neither god nor mortal, not king <s>Varuṇa</s> the mighty, not <s>Agni</s>, not <s>Indra</s>, not <s>Pavamāna</s> (the Wind),

! ŚvetU 3.4: yo devānāṃ prabhavaś codbhavaś ca viśvādhipo rudro maharṣiḥ.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 790] <s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 3.2: '<s>Rudra</s> is indeed one; they do not stand for a second — he who rules these worlds with his ruling powers.'
The absence of equality of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: mātṛkkaś ca na vidyate - ity ārabhya "etad rudrasya dhanuḥ. rudrasyatvena dhanurārtniḥ. śira utpipeṣa. sa pravargyo 'bhavat. tasmād yas sapravargyeṇa yajñena yajate. rudrasya sa śiraḥ pratidhāti. nainaṃ rudra āruko bhavati" ity uktatvāc ca rudrasya brahmaśabdavācyatvaṃ na sambhavati. rudra hara paśupati nīlagrīva śitikaṇṭha bhava śarva kapardītyādīnām ekatvena śruyamāṇānām ekatvaṃ na sambhavati. īśvara maheśvara paramamaheśvara iti paramamaheśvaraśabdaśravaṇāt. "śiva eko dhyeyaḥ śivaśśaṅkaraḥ sarvam anyatparityajye" tyādinā śivaśabdavācyād adhikatvena śivataraśivatamaśabdavācyasya vidyamānatvāt. śambhuśabdasya viśvaśambhutvaśravaṇāt īśānasya jagadīśānatvaśravaṇāt mahādevasya "tamīśvarāṇāṃ paramaṃ maheśvaraṃ taṃ devatānāṃ paramañ ca daivatam" iti śravaṇāc ca rudrādīnāṃ paraṃbrahmaśabdavācyatvaṃ na sambhavati.
children.translated_text: [continuing] 'and no mother is found' — beginning thus — 'That is the bow of <s>Rudra</s>. By the bowstring of <s>Rudra</s>, he crushed the head. That became the <s>Pravargya</s> rite. Therefore, he who sacrifices with the sacrifice that includes the <s>Pravargya</s> restores the head of <s>Rudra</s>. <s>Rudra</s> does not become hostile to him.' Because of such statements, it is not possible for <s>Rudra</s> to be denoted by the word <s>Brahman</s>. The unity of those heard as one — <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Nīlagrīva</s>, <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Kapardī</s>, etc. — is not possible. Because the word <s>Paramamaheśvara</s> (Supreme Great Lord) is heard [along with the words] <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Paramamaheśvara</s>. Because, since 'the one <s>Śiva</s> is to be meditated upon, <s>Śiva</s> who is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, abandoning everything else' — [there exists] one superior to the one denoted by the word <s>Śiva</s>, namely the one denoted by the words <s>Śivatara</s> (more auspicious) and <s>Śivatama</s> (most auspicious). Because the word <s>Śambhu</s> is heard [to mean] 'beneficent to the universe.' Because the word <s>Īśāna</s> is heard [to mean] 'ruler of the world.' Because of the hearing of <s>Mahādeva</s>: 'Him, the supreme great lord of lords, him, the supreme deity of deities' — therefore, it is not possible for <s>Rudra</s> and others to be denoted by the words <s>Parabrahman</s> (Supreme <s>Brahman</s>).

children.text: nanu - śvetāśvatare - umāsahayaviśeṣita paramamaheśvaraśabdavācyasya rudratvasambhavāt paraṃbrahmaśabdavācyatvaṃ tasya sambhavatīti cet - na. paramamaheśvaraśabdasya umāsahāyam ity atra rudrādiṣv anupapannatvāt. ukārastvavadhāraṇārthaḥ. u - mā sahāyaṃ lakṣmīsahāyaṃ paramaṃ maheśvaram eva trilocanatvādiviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭhaṃ lakṣmīnarasiṃhaṃ dhyātvetyarthaḥ. yadvā. devamanuṣyādyapekṣayā paramamaheśvaratvāt,
children.translated_text: Now — if it is objected that in the <s>Śvetāśvatara</s>, since the word <s>Paramamaheśvara</s>, qualified by being the companion of <s>Umā</s>, can denote <s>Rudra</s>, therefore he can be denoted by the word <s>Parabrahman</s> — no. Because the word <s>Paramamaheśvara</s> is inapplicable to <s>Rudra</s> and others in the phrase '<s>umāsahāyam</s>' (companion of <s>Umā</s>). The syllable 'u' is used in the sense of emphatic restriction. 'U-mā sahāyam' means 'the supreme great lord whose companion is <s>Lakṣmī</s>' — the meaning is that one should meditate on <s>Lakṣmī-Narasiṃha</s>, who is qualified by the attribute of having three eyes and so forth. Alternatively, he is the supreme great lord relative to gods, humans, and others,
'He who takes on the functions of creation, sustenance, and dissolution — [functioning as] <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: sa saṃjñāṃ yāti bhagavān eka eva janārdanaḥ //"
children.translated_text: that one Lord <s>Janārdana</s> alone assumes these designations.' //

children.text: iti bhagavaccharīrabhūtatvāc ca rudrasya paramamaheśvaratvam. evaṃ bhūtaṃ rudraṃ dhyātvā munir mananaśīlassan bhūtayoniṃ sarvakāraṇakāraṇaṃ samstarakṣakaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt gacchati. "ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastād" ityādibhiḥ tamasaḥ pāravartinaṃ prakṛteḥ paraṃ paramātmānaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ gacchati - prāpnoti ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: Because <s>Rudra</s> is a body of the Lord — therefore <s>Rudra</s> possesses the status of <s>Paramamaheśvara</s> [only derivatively]. Having meditated on <s>Rudra</s>, who is of this nature, the sage — one whose nature is contemplation — goes to the Source of beings, the cause of all causes, the protector of all, beyond darkness. By [texts] such as 'Of the color of the sun, beyond darkness' — the meaning is that he goes to, i.e. attains, the Supreme Self <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is beyond darkness, beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).

children.text: kiñca - atra: sano devaḥ śubhayā smṛtyā saṃyunaktu. ity anena
children.translated_text: Moreover — here [in the verse]: 'May that god unite us with auspicious meditation' — by this,
'One should desire health from the Sun, one should desire wealth from <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: śaṅkarāt jñānam anvicchet mokṣam icchej janārdanāt //"
children.translated_text: one should desire knowledge from <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and one should desire liberation from <s>Janārdana</s>.' //

children.text: iti jñānapradatvāt śaṅkaropāsanam ucyate. ato bhagavatā nārāyaṇena sāmyaṃ brahmarudrādīnāṃ nopapadyate.
children.translated_text: Because [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] grants knowledge, the worship of <s>Śaṅkara</s> is prescribed [in certain contexts]. Therefore, equality of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others with the Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is not tenable.
In the <s>Mahābhārata</s>: 'Those who regard the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>) as equal [to other gods],
they should be known as heretics (<s>pāṣaṇḍas</s>), excluded from all rites.' // [MBh]
The misfortune of those who disrespect <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> by equating him with <s>Rudra</s> and others
'He who regards the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as equal [to other gods],

children.text: sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ yāvac candrādivākaram // [MB.h ]
children.translated_text: goes to a terrible hell for as long as the sun and moon [endure].' // [MBh]
'He who, evil-minded, even once calls the great <s>Viṣṇu</s> equal to an inferior deity,
he is an outcaste — and [even] an outcaste is not [such] an outcaste.' // [MBh]

children.text: vārāhe: "anyadevasamaṃ ye tu manyante māṃ narādhamāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Varāha</s> [Purāṇa]: 'Those lowest of men who regard Me as equal to another god,

children.text: caṇḍālatāṃ vrajanty āśu janmani nava pañca ca //" iti [VarāhaP]
children.translated_text: quickly attain the state of a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) for fourteen births.' // Thus. [<s>Varāha Purāṇa</s>]
In the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> [Purāṇa]: 'He who disrespects the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> by regarding him as equal,
by even a single such disrespect, does not escape from hell.' // [<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: asmād anyaṃ paratvena cintayāno hy acetanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who, being senseless, contemplates someone other than Him as supreme,
should be known as a heretic (<s>pāṣaṇḍin</s>), excluded from all rites.' // Thus. [<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s>]
In the <s>Kūrma</s> [Purāṇa]: 'Those who, deluded by ignorance, declare another god as supreme

children.text: nārāyaṇāj jagannāthāt te vai pāṣaṇḍinaḥ smṛtāḥ // [KūrmaP ]
children.translated_text: over <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Lord of the world — they are indeed regarded as heretics.' // [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s>]
'He who regards the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as equal to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and other deities,

children.text: samatvenaiva vīkṣeta sa pāṣaṇḍī bhaved dvijaḥ //" iti [KūrmaP ]
children.translated_text: that twice-born person becomes a heretic.' // Thus. [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s>]
<s>Bhāradvāja</s> [says]: '<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others are impure, they are <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), manifestations of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tān vai kudṛṣṭayas samyak paratvenāpy upāsate //" iti
children.translated_text: Those of false views worship them as supreme.' // Thus.
In the <s>Varāha</s> [Purāṇa]: <s>Rudra</s> [speaking] to <s>Agastya</s>:

children.text: "yo yajñair ijyate devo yasmāt sarvam idaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: 'The god who is worshipped through sacrifices, from whom this entire world
has arisen, in whom all [things] both moving and unmoving always dissolve, // [<s>Varāha Purāṇa</s>]
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the supreme god, <s>Janārdana</s> whose nature is <s>sattva</s> (pure goodness).
That Lord, the Supreme Ruler, created himself in a threefold form. // [<s>Varāha Purāṇa</s>]
As pure <s>sattva</s>, he himself was born; the all-pervading one
created <s>Brahmā</s>, seated on the lotus, in [his] navel-lotus, // [<s>Varāha Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: rajasā tamasā yuktaṃ so 'pi māṃ sasṛje prabhur //" iti [VarāhaP]
children.translated_text: endowed with <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>tamas</s> (darkness); and that lord in turn created me.' // Thus. [<s>Varāha Purāṇa</s>]
[Textual variant note:] Read: 'mahāviṣṇum' (great <s>Viṣṇu</s>).
Objection: "Destroying all sins here, and hereafter destroying <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth),
with gold, silver, copper, and the like, and also with iron, // [<s>VarāhaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: tathā rayāṅgam*{796}* aṣṭāṅgaṃ sunābhañ ca suvṛttakam /
children.translated_text: and likewise making the disc-shaped, eight-spoked, well-hubbed, and circular [<s>cakra</s>],
furnished with four flames, according to the prescribed procedure, // [<s>VarāhaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: agnau pratāpya vidhivat dhārayed bhaktisaṃyutaḥ //" iti [VarāhaP]
children.translated_text: having heated it in the fire as prescribed, one should bear it with devotion." Thus. [<s>VarāhaPurāṇa</s>]
"Sacrifice, gift, austerity, <s>homa</s> (fire-oblation), feeding, and gratification of ancestors —
for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who lacks the mark of the <s>cakra</s> (discus-brand), [all these] become fruitless. // [<s>VarāhaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: śrāddhe dāne vrate yajñe vivāhe copanāyane /
children.translated_text: At <s>śrāddha</s>s, gifts, vows, sacrifices, marriages, and <s>upanayana</s>s,

children.text: cakrāṅkitaṃ vipram eva pūjayed aparaṃ na tu //" [VarāhaP]
children.translated_text: one should honor only a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> marked with the <s>cakra</s> — not another." [<s>VarāhaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: ityādivacanaiḥ cakrādinānaṅkitasya*{797}* vaiṣṇavatvābhāvāt vaikhānasānāṃ*{798}* kathaṃ vā vaiṣṇavatvam iti cet - ucyate.
children.translated_text: If, by these and other statements, [it is argued that] because one unmarked by the <s>cakra</s> and other [emblems] lacks <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> status, how can the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s have <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> status? — To this it is replied:
The <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> status of <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s even without being marked by the <s>cakra</s> and other emblems

children.text: "yasya me śriyam amitāṃ dātuṃ garbha eva kare cakraṃ dhārayāmi sa cakravartī bhavati" iti śruteḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Śruti</s>: "In whose hand I place the <s>cakra</s> (discus) while yet in the womb, in order to bestow upon him my boundless prosperity — he becomes a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch)."
"For all <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s, who are <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>s from the womb,

children.text: nārāyaṇaḥ svayaṃ garbhe mudrāṃ dhārayate nijām* //{799}*" iti
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself places His own mark (<s>mudrā</s>) in the womb." Thus.
"Having uttered '<s>Sudarśanam</s>' as the invocation, one should bear the <s>Sudarśana</s> [emblem] on the right [hand];

children.text: ravipām iti vāme tu śaṅkhañ ca bibhṛyāt kare* //{800}*"
children.translated_text: with '<s>Ravipām</s>' [as the invocation], one should bear the <s>Śaṅkha</s> (conch) on the left hand."
The <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> status of <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s from the womb

children.text: iti bhṛguṇoktatvāc ca śrīviṣṇubalikarmaṇā vaikhānasānāṃ garbhavaiṣṇavatvādikaṃ pratipannam.
children.translated_text: Because it is thus stated by <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and through the <s>Śrīviṣṇubalikarman</s> (offering ritual to <s>Viṣṇu</s>), the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> status of <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s from the womb and related matters are established.

children.text: tathā*{801}*: "indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā hy arthebhyaś ca paraṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise: "Beyond the sense-objects are the senses; beyond the objects is the mind;

children.text: manasas tu parā buddhir buddher ātmā mahān paraḥ //
children.translated_text: beyond the mind is the intellect; beyond the intellect is the great self (<s>Mahān Ātmā</s>). //

children.text: mahataḥ param avyaktam avyaktāt puruṣaḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: Beyond the great is the unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>); beyond the unmanifest is the <s>Puruṣa</s>;

children.text: puruṣān na paraṃ kiñcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ //"
children.translated_text: beyond the <s>Puruṣa</s> there is nothing — that is the limit, that is the supreme goal." //
The possibility of <s>prapatti</s> (self-surrender) for one still in the womb

children.text: iti śruteḥ paramaikāntitvaṃ paramapuruṣavaśīkaraṇadvārā garbhagatasya prapattir api sambhavati.
children.translated_text: From this <s>Śruti</s>, supreme exclusive devotion — [and] through the means of bringing the Supreme Person under one's allegiance, <s>prapatti</s> (self-surrender) is also possible for one still in the womb.

children.text: garbhagatasya prapattir api garbhopaniṣadi śrūyate. "jñānād dhyanād akṣaram oṅkāraḥ cintayati."*{802}*
children.translated_text: The <s>prapatti</s> of one in the womb is also heard in the <s>Garbhopaniṣad</s>: "Through knowledge, through meditation, he contemplates the imperishable syllable <s>Oṃ</s>."

children.text: ! Dieser Vers ist auch als "Purātantra" in DHN[D] 36.22-23 zitiert; der zweite Halbvers ist auch in KrA 36.43ab enthalten. Vgl. ĀS 16.33 (Nārāyaṇa spricht zu Vikhanas): tvadvaṃśajānāṃ sarveṣāṃ garbhavaiṣṇavajanmanāṃ / ahaṃ eva svayaṃ garbhe manmudrāṃ dhārayāṃy ahaṃ ; vgl. ĀS 19.12: vaikhānasānāṃ sarveṣāṃ garbhavaiṣṇavajanmanāṃ / aham eva svayaṃ garbhe mannudrāṃ dhārayāmi tāṃ.
! ĀS 11.6: śaṅkhaṃ ca bibhṛyād iti; dieser Vers ist auch als "Bhagavacchāstra" in DHN[D] 106.20-21 zitiert.
! DHN[T] 609 statt DHN[D] 103.18-19: iti bhṛguṇoktatvāc ca śrīviṣṇubalikarmaṇā garbhavaiṣṇavatvādikaṃ.
! Bezug auf GarbhaU 3.10: pañcātmakaḥ samarthaḥ pañcātmikā cetasā buddhir gandharasādijñānā dhyyānāt kṣaram akṣaraṃ mokṣaṃ cintayatīti /. DHN[T] 610: oṅkāraṃ cintayatīty.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 796: DHN[T] 607: <s>rathāṅgam</s> (chariot-wheel, i.e., discus).]

children.text: ity uktvā "atha navame māsi sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇo bhavati. pūrvajātiṃ smarati. kṛtākṛtañ ca karma bhavati. śubhāśubhañ ca karma vindati."*{803}*
children.translated_text: Having stated thus, [the <s>Upaniṣad</s> continues:] "Then, in the ninth month, [the fetus] becomes complete in all characteristics. It remembers its previous births. It knows both the done and the undone <s>karma</s>. It perceives both auspicious and inauspicious <s>karma</s>."
"Thousands of various wombs have been seen by me;

children.text: āhārā vividhā bhuktāḥ pītāś ca vividhāḥ stanāḥ // [Garbha.U 4.1]
children.translated_text: various foods have been consumed, and various breasts have been suckled. // [<s>GarbhaUpaniṣad</s> 4.1]

children.text: jātasyaiva mṛtasyaiva janma caiva punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Born and dying, and birth again and again —

children.text: aho duḥkho dadhau magno na paśyāmi pratikriyām //" ityuktvā [GarbhaU 4.2]
children.translated_text: alas, submerged in the ocean of suffering, I see no remedy." // Having said thus, [<s>GarbhaUpaniṣad</s> 4.2]
"If I am released from this womb, I shall take refuge in <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
the destroyer of all inauspiciousness, the bestower of the fruit of liberation." // Thus. [<s>GarbhaUpaniṣad</s> 4.6]

children.text: *{807}*puruṣasūktabhāṣye - mudgalopaniṣadi - "vāmadevo 'py āṅgirasas san pūrvapūjāṃ samārātriṃ patnyanasūyāgarbha eva śayāno brahmaiva vedayāñ cakre sa garbhaṃ puro bhitvā brahmalokam upacakrāma tam utkrāmāntam āha madhye 'dhvānam indraḥ upaniṣada uvāca, bhagavan garbhapañjare evābhiniveśamāna anabhijñātopāyo 'smāt kiñcid dhādityā sa garbhas sarvo manyamāno 'dhvanaḥ pāram upagacchasī"tyādi. tathā ca garbhagatasya prapadanavicāraśravaṇādyupapadyata eva.
children.translated_text: In the commentary on the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> — in the <s>Mudgalopaniṣad</s> — "<s>Vāmadeva</s>, being of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> [lineage], while lying in the womb of his mother <s>Anasūyā</s>, having performed the earlier worship throughout the night (<s>samārātri</s>), knew <s>Brahman</s> itself. He broke through the womb and ascended to the world of <s>Brahman</s>. As he was departing, <s>Indra</s> addressed him midway on the path: '<s>Bhagavan</s>, while abiding in the prison of the womb, unaware of the means [of escape], how do you, considering yourself as the entirety of the embryo, reach the far shore of the path?' and so forth. Thus, investigation of <s>prapatti</s>, hearing, and so forth are indeed possible for one in the womb.
The twofold nature of <s>prapatti</s> as Vedic and <s>tāntrika</s>

children.text: vaidikatāntrikabhedena prapattir dvividhā - praṇavapūrvakatvena puruṣādyāvāhanādikaṃ vaidikam.
children.translated_text: <s>Prapatti</s> (self-surrender) is of two kinds according to the distinction between Vedic and <s>tāntrika</s> — the Vedic consists of the invocation of <s>Puruṣa</s> and others preceded by the syllable <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>).
Definition of Vedic <s>prapatti</s>
In another <s>Śruti</s>: "By the syllable 'a' is denoted <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Hari</s>, the lord of all worlds;
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, who was raised up by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is likewise denoted by the syllable 'u';

children.text: makāras tu tayor dāsa iti praṇavalakṣaṇam* //{808}*" iti
children.translated_text: the syllable 'ma' denotes their servant — such is the definition of <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>)." Thus.

children.text: kiñca. praṇavoccāraṇamātreṇa śaṅkhacakrādidhāraṇam api sambhavatīti śruyate*{809}*.
children.translated_text: Moreover, it is heard [in <s>Śruti</s>] that even the bearing of the conch, discus, and other [emblems] is possible by the mere utterance of the <s>Praṇava</s>.

children.text: kaivalyopaniṣadi - "dhṛtordhvapuṇḍraḥ kṛtacakradhārī viṣṇuṃ paraṃ dhyāyati yo mahātmā. svareṇa mantreṇa sadā hṛdisthaṃ parāt paraṃ yanmahato mahāntam." iti. sarvakāraṇabhūtāya sarvarakṣakāya sarvaśeṣiṇe śriyaḥ pataye eva svābhāvikaśeṣabhūta iti sarvadānusandhānam eva vaidikī prapattiḥ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kaivalyopaniṣad</s>: "Wearing the vertical <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> mark, bearing the <s>cakra</s> [emblem], one who meditates on the supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that great soul, with the syllable-<s>mantra</s>, always present in the heart — the one who is beyond the beyond, the great one greater than the great." Thus. Vedic <s>prapatti</s> is the constant contemplation: 'I am by nature a servant (<s>śeṣa</s>) of the Lord of <s>Śrī</s> alone, who is the cause of all, the protector of all, the master of all.'

children.text: !{803}! Bezug auf GarbhaU 3.12: atha navame māsi sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇo bhavati. pūrvajātīḥ smarati. kṛtākṛtañ ca karma bhavati. śubhāśubhañ ca karma vindati.
! Lies: nārāyaṇaṃ; DHN[T] 610 und GarbhaU 4.6: nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ.

! GarbhaU 4.4-4.7 lautet vollständig: yadi yonyāḥ pramucyāmi sāṃkhyaṃ yogam vā samāśraye / aśubhakṣayakartāraṃ phalamuktipradāyakam // yad.i yonyāḥ pramucyāmi taṃ prapadye maheśvaram / aśubhakṣayakartāraṃ phalamuktipradāyakam // yad.i yonyāḥ pramucyāmitaṃ prapadye bhagavantaṃ nārāyaṇam devam / aśubhakṣayakartāraṃ phalamuktipradāyakam // yad.i yonyāḥ pramucyāmi dhyāye brahma sanātanam //.

! DHN[T] 611 statt DHN[D] 104.9-14: puruṣasūktabhāṣye - mudgalopaniṣadi - "vāmadevo 'py āṅgīrasas san pūrvapūjāṃ samārātri patnyanasūyayā garbha eva śayāno brahmaiva vedayāñ cakre sa garbhaṃ puro bhitvā brahmalokam upacakrāma tam utkrāmantam āha madhye 'dhvānam indra upaniṣada uvāca, bhagavan garbhapañjara evābhiniveśamāno 'bhijñātopāyo 'smāt kiñcid dhādityā sa garbhas sarvo manyamāno 'dhvanaḥ pāram upagacchasī"tyādi. garbhagatasya prapadanavicāraśravaṇād upapadyata eva.
! Diese Verse sind als "Lakṣmīviśiṣṭādvaita" zitiert in Mokṣopāyapradīpikā, S. 54(1), und in Vaikhānasamahimāmāñjarī, S. 17.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 803: Reference to <s>GarbhaUpaniṣad</s> 3.12: 'Then, in the ninth month, complete in all characteristics, one remembers previous births, knows done and undone <s>karma</s>, and perceives auspicious and inauspicious <s>karma</s>.']
"If you desire the revival of the self, if you have longing for your own existence,

children.text: ātmadāsyaṃ hareḥ svāmyaṃ svabhāvañ ca sadā smara //"
children.translated_text: always remember the servitude of the self, the lordship of <s>Hari</s>, and [your] own nature." //
This is what is established in the <s>sūtra</s>.
But in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>:

children.text: "tyaktvā trayīṃ tantram eva prapadya śaraṇaṃ sthitāḥ //" iti [PādmaS caryāpāda 21.56cd]
children.translated_text: "Having abandoned the three [<s>Veda</s>s], they have taken refuge in the <s>tantra</s> alone, standing [in that]." // Thus. [<s>PādmaSaṃhitā</s>, <s>Caryāpāda</s> 21.56cd]
"For what is unattainable by other means, with great faith as the prerequisite,
the prayer that it is the sole means — [that is] <s>prapatti</s> (self-surrender), <s>śaraṇāgati</s> (taking refuge)." //

children.text: *{810}*iti ca upadiśyate. tasyāḥ prapatteḥ sakṛtkaraṇāt samantrakatvābhāvāt taccheṣagatyanusmaraṇābhāvāc ca tāṃ tāntrikaprapattiṃ vihāya "yad eva vidyayā karoti tad eva vīryavattaraṃ bhavatī"ti śrutyā vaidikaprapattim evoktavān sūtrakāraḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus it is taught. Because that <s>prapatti</s> is performed only once, because it lacks the character of being accompanied by <s>mantra</s>s, and because it lacks the recollection of the subsequent course that is auxiliary to it — setting aside that <s>tāntrika prapatti</s>, the author of the <s>Sūtra</s> has taught only Vedic <s>prapatti</s>, in accordance with the <s>Śruti</s>: 'What one does with knowledge, that indeed becomes more powerful.'
The heated <s>cakra</s> brand and other marks are not for twice-born ones
In the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa]: "For those initiated in the <s>Viṣṇu Āgama</s>s and other <s>tantra</s>s, it is prescribed —
branding with the conch, discus, mace, and other [emblems]; not for other embodied beings. // [<s>SkandaPurāṇa</s>]
For those initiated in the <s>Śiva Āgama</s>s and other [systems], the horizontal <s>tripuṇḍra</s> mark is to be worn." // Thus. [<s>SkandaPurāṇa</s>]
<s>Viṣṇu</s> [Purāṇa]: "Branding with the conch, discus, and other [emblems], as well as singing, dancing, and the like —

children.text: ekajāter ayaṃ dharmaḥ na jātu syād dvijanmanām* //{811}*" iti [ViṣṇuP ]
children.translated_text: this is the <s>dharma</s> of those of single birth (<s>ekajāti</s>, i.e., <s>Śūdra</s>s); it should never be for the twice-born." // Thus. [<s>ViṣṇuPurāṇa</s>]
In the <s>Śrībhāgavata</s>, in the tenth <s>skanda</s> (book):
"<s>Trivakrā</s>'s son <s>Upaśloka</s>, devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: śiṣyas sākṣān nāradasya dadau cittam akhaṇḍitam //
children.translated_text: a direct disciple of <s>Nārada</s>, gave his undivided mind [to the Lord]. //

children.text: tenoktaṃ sāttvataṃ tantraṃ yat jñātvā mokṣabhāg bhavet /
children.translated_text: By him was taught the <s>Sāttvata Tantra</s>, knowing which one attains liberation;

children.text: yatra strīśūdradāsānāṃ saṃskāro vaiṣṇavaḥ smṛtaḥ //" iti [BhāgavataP ]
children.translated_text: wherein the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration) for women, <s>Śūdra</s>s, and servants is prescribed." // Thus. [<s>BhāgavataPurāṇa</s>]
Definition and related matters of <s>tāntrika prapatti</s>

children.text: padmapurāṇe: "vedajñe brāhmaṇe nityaṃ sarvās tiṣṭhanti devatāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>: "In a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who knows the <s>Veda</s>s, all deities always reside;
thus it is heard in the <s>Taittirīya</s> branch, O best of kings. // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]
On the right shoulder of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s> — bearing the conch, discus, and mace — resides;

children.text: haris tiṣṭhati vāme tu devakīsūnur ādarāt // [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: and on the left, the son of <s>Devakī</s> [resides] with reverence. // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: !{810}! DHN[T] 614 statt DHN[D] 105.8-10: iti sakṛtkṛtatvāt mantrakatvābhāvāt taccheṣagatyanusmaraṇābhāvāc. (yad eva vidyayā karoti tad eva vīryavattaraṃ bhavatī"ti śrutyā tāntrikaprapattiṃ vihāya vaidikaprapatti)m evoktavān.
! DHN[T] 614: ekajātīr ayaṃ dharmo na jātus syād dvijanmanām.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 810: DHN[T] 614 instead of DHN[D] 105.8-10: 'Thus, because it is performed only once, because it lacks the character of [being accompanied by] <s>mantra</s>s, because it lacks the recollection of the subsequent course. (Setting aside the <s>tāntrika prapatti</s> by the <s>Śruti</s> "What one does with knowledge, that becomes more powerful," he taught only Vedic <s>prapatti</s>.)']
Therefore this body of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is called the temple of the deities;

children.text: taddāhe devatās sarve palāyante diśo daśa // [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: when it is burned, all the deities flee in the ten directions. // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]
The qualified persons for the rite of heated <s>cakra</s>-branding, etc.
He who burns [the body of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] would become a burner of [the divine] abode — that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-burner is the lowest;

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ mṛdā yas tu kuryāt taptāyasena vā // [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: one who applies the conch and discus with clay or heated iron, // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]
he should be excluded like a <s>Śūdra</s> from all twice-born rites;
just as wood from a cremation-ground is unfit for all [ritual] purposes, // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: tathā cakrāṅkito vipras sarvakarmasu garhitaḥ //" iti. [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: so a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> branded with the <s>cakra</s> is condemned in all rites." Thus. [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: tatraiva: "mohād vā lobhato vāpi vipraś cakrāṅkito yadi /
children.translated_text: In the same [text]: "If a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, whether from delusion or from greed, is branded with the <s>cakra</s>,

children.text: anarhas sa hi vijñeyaḥ śrautasmārteṣu karmasu // [Padma.P ]
children.translated_text: he is to be known as unfit for <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> rites. // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: kriyāsv anarhatām eti yathā kāṣṭhaṃ śmaśānagam /
children.translated_text: He becomes unfit for [all] rites, just as wood from a cremation-ground;
likewise, those burned by the <s>cakra</s> and other [brands] become unfit for all rites. // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]
Wherever there is one whose body is half-burned — in a village or in a district —

children.text: śmaśānaṃ tad dhi vijñeyaṃ vāsānarhaṃ dvijanmanām //" [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: that [place] should be known as a cremation-ground, unfit for the dwelling of twice-born ones." // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]

children.text: ityādinā dūṣaṇam uktam. etāni taptacakrāṅkanavidhāyakāni vacanāni "viṣṇvāgamāditantreṣu dīkṣitānām" ity uktatvāt ekajātiviṣayatvenoktatvāt "nānyadehinām" ityuktatvāc ca tāntrikāgamoktaprakāreṇa dīkṣitaviṣayāṇīty*{813}* avagamyate.
children.translated_text: Thus the censure is stated by these and other [passages]. These statements that prescribe the heated <s>cakra</s>-branding are understood to pertain [only] to those initiated in the manner prescribed by the <s>tāntrika Āgama</s>s — because it is said 'for those initiated in the <s>Viṣṇu Āgama</s>s and other <s>tantra</s>s,' because it is said to pertain to those of single birth (<s>ekajāti</s>), and because it is said 'not for other embodied beings.'

children.text: yadvā vidhiniṣedhavacanānāṃ vaiyarthyaparihārāya "vapāśrapaṇībhyām*{814}* anvārabhate tannaivānvārabdhaṃ naivānanvārabdhaṃ"*{815}* "avaghreyam eva tat naiva prāśitaṃ naivāprāśitam" ityādi śrutinyāyena samantrakatvena bhāvanārūpeṇa śrīvaikhānasaśāstre pratipāditam.*{816}*. yathā:
children.translated_text: Alternatively, in order to avoid the purposelessness of both prescriptive and prohibitive statements, it is established in the <s>Śrīvaikhānasa Śāstra</s> in the form of meditation accompanied by <s>mantra</s>s, following the <s>Śruti</s> principle: 'One grasps the <s>vapā</s> offering; it is neither grasped nor not-grasped'; 'It is to be smelled only; it is neither consumed nor not-consumed' — and so forth. As follows:
"Having uttered '<s>Sudarśanam</s>' as the invocation, one should bear the <s>Sudarśana</s> [emblem] on the right [hand];

children.text: ravipām iti vāme ca śaṅkhañ ca bibhṛyāt kare* //{817}*" iti
children.translated_text: with '<s>Ravipām</s>' [as invocation], one should bear the conch on the left hand." //
In the <s>Mahopaniṣad</s> — in the <s>Brahmasūkta</s>:

children.text: "dakṣiṇe tu bhuje vipro bibhṛyād vai sudarśanam /
children.translated_text: "On the right arm, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should bear the <s>Sudarśana</s> [emblem];

children.text: savye tu śaṅkhaṃ bibhṛyād iti vedavido viduḥ* //{818}*" iti.
children.translated_text: on the left, he should bear the conch — thus the knowers of the <s>Veda</s> know." //

children.text: ! Bezug auf TS 6.3.8.2.1: paśur iti yan nānvārabheta suvargāl lokād yajamāno hīyeta vapāśrapaṇībhyām anvārabhate tan nevānvārabdhaṃ nevānanvārabdham.
! Anmerkung im Devanāgarī-Text: pratipāditam iti. vidhivacanānāṃ bhāvanārūpeṇānuṣṭhānaṃ, niṣedhavacanānāṃ tāparūpeṇānuṣṭhānaṃ ca tātparyārthaḥ iti ubhayaṃ saṃgacchata iti bhāvaḥ.
! ĀS 11.6: ravipām iti vāme tu śaṅkhaṃ ca bibhṛyād iti; dieser Vers ist auch zitiert in DHN[D] 103.16-18.
! Dieser Vers ist ähnlich in PadmaP uttarabhāga 224.57 zitiert (dort statt savye lies vāme) und in Vṛddhahārītasmṛti 2.38cd/39ab als "Śruti" zitiert. DHN[T] 618: brahmavido statt vedavido.

children.translated_text: [Footnote 812: DHN[T] 615: <s>śmaśānagaṃ</s>.]
The non-universal applicability of the heated <s>cakra</s>-bearing prescribed in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>
The <s>Pāñcarātra</s> and other [systems
as deluding scriptures]

children.text: mohaśāstratvāt śaptaviṣayatvāc ca pañcarātre tāpavidhānaṃ uktam iti kecit vadanti.*{819}*
children.translated_text: Some say that the procedure of branding in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> was taught because it is a deluding <s>śāstra</s> and because it pertains to those who are cursed.

children.text: padmapurāṇe gautama: "yan mayi brāhmaṇābhāsāḥ ṛjau kaitavam īdṛśam /
children.translated_text: In the <s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>, <s>Gautama</s> [speaks]: "What deceit of this kind has been practiced upon me by those who resemble <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s!
Therefore they are sinners, fallen from the Vedic path, // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]
initiated into the <s>Kālamukha</s>, <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, <s>Kālapāla</s>, <s>Śāmbhava</s>,

children.text: śākte ca dīkṣitā yūyaṃ bhavata brāhmaṇādhamāḥ //" iti [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: and <s>Śākta</s> [systems] — you have become the lowest of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s." Thus. [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]
<s>Brahmā</s> [speaks]: "Those twice-born ones initiated into the Buddhist, <s>Bhāgavata</s>, and third, the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> <s>tantra</s>s,

children.text: dīkṣitāś ca dvijā nityaṃ bhaveyur nirbhayā hare // [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: may they forever become fearless, O <s>Hari</s>! // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]
In the <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> conduct, which is auspicious and grants immediate liberation,
may they be forever averse to devotion to You, deluded! // [<s>PadmaPurāṇa</s>]
With the conch, discus of <s>Vikhanas</s>, mace, <s>vajra</s>, noose, goad, and other [emblems],

children.text: aṅkitāḥ śraddhayā yūyaṃ bhavata brāhmaṇādhamāḥ //" iti [PadmaP ]
children.translated_text: You who are branded are the lowest of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>!" Thus [in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>].
In the <s>Skānda</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] — in the <s>Sūtasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Rudra</s> [speaks] to <s>Sarasvatī</s>:

children.text: "śrutir balīyasīty uktā pramāṇānāṃ sulocane" ity ārabhya [SkandaP ]
children.translated_text: "<s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) has been declared the strongest among the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), O beautiful-eyed one," beginning thus, [<s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>]
"The Vedic rootedness of the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> and other paths is [accepted] by the orthodox;

children.text: na hi svatantratas tena bhrāntimūlāni rūpiṇi // [SkandaP ]
children.translated_text: For they are not independently rooted in delusion, O embodied one. [<s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>]
Nevertheless, that portion of the path which does not contradict the Vedic [way],

children.text: so 'ṃśaḥ pramāṇam ity uktaṃ keṣāñcid adhikāriṇām // [SkandaP ]
children.translated_text: that portion is declared to be authoritative — for certain qualified persons. [<s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>]
But for beings who have completely fallen from the Vedic path,
the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> and other paths are beneficial merely in the course of time;

children.text: tāntrikāṇāṃ mahādevi na labhyo 'vyavadhānataḥ //" iti pratipāditam. [SkandaP ]
children.translated_text: for those who follow <s>Tantric</s> [practices], O <s>Mahādevī</s>, [liberation] is not attainable directly." Thus it is established. [<s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>]
In the <s>Kaurma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]: "Formerly in the sacred <s>Dāruvana</s> (pine forest), the sages who were householders —" [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.97ab]

children.text: ity ārabhya māyayā gokalpanādi śāpaprāptiparyantam uktvā:
children.translated_text: Beginning thus, and after narrating through <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) the fabrication of a cow and other [events] up to the incurring of the curse:

children.text: "kā no vṛttir mahādeva śāpānnaḥ trātum arhasi* /{821}* [KūrmaP 16.112cd]
children.translated_text: "What shall be our livelihood, O <s>Mahādeva</s>? Please save us from the curse!" *{821}* [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.112cd]
Then <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s> (the Bull-bannered one, <s>Śiva</s>), looking at <s>Viṣṇu</s> standing beside him, *{822}*

children.text: !{819}! DHN[T] 619: mohaśāstratvāc chaptaviṣayatvāc ca pañcarātra uktam iti kecit vadanti. yathā.
! DHN[T] 619: vedamārgabhraṣṭhā bhavet ivaikālāmukhe pāñcarātre statt vedamārgabhraṣṭhāś ca pāpinaḥ kālamukhe pāñcarātre.
! KūrmaP: kāmavṛttyā mahāyogau pāpānnas trātum arhataḥ.
! KūrmaP: tadā pārśvasthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ samprekṣya vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ.

children.translated_text: !{819}! DHN[T] 619: Some say that <s>Pañcarātra</s> is called thus because it is a <s>mohaśāstra</s> (scripture of delusion) and because it is the subject of a curse. As follows:
The <s>Pāñcarātra</s>'s origin as directed toward those fallen from the <s>Veda</s>

children.text: kim eteṣāṃ bhavet kāryaṃ prāha puṇyaiṣiṇām iti // [Kūrma.P 16.113]
children.translated_text: 'What shall be done for these who desire merit?' — thus he spoke. [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.113]

children.text: tatas sa bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śaraṇyo bhaktavatsalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s>, the refuge [of all], who is affectionate toward devotees,

children.text: gopatiṃ prāha viprendrān ālokya praṇatān hariḥ // [KūrmaP 16.114]
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, looking at the prostrated chief <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, spoke to <s>Gopati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, lord of cattle): [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.114]

children.text: na vedabāhye śāstre ca*{823}* puṇyaleśo 'pi śaṅkara /
children.translated_text: "In a scripture outside the <s>Veda</s>, *{823}* not even a trace of merit, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: saṅgacchate yato dharmo vedād eva hi nirbabhau* //{824}* [KūrmaP 16.115]
children.translated_text: is found, since <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) has arisen from the <s>Veda</s> alone." *{824}* [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.115]
"Nevertheless, out of affection for devotees, they must be protected, O <s>Maheśvara</s>, *{825}*

children.text: āvābhyāṃ sarva evaite viprā vai nātrasaṃśayaḥ* //{826}* [KūrmaP 16.116]
children.translated_text: all these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — by us two; there is no doubt about this." *{826}* [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.116]

children.text: tasmād vai vedabāhyānāṃ rakṣaṇārthañ ca pāpinām* /{827}*
children.translated_text: "Therefore, for the protection of the sinful ones who are outside the <s>Veda</s>, *{827}*
I shall compose scriptures for their delusion, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> (Bull-bannered one)." *{828}* [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.117]
Thus urged by <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the enemy of demons, *{829}*
<s>Rudra</s> composed the scriptures of delusion, and <s>Keśava</s> too, at <s>Śiva</s>'s request: [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.118]
the <s>Kāpāla</s>, the <s>Yāmala</s>, the <s>Vāma</s>, *{830}* the <s>Bhairava</s>, the Eastern and Western [Tantras],
the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, the <s>Pāśupata</s>, *{831}* and thousands of others likewise. [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.119]

children.text: kṛtvā cārcya ca tad devān *{832}* kurvāṇās tatra coditam* /{833}*
children.translated_text: Having composed [them] and worshipping those gods, *{832}* those who perform what is enjoined therein *{833}*

children.text: patanti narake ghore bahūn kalpān punaḥ punaḥ //" ityādi coktam [KūrmaP 16.120]
children.translated_text: fall into a terrible hell for many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), again and again." And so forth it is also stated. [<s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> 16.120]
In the <s>Skānda</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>], in the <s>Śaṅkarasaṃhitā</s>:
"One should not look, at the time of worship, upon a person who is excluded, O child;
those lowest of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who were cursed by <s>Dadhīci</s> and <s>Gautama</s>, [<s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: kalāv avatariṣyanti ninditās*{834}* te bahiṣkṛtāḥ //" iti [SkandaP ]
children.translated_text: they, condemned *{834}* and excluded, will take birth in the <s>Kali</s> [age]." Thus [<s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>].
In the <s>Sāmba Purāṇa</s>: "One who has fallen from <s>Śruti</s>, who is declared by <s>Smṛti</s> *{835}* to have incurred the state of requiring <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation),
should gradually resort to <s>Tantra</s> for the purpose of attaining [the fruit of] <s>Śruti</s>. [<s>Sāmba Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: dharmaśāstre purāṇe ca proktaṃ hi maraṇāntikam /
children.translated_text: In <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>, the prescribed <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation)
for the most sinful persons is exceedingly severe, [extending] until death. [<s>Sāmba Purāṇa</s>]

children.text: ! KūrmaP: saṅgacchate mahādeva dharmo vedād vinirbabhau.
! KūrmaP: asmābhiḥ sarva evaite gantāro narakān api.
! KūrmaP: tasmād dhi vedabāhyānāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya pāpinām.
! KūrmaP: evaṃ saṃbodhito rudro mādhavena murāriṇā.
! Anmerkung in Devanāgarī-Text: tad devān - teṣu śāstreṣu paratvenoktān devān ity arthaḥ.
! KūrmaP: sṛṣtvā tān āha nirvedāḥ kurvāṇāḥ śāstracoditam.

children.translated_text: !{823}! <s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> [reads]: 'not in a person outside the <s>Veda</s>.'
The followers of the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> path are outside <s>Śrauta</s> and <s>Smārta</s> [traditions
Fear arises greatly in the weak-minded at the time of death;

children.text: teṣām evābhirakṣārthaṃ tad ahaṃ tantram uktavān // [SāmbaP]
children.translated_text: for their protection I have taught that <s>Tantra</s>. [<s>Sāmba Purāṇa</s>]
The <s>Tantra</s> [known as] <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, <s>Bhāgavata</s>, and called <s>Sāttvata</s> —
the Lord of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) spoke it, directed toward those who have fallen from the <s>Veda</s>." *{836}* Thus [<s>Sāmba Purāṇa</s>].
Elsewhere: "Then a portion [of <s>Viṣṇu</s>] named <s>Sāttvata</s>, a mighty devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
a great soul, devoted to charity, the best among those skilled in the science of archery —
he, at the command of <s>Nārada</s>, devoted to the worship of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
promulgated a scripture based on <s>kuṇḍa</s> (fire-pit), <s>gola</s> (sphere), and other [ritual implements];

children.text: tasya nāmnā tu vikhyātaṃ sāttvataṃ nāma śobhanam /
children.translated_text: famous by his name, the auspicious [scripture] called <s>Sāttvata</s>

In the <s>Laiṅga</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] — in the ninth chapter, on the <s>Yugadharma</s> (law of the ages):
"They will be branded with the insignia of divine weapons,

Other rituals that are <s>Śrauta</s> (Vedic), O best of sages,

children.text: āmnāyaṃ dharmaśāstrañ ca purāṇaṃ bhārataṃ mune /

children.text: alpamātram iti brahman*{839}* vadiṣyanti kalau yuge // [LiṅgaP]

They will not perform <s>Śrauta</s> rituals with faith, O best of sages;

children.text: svadharme rucitā nāsti brāhmaṇānāṃ kalau yuge // [LiṅgaP]

children.text: śāmbhavaṃ kecid icchanti yāmalaṃ bhuvi kecana /
